reciprocal_cbbmfanpgihdbnem.label: structural-rank put to use
reciprocal_cbbmfanpgihdbnem.meaning: An understanding of structural-rank that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_phkfcjfjecnkhbei.label: freely assembled row
reciprocal_phkfcjfjecnkhbei.meaning: row — A group of this kind whose members have had a real opportunity to leave and have chosen to remain together for this purpose.

reciprocal_pmldphgapbmdnmfm.label: A row the frost missed as a deed

reciprocal_iggekgfnjmjcejje.label: A row the frost missed turned towards someone

reciprocal_epdjmcnklennhgam.label: the second occasion for A row the frost missed

reciprocal_naolenhfakhlkmgg.label: Trace through successive hands · recording descent · by private agreement

reciprocal_egpeheichneliflh.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · recording descent · after consent
reciprocal_egpeheichneliflh.meaning: The share of a decision about the record of a descent that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to Jerah in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, Genesis 10:26.

reciprocal_olafahmifcohbljg.label: distinguish an inherited fault in division of a household · before a witness
reciprocal_olafahmifcohbljg.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to jerahmeel-hammelech in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, Jeremiah 36:26.

reciprocal_lfmpdloijkaidmmm.label: duty that survives the key in record of a descent · on first use
reciprocal_lfmpdloijkaidmmm.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Applies on a first attempt, while those involved still have no local precedent of their own. Allusion to jerahmeel-hezron in KJV Bible - Compact Letter Edition v0.10-kjv.281, 1 Chronicles 2:33.

reciprocal_iepjahioahbnmjoe.label: Identify by its company · teaching a route · with a reserve
reciprocal_iepjahioahbnmjoe.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the teaching of a route by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. reciprocal_henbhapncjhlkjeb.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · opening roads · at the second attempt
reciprocal_henbhapncjhlkjeb.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the opening of a road at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. reciprocal_kcdogijhmgfaodeo.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · teaching a route · at one's own cost
reciprocal_kcdogijhmgfaodeo.meaning: To give a judgment about the teaching of a route temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. reciprocal_hliklhnejpecakip.label: voice of the first correction in opening of a road · by inherited custom
reciprocal_hliklhnejpecakip.meaning: A small change in a repeated account which identifies the person who first corrected it. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Jerahmeelite in KJV Bible - Compact Letter Edition v0.10-kjv.281, 1 Samuel 27:10.

reciprocal_jfhnegppklppomfi.label: Identify by its company · choosing witnesses · by inherited custom

reciprocal_jgllbecldjpagoaa.label: so far as the hand remembers in naming of a child · at one's own cost
reciprocal_jgllbecldjpagoaa.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to Gerald in The Two Noble Kinsmen 00403a.

reciprocal_mglcdcliknnmgdae.label: restore the order of taking of testimony · under divided authority
reciprocal_mglcdcliknnmgdae.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Geraldo in The Two Noble Kinsmen 00722a.

reciprocal_dgeaddionjpecljd.label: up to the point of parting in taking of testimony · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_dgeaddionjpecljd.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Geraldo in The Two Noble Kinsmen 00722a.

reciprocal_dbmoaegcddbfpbgj.label: nail hand-wear
reciprocal_dbmoaegcddbfpbgj.meaning: The polish or hollow left by repeated handling of nail, valued as evidence of who used it or how.

reciprocal_gpknijokpnlkjikf.label: nail stand-in
reciprocal_gpknijokpnlkjikf.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of nail during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_kjanlmmdbcedaemc.label: nail kept in service
reciprocal_kjanlmmdbcedaemc.meaning: nail — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_mkdpaeoliboeeodd.label: To move the nail with the picture as a deed

reciprocal_gmhogkiogfedpalp.label: To move the nail with the picture turned towards someone

reciprocal_aebndekmafgfnohf.label: the second occasion for To move the nail with the picture

reciprocal_cojmbagacbkiebpj.label: The scratch beneath the gold as a deed

reciprocal_dakgpfonlilcifeh.label: trained scrabble
reciprocal_dakgpfonlilcifeh.meaning: An instance of scrabble performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_kmhcnjopgigpeeje.label: do scrabble on another's account
reciprocal_kmhcnjopgigpeeje.meaning: scrabble — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_jkjppkppjlnlkhmp.label: claw sign
reciprocal_jkjppkppjlnlkhmp.meaning: The presence of claw inferred from a fresh trace, while the creature itself remains out of sight.

reciprocal_bhegbdjngcckfojh.label: claw refuge

reciprocal_kkdhlpcpkobakkpb.label: site-faithful claw

reciprocal_fbkficnoochhcoic.label: scorpion by practice

reciprocal_eknmamdgabpgfebg.meaning: Someone who carries the obligations of scorpion for an absence with a definite end.

reciprocal_npiejbobkeajpflm.meaning: scorpion — Someone in this role to whom a community actually brings the difficult cases. Title or seniority alone does not confer the distinction.

reciprocal_omlinjeffmkagmjn.label: paddle by a chosen course

reciprocal_nbhjndaehmehgpgp.meaning: Movement of the kind described by paddle that continues after the initiating effort has stopped.

reciprocal_bikocmfabkihnpmf.label: guide a movement of paddle

reciprocal_gmgdkpkleikhmboc.label: duty that survives the key in care of a grave · by a trace

reciprocal_apbdjlllhbnmibnl.label: Detect an omission by the count · keeping a promise · on independent confirmation

reciprocal_oeilpnmmpgelpdok.label: Restore a neglected voice · distributing bread · after a disputed account

reciprocal_blnjagfmfjnajfdb.label: read the gap in making of a mould · by a trace

reciprocal_cjiogclahjckbcme.label: chosen fly

reciprocal_gnkbkmbonjbhdpib.label: do fly on another's account

reciprocal_dadiifahocbbkeoc.label: A surviving thread one can work from · recovering strays · without a common tongue

reciprocal_ioeagnfegecpoedn.label: share left without a voice in rescue of a stray animal · without a common tongue

reciprocal_dkbedmdkdckdacea.label: recover the old edge of opening of a road · against the tally

reciprocal_gihkcjddnhpcefao.label: bracket the uncertainty in telling of a voyage · after consent

reciprocal_eiehldjhhjlghdbc.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · telling a voyage · between strangers

reciprocal_ngmeceldiocpplpo.label: Identify by its company · learning a dance · after a failed trial

reciprocal_ndamnnihbdbphjkd.label: up to the point of parting in learning of a dance · as a rehearsal

reciprocal_eidjbknkpcjiehkl.meaning: The share of a decision about the opening of a road that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. reciprocal_plmhnigcfgfbnbmc.label: Stay past the handover · telling a voyage · for another's benefit

Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Juvenal in A New Voyage Round the World, Bookseller’s catalogue, 2335.1.

reciprocal_gjhpnllfnmfebhjn.label: learned well enough to reverse in telling of a voyage · for another's benefit
reciprocal_gjhpnllfnmfebhjn.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. reciprocal_mdnfalablgbimdjg.label: Stand by within reach · measuring a fever · in the wrong season

reciprocal_bogiinlmcjbabnib.label: A difficulty deliberately left to the learner · measuring a fever · after a handover

reciprocal_lmdifddgbgdmekbc.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · choosing witnesses · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_lmdifddgbgdmekbc.meaning: To give a judgment about the selection of a witness temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. reciprocal_dmkmbdpglmooanje.label: A voice recognizable in the retelling · choosing witnesses · at a distance
reciprocal_dmkmbdpglmooanje.meaning: A remembered turn of phrase that discloses whose account of the selection of a witness is being repeated even after the speaker's name has dropped out. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to julia-romans in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, Romans 16:15.

reciprocal_nedbejmjojenhpap.label: read the gap in care of a grave · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_nedbejmjojenhpap.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. reciprocal_jbmlolhncpkppgge.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · caring for graves · between generations
reciprocal_jbmlolhncpkppgge.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the care of a grave at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. reciprocal_cjginibkbkncnjca.label: recover the old edge of division of a household · pending a challenge

reciprocal_jlfkpkipficlpjmn.label: by the point of last agreement in naming of a child · after loss of the original

reciprocal_oaipfkpjjlkckdbh.label: read the gap in making of a mould · as the sole available course

reciprocal_jfjgmcnhhihbiaoi.label: as far as the old promise ran in making of a mould · in company with a novice
reciprocal_jfjgmcnhhihbiaoi.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to Julietta in Measure for Measure 00058a.

reciprocal_hfbbpaejfckpepgl.label: Identify by its company · keeping a promise · with a reserve

reciprocal_mkahmlbliegjofae.label: up to the point of parting in laying down of an office · as the sole available course
reciprocal_mkahmlbliegjofae.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Junia in Romans 16:7.

reciprocal_kaakdmiceefcodcp.label: juniper season-sign

reciprocal_ocjcopdpepbnfogc.label: juniper reserve-stock

reciprocal_hokdjoedagnjnkgj.label: volunteer juniper

reciprocal_oneibddkahkffjnj.label: restore the order of tending of a sickbed · at a distance

reciprocal_pgomeellfcgjdccd.label: as far as the old promise ran in setting of a trap · at the second attempt

reciprocal_obgfcgodpanpoigo.label: Identify by its company · returning a loan · after a failed trial

reciprocal_iijlghkbbafncoaf.label: up to the point of parting in rescue of a stray animal · under shared liability

reciprocal_iagmoogppefnlfmp.label: Distinguish by the smaller sign · making a mould · by inherited custom
reciprocal_iagmoogppefnlfmp.meaning: To distinguish two instances within the making of a mould bearing the same public sign by a smaller mark meaningful to the people who deal with it. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Justus in Acts 1:23.

reciprocal_mhkfnfacbpmgcmck.label: as far as the old promise ran in fitting of a hinge · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_mhkfnfacbpmgcmck.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Justus in Acts 1:23.

reciprocal_idnnpjmnipinpocc.label: distinguish an inherited fault in record of a descent · under divided authority
reciprocal_idnnpjmnipinpocc.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. reciprocal_hnmjplmgbnbplocd.label: exact at the fork of record of a descent · on first use

reciprocal_fhnpdnobpchkndmf.label: stay to see dividing of inherited tools take hold · at the second attempt

reciprocal_fpgfalckpiomggid.label: learned well enough to reverse in dividing of inherited tools · by a trace
reciprocal_fpgfalckpiomggid.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. reciprocal_behklijgfjemojgm.label: restore the order of dividing of inherited tools · out of public sight

reciprocal_ceghejlabcamgmnp.label: so far as the hand remembers in dividing of inherited tools · between strangers

reciprocal_khilfhokbmlnofgd.label: trained permission

reciprocal_hghhlaeackbhcdjm.label: first stir of licence

reciprocal_imednoajdokhbgef.label: wake of licence

reciprocal_gpfncmiokaielfnf.label: witnessed licence

reciprocal_nkljgmiifddjfhbi.label: Identify by its company · naming a child · with a right to withdraw

reciprocal_ijejigdbopifdgam.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · naming a child · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_ijejigdbopifdgam.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the naming of a child at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to Katherine in The Taming of the Shrew 00247a.

reciprocal_apifhpijeecklndi.label: read the gap in making of a mould · after loss of the original
reciprocal_apifhpijeecklndi.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. reciprocal_oabcifimdjmihioe.label: so far as the hand remembers in making of a mould · after a failed trial

reciprocal_henonicbfobnhhaf.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · counting sleepers · in the wrong season
reciprocal_henonicbfobnhhaf.meaning: To give a judgment about the counting of sleepers temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. reciprocal_cekohnmcmedmdcag.label: duty that survives the key in counting of sleepers · between generations
reciprocal_cekohnmcmedmdcag.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Catiline in Leviathan, Chapter 11, Hobbes_0161_315.2.

reciprocal_cidpfaommofnnoji.label: Bound a disagreement · keeping a child’s confidence · by a trace

reciprocal_kppoeklehmnchbmk.label: so far as the hand remembers in keeping of a child's confidence · with a reserve

reciprocal_pnbhbjgpalpnpoko.label: restore the order of reckoning of a debt · against the tally

reciprocal_dpffifpjocbjnpbf.label: Identify by its company · choosing witnesses · without a common tongue

reciprocal_eofoghonmmohdkia.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · choosing witnesses · after consent

reciprocal_mfgjbmabmbifmopn.label: first stir of cough

reciprocal_fcfnfkddiommehoe.label: wake of cough
reciprocal_fcfnfkddiommehoe.meaning: The changes left behind by cough after the event itself has come to an end.

reciprocal_fghcbohlkjdlegil.label: witnessed cough

reciprocal_bombcclnellfoglg.label: restore the order of laying out of a boundary · after consent

reciprocal_kefahakelcfkfdgl.label: Learned down one branch · making a mould · as the sole available course

reciprocal_kefooahflbjlccmo.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · carrying a burden · under divided authority

reciprocal_ogdbiljdeopncaej.label: Trace through successive hands · naming a child · after loss of the original

reciprocal_bghleokggemchjoa.label: exact at the fork of naming of a child · after a handover

reciprocal_mkmolbeelcobnmka.label: stay to see drawing of a chart take hold · in the wrong season
reciprocal_mkmolbeelcobnmka.meaning: To accompany a person far enough beyond a handover to see whether they can actually continue alone. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Clauda in Acts 27:16.

reciprocal_aloikgbinmciicep.label: By retracing the last sure mark · drawing charts · by private agreement
reciprocal_aloikgbinmciicep.meaning: In a manner that retraces the drawing of a chart from the last point one can still positively identify. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Clauda in Acts 27:16.

reciprocal_dgkbgomahelajdgm.label: unmix two accounts of care of a shared lamp · against the tally
reciprocal_dgkbgomahelajdgm.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to Clowder in The Taming of the Shrew 00011a.

reciprocal_lpbdfaahnmajefii.label: up to the point of parting in carrying of a burden · against the tally
reciprocal_lpbdfaahnmajefii.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to Clowder in The Taming of the Shrew 00011a.

reciprocal_knjnhejkfadoideb.label: unmix two accounts of selection of a witness · against the tally
reciprocal_knjnhejkfadoideb.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to Claudia in 2 Timothy 4:21.

reciprocal_emejmdfjlimdjcbp.label: up to the point of parting in selection of a witness · by a trace
reciprocal_emejmdfjlimdjcbp.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to Claudia in 2 Timothy 4:21.

reciprocal_milfohdfgdcndgof.label: stay to see laying down of an office take hold · as the sole available course
reciprocal_milfohdfgdcndgof.meaning: To accompany a person far enough beyond a handover to see whether they can actually continue alone. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Claudio in Hamlet 00928a.

reciprocal_efdhminabnogcioh.label: Time made free by a prior gift · collecting tolls · against the tally
reciprocal_efdhminabnogcioh.meaning: Said of a period of freedom in which an earlier provision of the collection of a toll allows someone else to choose a course without immediate dependence. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to Claudio in Hamlet 00928a.

reciprocal_omhbpicjegocjdkn.label: Restore a neglected voice · keeping a child’s confidence · between generations
reciprocal_omhbpicjegocjdkn.meaning: To bring a disregarded account of the keeping of a child's confidence into hearing without taking credit for originating it. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Claudius in Julius Caesar 00693a.

reciprocal_dninehfbiifecflg.label: A voice recognizable in the retelling · keeping a child’s confidence · after consent
reciprocal_dninehfbiifecflg.meaning: A remembered turn of phrase that discloses whose account of the keeping of a child's confidence is being repeated even after the speaker's name has dropped out. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to Claudius in Julius Caesar 00693a.

reciprocal_hbdhkigjjemcgfdk.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · sealing a letter · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_hbdhkigjjemcgfdk.meaning: To give a judgment about the sealing of a letter temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to Claudius-Lysias in Acts 23:26.

reciprocal_ciapjalepnokpllp.label: learned well enough to reverse in sealing of a letter · out of public sight
reciprocal_ciapjalepnokpllp.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to Claudius-Lysias in Acts 23:26.

reciprocal_jjjboogahacbkmgg.label: clear approach
reciprocal_jjjboogahacbkmgg.meaning: The approach from which a traveller first recognizes clear before reaching the place itself.

reciprocal_ledghojledjjgdnh.label: clear meeting-ground
reciprocal_ledghojledjjgdnh.meaning: The part of clear people use to meet or change hands, identified by what happens there.

reciprocal_ecdjlhjepbpijlbk.label: clear known as shelter
reciprocal_ecdjlhjepbpijlbk.meaning: clear — A place of this kind that someone knows how to reach for safety from experience, even if it has never been formally set aside as a refuge.

reciprocal_glbjcpkkebhmlhfp.label: clearly by local measure
reciprocal_glbjcpkkebhmlhfp.meaning: The quality called clearly as judged against the things actually available for comparison here.

reciprocal_kgdicfkpddidhoni.label: clearly under strain
reciprocal_kgdicfkpddidhoni.meaning: The degree of clearly that remains when the quality is put under an adverse condition.

reciprocal_dlhbfhmckimemodm.label: clearly to the practical threshold
reciprocal_dlhbfhmckimemodm.meaning: clearly — Having the quality in question to the degree required for the immediate work. Further degrees may be perceptible yet irrelevant to the present choice.

reciprocal_ffifammdmcegkkfb.label: Stay past the handover · learning a dance · out of public sight
reciprocal_ffifammdmcegkkfb.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the learning of a dance after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to Cleve in A New Voyage Round the World, Bookseller’s catalogue, 2503.1.

reciprocal_ddmcpkgakaalgfaj.label: Learned well enough to retrace · learning a dance · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_ddmcpkgakaalgfaj.meaning: Said of a route, habit, or piece of knowledge of the learning of a dance which can be retraced independently after learning it in someone else's company. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to Cleve in A New Voyage Round the World, Bookseller’s catalogue, 2503.1.

reciprocal_enopfkeieiogidnh.label: Distinguish by the smaller sign · choosing witnesses · under divided authority
reciprocal_enopfkeieiogidnh.meaning: To distinguish two instances within the selection of a witness bearing the same public sign by a smaller mark meaningful to the people who deal with it. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Clement in Philippians 4:3.

reciprocal_bhandfpijeibobai.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · choosing witnesses · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_bhandfpijeibobai.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the selection of a witness at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Clement in Philippians 4:3.

reciprocal_enedfbedcdfkohfj.label: unmix two accounts of dividing of inherited tools · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_enedfbedcdfkohfj.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Clement in Henry IV, Part 2 00473a.

reciprocal_hncjojmechocadfa.label: as far as the old promise ran in dividing of inherited tools · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_hncjojmechocadfa.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to Clement in Henry IV, Part 2 00473a.

reciprocal_ikgfcebbeledceal.label: galaxy acting together
reciprocal_ikgfcebbeledceal.meaning: galaxy understood as acting with an agreed voice. Mere co-presence gives no one authority to speak for the group.

reciprocal_dmjjgnjhpbcofcbf.label: edge of galaxy
reciprocal_dmjjgnjhpbcofcbf.meaning: Those whose connection with galaxy matters in practice although their membership is disputed or left unrecorded.

reciprocal_fojjbmmkkdjapchm.label: freely assembled galaxy
reciprocal_fojjbmmkkdjapchm.meaning: galaxy — A group of this kind whose members have had a real opportunity to leave and have chosen to remain together for this purpose.

reciprocal_mebcglkfhdgaalcm.label: unmix two accounts of learning of a dance · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_mebcglkfhdgaalcm.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to Cleitus in Henry V 00608a.

reciprocal_pfaiejcknekofogb.label: so far as the hand remembers in reckoning of a debt · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_pfaiejcknekofogb.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Cleitus in Henry V 00608a.

reciprocal_hmdemjpecpkcpelb.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · learning a dance · in company with a novice
reciprocal_hmdemjpecpkcpelb.meaning: To give a judgment about the learning of a dance temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to Cleopatra in Antony and Cleopatra 00190a.

reciprocal_bpmljpkaaajmkgmc.label: duty that survives the key in learning of a dance · out of public sight
reciprocal_bpmljpkaaajmkgmc.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to Cleopatra in Antony and Cleopatra 00190a.

reciprocal_kkedoodigcpmdghp.label: Stay past the handover · teaching a route · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_kkedoodigcpmdghp.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the teaching of a route after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to Cleopas in Luke 24:18.

reciprocal_jpkecjfipbnfcmap.label: A difficulty deliberately left to the learner · teaching a route · in the wrong season
reciprocal_jpkecjfipbnfcmap.meaning: The margin of difficulty in the teaching of a route a helper leaves untouched so the learner can discover their own reach. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Cleopas in Luke 24:18.

reciprocal_koffdkmdapcnmhbi.label: Stand by within reach · naming a child · out of public sight
reciprocal_koffdkmdapcnmhbi.meaning: To remain close enough to help with the naming of a child while leaving the person concerned free to finish the act. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to Cleophas in John 19:25.

reciprocal_becckahknkmpachi.label: A difficulty deliberately left to the learner · naming a child · on first use
reciprocal_becckahknkmpachi.meaning: The margin of difficulty in the naming of a child a helper leaves untouched so the learner can discover their own reach. Applies on a first attempt, while those involved still have no local precedent of their own. Allusion to Cleophas in John 19:25.

reciprocal_gmiippkfadampkfc.label: restore the order of division of a catch · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_gmiippkfadampkfc.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to Cleombrotus in Paradise Lost, Book III, 469–475.

reciprocal_canffaglenhfbifp.label: as far as the old promise ran in taking of soundings · between generations
reciprocal_canffaglenhfbifp.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Cleombrotus in Paradise Lost, Book III, 469–475.

reciprocal_ahhbggglibpenccc.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · storing water · after a handover
reciprocal_ahhbggglibpenccc.meaning: To give a judgment about the storage of water temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to Cleomenes in The Winter's Tale 00668a.

reciprocal_dpbkfmlhkpcliijp.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · storing water · after loss of the original
reciprocal_dpbkfmlhkpcliijp.meaning: The share of a decision about the storage of water that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to Cleomenes in The Winter's Tale 00668a.

reciprocal_kfnkemfjbjpfkbaa.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · calling a council · at one's own cost
reciprocal_kfnkemfjbjpfkbaa.meaning: To give a judgment about the calling of a council temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. reciprocal_ndlbbogbgolliceh.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · calling a council · at a distance
reciprocal_ndlbbogbgolliceh.meaning: The share of a decision about the calling of a council that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to Cleon in Pericles, Prince of Tyre 00483a.

reciprocal_fgmjampeipaffceh.label: Detect an omission by the count · choosing witnesses · under shared liability
reciprocal_fgmjampeipaffceh.meaning: To detect a gap in the selection of a witness because the count or pattern expects another occurrence before it can close. reciprocal_lfndmhekglfbghjp.label: Counted without a hearing · choosing witnesses · under divided authority
reciprocal_lfndmhekglfbghjp.meaning: A member or instance of the selection of a witness counted in a total but never called individually. It has numerical presence without an individual hearing. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Clement in Leviathan, Chapter 33, Hobbes_0161_888.5.

reciprocal_njdmbiflgclabgdo.label: Identify by its company · telling a voyage · between strangers
reciprocal_njdmbiflgclabgdo.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the telling of a voyage by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to Clitus in Julius Caesar 00830a.

reciprocal_hpgombdpdjlofmfl.label: as far as the old promise ran in telling of a voyage · pending a challenge
reciprocal_hpgombdpdjlofmfl.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Names a provisional arrangement that stands until someone brings a specific objection. Allusion to Clitus in Julius Caesar 00830a.

reciprocal_bapjjfnbopnphlmj.label: Restore a neglected voice · choosing witnesses · after a handover
reciprocal_bapjjfnbopnphlmj.meaning: To bring a disregarded account of the selection of a witness into hearing without taking credit for originating it. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to Cleveland in A New Voyage Round the World, Bookseller’s catalogue, 2351.1.

reciprocal_ipbofgbkfojmikae.label: Learned well enough to retrace · choosing witnesses · in company with a novice
reciprocal_ipbofgbkfojmikae.meaning: Said of a route, habit, or piece of knowledge of the selection of a witness which can be retraced independently after learning it in someone else's company. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to Cleveland in A New Voyage Round the World, Bookseller’s catalogue, 2351.1.

reciprocal_ddjachgikhnhhapp.label: trace the hand behind tending of a sickbed · after a failed trial
reciprocal_ddjachgikhnhhapp.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to Clifton in Henry IV, Part I 00825a.

reciprocal_fefhpgjoffbfbkpa.label: exact at the fork of tending of a sickbed · on first use
reciprocal_fefhpgjoffbfbkpa.meaning: Said of knowledge that can distinguish two lines at the moment they parted, even if their subsequent history is obscure. Applies on a first attempt, while those involved still have no local precedent of their own. Allusion to Clifton in Henry IV, Part I 00825a.

reciprocal_kopcgldbfkjjkeeb.label: Trace through successive hands · dividing a household · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_kopcgldbfkjjkeeb.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the division of a household by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. reciprocal_jbkocdfdfeocpjai.label: so far as the hand remembers in record of a descent · after a failed trial
reciprocal_jbkocdfdfeocpjai.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. reciprocal_khgifknmmopclfpn.label: chosen draw
reciprocal_khgifknmmopclfpn.meaning: An instance of draw that someone deliberately undertakes and can answer for. The outward act may look the same when it happens by accident.

reciprocal_bnlhjedbbdonaelj.label: settled extract
reciprocal_bnlhjedbbdonaelj.meaning: A change of the kind described by extract that holds after the conditions that produced it have gone.

reciprocal_jlipnomggbnhbebn.label: do draw on another's account
reciprocal_jlipnomggbnhbebn.meaning: draw — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_omggmkejlpkkjpep.label: first stir of attraction
reciprocal_omggmkejlpkkjpep.meaning: The earliest observable part of attraction, identifiable before its full course can be known.

reciprocal_dkmpjdcijnfbmiaf.label: wake of attraction
reciprocal_dkmpjdcijnfbmiaf.meaning: The changes left behind by attraction after the event itself has come to an end.

reciprocal_jfmfogjngpmkndgc.label: witnessed attraction
reciprocal_jfmfogjngpmkndgc.meaning: attraction — An occurrence of this kind someone can date or place from their own presence. The word marks what that witness can vouch for.

reciprocal_coeehmonppfliddp.label: table acting together
reciprocal_coeehmonppfliddp.meaning: table understood as acting with an agreed voice. Mere co-presence gives no one authority to speak for the group.

reciprocal_mdpaphlcblemodeo.label: edge of table
reciprocal_mdpaphlcblemodeo.meaning: Those whose connection with table matters in practice although their membership is disputed or left unrecorded.

reciprocal_jecoikefbnlmhbhe.label: freely assembled table
reciprocal_jecoikefbnlmhbhe.meaning: table — A group of this kind whose members have had a real opportunity to leave and have chosen to remain together for this purpose.

reciprocal_cocpgiimcchjampi.label: meal courtesy-portion

reciprocal_pfmbhpgjpenaclho.label: table-meal lingering taste
reciprocal_pfmbhpgjpenaclho.meaning: The taste by which table-meal can still be recognized after it has been swallowed or taken away.

reciprocal_gimknomoopemleip.label: household-owed meal

reciprocal_nkihblnhalggefeg.label: The meal you wear on your sleeve turned towards someone

reciprocal_ocfmiomboaacgmod.label: the second occasion for The meal you wear on your sleeve

reciprocal_gebehibgcfafpknf.meaning: The taste by which meal-blessing can still be recognized after it has been swallowed or taken away.

reciprocal_nloenpolonpednmg.label: table steward by practice

reciprocal_jhbpfpghkkodbmkj.label: acting table steward
reciprocal_jhbpfpghkkodbmkj.meaning: Someone who carries the obligations of table steward for an absence with a definite end.

reciprocal_cikegfeecfaglcpf.label: trusted working table steward
reciprocal_cikegfeecfaglcpf.meaning: table steward — Someone in this role to whom a community actually brings the difficult cases. Title or seniority alone does not confer the distinction.

reciprocal_ccajfogecnkcnbbc.label: chosen dine

reciprocal_hahlamdijflmdcod.label: trained dine
reciprocal_hahlamdijflmdcod.meaning: An instance of dine performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_egaklcnpbdjdckgi.label: do dine on another's account
reciprocal_egaklcnpbdjdckgi.meaning: dine — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_ppollhahompdggom.label: table-column hand-wear
reciprocal_ppollhahompdggom.meaning: The polish or hollow left by repeated handling of table-column, valued as evidence of who used it or how.

reciprocal_mlolnhgjpephgcha.label: table-column stand-in
reciprocal_mlolnhgjpephgcha.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of table-column during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_ikedpkjghclppdpj.label: table-column kept in service
reciprocal_ikedpkjghclppdpj.meaning: table-column — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_depkckiiilckhllp.label: attractive by local measure
reciprocal_depkckiiilckhllp.meaning: The quality called attractive as judged against the things actually available for comparison here.

reciprocal_akeeghgihcbakfjc.label: unmix two accounts of opening of a road · on independent confirmation

reciprocal_mpbdfhnpcnihalig.label: so far as the hand remembers in opening of a road · in the owner's absence

reciprocal_phllollejbaflcge.label: restore the order of settling of a quarrel · by a trace

reciprocal_blhaigaahdlkdaii.label: rel in another's terms

reciprocal_emgchdkabjpkjdgm.label: bracket the uncertainty in drawing of a chart · after a handover

reciprocal_fbloabhmcinlmkco.label: by the point of last agreement in drawing of a chart · at the point of commitment

reciprocal_aoeamgncfdgcfjfc.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · naming a child · between strangers

reciprocal_daopcfojehooibnf.meaning: Said of an assurance about the keeping of a promise whose hearer can identify who will actually bear a loss. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Keech in Henry IV, Part 2 00174b.

reciprocal_hmefoglfpoenmmba.label: Identify by its company · sealing a letter · under divided authority
reciprocal_hmefoglfpoenmmba.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the sealing of a letter by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to civitas in Two Treatises of Government, Second Treatise, Chapter X, 872.1.

reciprocal_dochgaahfcifcpkj.label: so far as the hand remembers in return of a borrowed thing · out of public sight
reciprocal_dochgaahfcifcpkj.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to civitas in Two Treatises of Government, Second Treatise, Chapter X, 872.1.

reciprocal_hjppbnhjeghfoihj.label: stance by local measure
reciprocal_hjppbnhjeghfoihj.meaning: The quality called stance as judged against the things actually available for comparison here.

reciprocal_dafkomdejniimakh.label: stand under strain

reciprocal_cjejnpgcffladikd.label: stance to the practical threshold
reciprocal_cjejnpgcffladikd.meaning: stance — Having the quality in question to the degree required for the immediate work. Further degrees may be perceptible yet irrelevant to the present choice.

reciprocal_ofgfclfhpfigdgem.label: pillar in silhouette
reciprocal_ofgfclfhpfigdgem.meaning: A likeness to pillar that depends on an outline and may disappear as soon as the object turns.

reciprocal_pmpehcgcjicknfch.label: pillar working fit
reciprocal_pmpehcgcjicknfch.meaning: A likeness to pillar close enough for two pieces to fit or do the same work even when their outlines differ.

reciprocal_cmjiijkljnhndipo.label: pillar through a turn

reciprocal_hfpbakfknnbgchfi.label: chapiter hand-wear

reciprocal_bipcoahgedilbeco.label: chapiter stand-in

reciprocal_cdjbkkghgcakgjii.label: chapiter kept in service
reciprocal_cdjbkkghgcakgjii.meaning: chapiter — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_bgoppkkfbpemilca.label: architrave hand-wear
reciprocal_bgoppkkfbpemilca.meaning: The polish or hollow left by repeated handling of architrave, valued as evidence of who used it or how.

reciprocal_menpdeeggpnciabh.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of architrave during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_fcjmigcjcdbddcek.label: scaffold-platform hand-wear

reciprocal_hnoccaaofoebejnm.meaning: scaffold-platform — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_hecpfadaljbogidn.label: constant by local measure
reciprocal_hecpfadaljbogidn.meaning: The quality called constant as judged against the things actually available for comparison here.

reciprocal_ikdpmjcpicalkpaf.label: proof under strain
reciprocal_ikdpmjcpicalkpaf.meaning: The degree of proof that remains when the quality is put under an adverse condition.

reciprocal_phegjocccijgjppk.label: constant to the practical threshold
reciprocal_phegjocccijgjppk.meaning: constant — Having the quality in question to the degree required for the immediate work. Further degrees may be perceptible yet irrelevant to the present choice.

reciprocal_dhhbbmgijcelilda.label: post approach
reciprocal_dhhbbmgijcelilda.meaning: The approach from which a traveller first recognizes post before reaching the place itself.

reciprocal_llbjnkppnihlmdgj.label: post meeting-ground
reciprocal_llbjnkppnihlmdgj.meaning: The part of post people use to meet or change hands, identified by what happens there.

reciprocal_mhnngjhebhnehdef.label: post known as shelter
reciprocal_mhnngjhebhnehdef.meaning: post — A place of this kind that someone knows how to reach for safety from experience, even if it has never been formally set aside as a refuge.

reciprocal_nddaikhhkjngledj.label: stand-to-it intimation
reciprocal_nddaikhhkjngledj.meaning: A first grasp of stand-to-it sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_fmkcdkpakfaoipao.label: stand-to-it put to use
reciprocal_fmkcdkpakfaoipao.meaning: An understanding of stand-to-it that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_cbjenafnlbogjbdp.label: stand-to-it held on trial
reciprocal_cbjenafnlbogjbdp.meaning: stand-to-it — A thought or belief of this kind deliberately entertained until a particular question can decide whether to keep it. The speaker owns the test as well as the idea.

reciprocal_gdngbloadjbjlagn.label: deputy by practice
reciprocal_gdngbloadjbjlagn.meaning: Someone recognized as deputy by the work they repeatedly perform before anyone grants a title.

reciprocal_kkgjelpcjmndahjn.label: acting deputy
reciprocal_kkgjelpcjmndahjn.meaning: Someone who carries the obligations of deputy for an absence with a definite end.

reciprocal_jojkopaccgdndigk.label: trusted working deputy
reciprocal_jojkopaccgdndigk.meaning: deputy — Someone in this role to whom a community actually brings the difficult cases. Title or seniority alone does not confer the distinction.

reciprocal_lmpmhcpikfddjaoh.label: station approach
reciprocal_lmpmhcpikfddjaoh.meaning: The approach from which a traveller first recognizes station before reaching the place itself.

reciprocal_iobnabnjadehphme.label: station meeting-ground
reciprocal_iobnabnjadehphme.meaning: The part of station people use to meet or change hands, identified by what happens there.

reciprocal_hhmedhiocnlbmkma.label: station known as shelter
reciprocal_hhmedhiocnlbmkma.meaning: station — A place of this kind that someone knows how to reach for safety from experience, even if it has never been formally set aside as a refuge.

reciprocal_kfajhdekolplfdga.label: read the gap in making of a mould · for another's benefit
reciprocal_kfajhdekolplfdga.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Coke in Leviathan, Chapter 26, Hobbes_0161_651-margin-1.1.

reciprocal_dldldcnchddeldkl.label: so far as the hand remembers in making of a mould · between generations
reciprocal_dldldcnchddeldkl.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Coke in Leviathan, Chapter 26, Hobbes_0161_651-margin-1.1.

reciprocal_khbjbngpdfehkjob.label: cockatrice by practice
reciprocal_khbjbngpdfehkjob.meaning: Someone recognized as cockatrice by the work they repeatedly perform before anyone grants a title.

reciprocal_ebfbiafkheafbbol.label: acting cockatrice
reciprocal_ebfbiafkheafbbol.meaning: Someone who carries the obligations of cockatrice for an absence with a definite end.

reciprocal_iedimkpnicblfdjg.label: trusted working cockatrice
reciprocal_iedimkpnicblfdjg.meaning: cockatrice — Someone in this role to whom a community actually brings the difficult cases. Title or seniority alone does not confer the distinction.

reciprocal_iopljnphkpbeaegk.label: cock sign
reciprocal_iopljnphkpbeaegk.meaning: The presence of cock inferred from a fresh trace, while the creature itself remains out of sight.

reciprocal_klbjoiooghjopojh.label: cock refuge
reciprocal_klbjoiooghjopojh.meaning: A place the observer leaves undisturbed because cock repeatedly returns to it for cover. One sighting alone gives no such claim.

reciprocal_jdmeflkjagafbdbm.label: site-faithful cock
reciprocal_jdmeflkjagafbdbm.meaning: cock — An individual of this kind whose repeated returns to one place are reliable enough for someone to recognize or await it there. The word describes one animal's habits and carries no claim that it is tame.

reciprocal_nopmioldicodfbfk.label: chosen cock-crow
reciprocal_nopmioldicodfbfk.meaning: An instance of cock-crow that someone deliberately undertakes and can answer for. The outward act may look the same when it happens by accident.

reciprocal_jckdddbagijfebcp.label: trained cock-crow
reciprocal_jckdddbagijfebcp.meaning: An instance of cock-crow performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_jefnecbdeoaccbpj.label: do cock-crow on another's account
reciprocal_jefnecbdeoaccbpj.meaning: cock-crow — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_cllcceobnngandpp.label: cockle courtesy-portion
reciprocal_cllcceobnngandpp.meaning: A share of cockle held back for someone who has yet to arrive, even when everyone at table could eat more.

reciprocal_micnbdlalihahkfd.label: cockle lingering taste
reciprocal_micnbdlalihahkfd.meaning: The taste by which cockle can still be recognized after it has been swallowed or taken away.

reciprocal_gpcknddaogpcjlel.label: household-owed cockle
reciprocal_gpcknddaogpcjlel.meaning: cockle — Food of this kind already owed to someone at the table before it is served. Offering it to a guest would spend another person's welcome.

reciprocal_bidgmddknibeiama.label: Stay past the handover · changing the night watch · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_bidgmddknibeiama.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the relief of a night watch after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to Coxon in A New Voyage Round the World, Introduction, 103.2.

reciprocal_dhebmfkmeafmamhk.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · changing the night watch · at one's own cost
reciprocal_dhebmfkmeafmamhk.meaning: The share of a decision about the relief of a night watch that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to Coxon in A New Voyage Round the World, Introduction, 103.2.

reciprocal_lpfijpbfonmpmkkh.label: bracket the uncertainty in care of a grave · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_lpfijpbfonmpmkkh.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to Cocytus in Paradise Lost, Book II, 577–581.

reciprocal_hgjcjobhilonnieg.label: By retracing the last sure mark · caring for graves · out of public sight
reciprocal_hgjcjobhilonnieg.meaning: In a manner that retraces the care of a grave from the last point one can still positively identify. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to Cocytus in Paradise Lost, Book II, 577–581.

reciprocal_camcdabjpcmligpl.label: bracket the uncertainty in telling of a voyage · at the second attempt
reciprocal_camcdabjpcmligpl.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Coquimbo in A New Voyage Round the World, Introduction, 107.4.

reciprocal_ddeoecdkjeoghfdf.label: by the point of last agreement in telling of a voyage · at one's own cost
reciprocal_ddeoecdkjeoghfdf.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to Coquimbo in A New Voyage Round the World, Introduction, 107.4.

reciprocal_hkpibpgpadileagk.label: bracket the uncertainty in teaching of a route · pending a challenge
reciprocal_hkpibpgpadileagk.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Names a provisional arrangement that stands until someone brings a specific objection. Allusion to Cocos in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter V, 475.4.

reciprocal_elcmpohcmaaffcpj.label: by the point of last agreement in teaching of a route · after a failed trial
reciprocal_elcmpohcmaaffcpj.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to Cocos in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter V, 475.4.

reciprocal_ahlpjopghhgglaia.label: Restore a neglected voice · naming a child · for another's benefit
reciprocal_ahlpjopghhgglaia.meaning: To bring a disregarded account of the naming of a child into hearing without taking credit for originating it. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to koa in Ezekiel 23:23.

reciprocal_opcpaaapbnbffpmn.label: A voice recognizable in the retelling · choosing witnesses · at the second attempt
reciprocal_opcpaaapbnbffpmn.meaning: A remembered turn of phrase that discloses whose account of the selection of a witness is being repeated even after the speaker's name has dropped out. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to koa in Ezekiel 23:23.

reciprocal_loippbkfihcheanf.label: Trace through successive hands · dividing a household · at one's own cost
reciprocal_loippbkfihcheanf.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the division of a household by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to Kohath in Numbers 3:30.

reciprocal_achnahjjiibhemhk.label: taught within one line of naming of a child · against the tally
reciprocal_achnahjjiibhemhk.meaning: Said of a skill transmitted within one line of teachers. Outsiders may perform the same work by a recognizably different sequence. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to Kohath in Numbers 3:30.

reciprocal_cpddefemebhcbabd.label: bracket the uncertainty in telling of a voyage · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_cpddefemebhcbabd.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Kohathite in 1 Chronicles 9:32.

reciprocal_jddlhkfgclldpmhe.label: Counted without a hearing · telling a voyage · by private agreement
reciprocal_jddlhkfgclldpmhe.meaning: A member or instance of the telling of a voyage counted in a total but never called individually. It has numerical presence without an individual hearing. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Kohathite in 1 Chronicles 9:32.

reciprocal_eeckjjpfflepjaea.label: Locate between known limits · telling a voyage · by inherited custom
reciprocal_eeckjjpfflepjaea.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the telling of a voyage by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Kohathite in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, 1 Chronicles 9:32.

reciprocal_dkneeknccklfgfah.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · telling a voyage · for another's benefit
reciprocal_dkneeknccklfgfah.meaning: The share of a decision about the telling of a voyage that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Kohathite in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, 1 Chronicles 9:32.

reciprocal_agmbcakigocppala.label: asleep by local measure
reciprocal_agmbcakigocppala.meaning: The quality called asleep as judged against the things actually available for comparison here.

reciprocal_albiificgndomddf.label: cor put to use
reciprocal_albiificgndomddf.meaning: An understanding of cor that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_jjccbibicinkmkap.label: asleep to the practical threshold
reciprocal_jjccbibicinkmkap.meaning: asleep — Having the quality in question to the degree required for the immediate work. Further degrees may be perceptible yet irrelevant to the present choice.

reciprocal_plagbaejliiieacp.label: share left without a voice in drying of a harvest · for another's benefit
reciprocal_plagbaejliiieacp.meaning: A part included in the total for which nobody present has authority to speak. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Korah in 1 Chronicles 1:35.

reciprocal_dnhhcpikbdfpaonc.label: Trace through successive hands · tending the hearth · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_dnhhcpikbdfpaonc.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the keeping of a hearth by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to korahite in 1 Chronicles 9:31.

reciprocal_fifpcmdacdnpaapl.label: taught within one line of keeping of a hearth · at one's own cost
reciprocal_fifpcmdacdnpaapl.meaning: Said of a skill transmitted within one line of teachers. Outsiders may perform the same work by a recognizably different sequence. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to korahite in 1 Chronicles 9:31.

reciprocal_flekibblnlkhfphh.label: Korhite intimation
reciprocal_flekibblnlkhfphh.meaning: A first grasp of Korhite sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_menkipglpkgmgnmo.label: Korhite put to use
reciprocal_menkipglpkgmgnmo.meaning: An understanding of Korhite that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_kiedaegabcicnhgp.label: Korhite held on trial
reciprocal_kiedaegabcicnhgp.meaning: Korhite — A thought or belief of this kind deliberately entertained until a particular question can decide whether to keep it. The speaker owns the test as well as the idea.

reciprocal_ceeonffoeogpjcka.label: trace the hand behind keeping of a hearth · by inherited custom
reciprocal_ceeonffoeogpjcka.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. reciprocal_nbmhmfdjnnonjnei.label: duty that survives the key in keeping of a hearth · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_nbmhmfdjnnonjnei.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to korahite in KJV Bible - Compact Letter Edition v0.10-kjv.281, 1 Chronicles 9:31.

reciprocal_nbogdkbopfehgcde.label: distinguish an inherited fault in record of a descent · against the tally
reciprocal_nbogdkbopfehgcde.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to Korathites in Numbers 26:58.

reciprocal_cjnbbckcplpgnlni.label: exact at the fork of division of a household · with a reserve
reciprocal_cjnbbckcplpgnlni.meaning: Said of knowledge that can distinguish two lines at the moment they parted, even if their subsequent history is obscure. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Korathites in Numbers 26:58.

reciprocal_ohmnhjjkapbnmafj.label: Trace through successive hands · dividing a household · on first use
reciprocal_ohmnhjjkapbnmafj.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the division of a household by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. Applies on a first attempt, while those involved still have no local precedent of their own. Allusion to Korathites in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, Numbers 26:58.

reciprocal_llkfaenibfdlpgmf.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · recording descent · for another's benefit
reciprocal_llkfaenibfdlpgmf.meaning: The share of a decision about the record of a descent that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Korathites in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, Numbers 26:58.

reciprocal_oflajcmfalfppcda.label: Locate between known limits · rehearsing a song · before a witness
reciprocal_oflajcmfalfppcda.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the rehearsal of a song by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to chorazin in Luke 10:13.

reciprocal_flfgbgidbnmgagdh.label: by the point of last agreement in collection of a toll · pending a challenge
reciprocal_flfgbgidbnmgagdh.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Names a provisional arrangement that stands until someone brings a specific objection. Allusion to chorazin in Luke 10:13.

reciprocal_obpngegkpjdomgjf.label: unmix two accounts of settling of a quarrel · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_obpngegkpjdomgjf.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to corambus in All's Well That Ends Well, passage 0887.

reciprocal_iahfbkjgilfmcegi.label: up to the point of parting in setting of a trap · against the tally
reciprocal_iahfbkjgilfmcegi.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to corambus in All's Well That Ends Well, passage 0887.

reciprocal_okgodjddfakgjphf.label: Locate between known limits · drawing charts · at a distance

reciprocal_jiiohkbmiopicmjf.label: by the point of last agreement in drawing of a chart · between generations

reciprocal_cnpnpeefgfkgcioi.label: Corban intimation
reciprocal_cnpnpeefgfkgcioi.meaning: A first grasp of Corban sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_fkhbgphlbdonhhhl.label: Corban put to use
reciprocal_fkhbgphlbdonhhhl.meaning: An understanding of Corban that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_bielcglalkhnognl.label: Corban held on trial
reciprocal_bielcglalkhnognl.meaning: Corban — A thought or belief of this kind deliberately entertained until a particular question can decide whether to keep it. The speaker owns the test as well as the idea.

reciprocal_pkimjjnaakckckba.label: cord threshold
reciprocal_pkimjjnaakckckba.meaning: cord taken as the least quantity that makes a difference to a decision.

reciprocal_mcecaelbgpjbhfmi.label: short of cord
reciprocal_mcecaelbgpjbhfmi.meaning: The amount still wanting when something is being made up to cord. Its size depends on what has already been counted.

reciprocal_ajciigbnjmfckknb.label: usable cord
reciprocal_ajciigbnjmfckknb.meaning: cord — An amount reckoned in this unit after what cannot actually be delivered has been taken out. The nominal amount may be greater.

reciprocal_fpcfcljahncdnejn.label: plummet hand-wear
reciprocal_fpcfcljahncdnejn.meaning: The polish or hollow left by repeated handling of plummet, valued as evidence of who used it or how.

reciprocal_nelkfminanhpnpfd.label: plummet stand-in
reciprocal_nelkfminanhpnpfd.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of plummet during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_mlinialmmheokaad.label: plummet kept in service
reciprocal_mlinialmmheokaad.meaning: plummet — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_ehnjepfimeklpkkd.meaning: The polish or hollow left by repeated handling of plumbline, valued as evidence of who used it or how.

reciprocal_fiiapggicbhjjkee.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of plumbline during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_imkbbjgbokehmbel.meaning: plumbline — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_bhekcgjildgfcfbp.label: whip hand-wear
reciprocal_bhekcgjildgfcfbp.meaning: The polish or hollow left by repeated handling of whip, valued as evidence of who used it or how.

reciprocal_fjgeglnjgkbagkgo.label: whip stand-in
reciprocal_fjgeglnjgkbagkgo.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of whip during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_ffnnmooaglnpnhan.label: whip kept in service
reciprocal_ffnnmooaglnpnhan.meaning: whip — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_olhneebfcfambdbc.label: Refuse to bid up one's love
reciprocal_olhneebfcfambdbc.meaning: To decline an invitation to compete in professions of affection because increasing the profession would falsify the feeling.

reciprocal_ceemadoekekidhen.label: Love misheard as silence
reciprocal_ceemadoekekidhen.meaning: Affection whose refusal to perform has been mistaken by its recipient for an absence of feeling.

reciprocal_dchamgfmpgiiapee.label: restore the order of telling of a voyage · after a disputed account
reciprocal_dchamgfmpgiiapee.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible.
