reciprocal_egfocjcjliknkpih.meaning: To accompany a person far enough beyond a handover to see whether they can actually continue alone. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Condore in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XIV, 1555.1.

reciprocal_lgbldabehhflhdfo.label: learned well enough to reverse in teaching of a route · as the sole available course
reciprocal_lgbldabehhflhdfo.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Condore in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XIV, 1555.1.

reciprocal_lkmpjigjphbhenlm.label: apparent congeal
reciprocal_lkmpjigjphbhenlm.meaning: A change described as congeal from its outward signs that reverses when its immediate cause is removed.

reciprocal_llpdgoiaimadndjd.label: settled congeal
reciprocal_llpdgoiaimadndjd.meaning: A change of the kind described by congeal that holds after the conditions that produced it have gone.

reciprocal_lfjejejklapbjgjl.label: undergo congeal past the turning point
reciprocal_lfjejejklapbjgjl.meaning: congeal — To undergo the change in question far enough that removing its first cause no longer restores the earlier state.

reciprocal_nmfbmadipognidbk.label: Identify by its company · returning a loan · before a witness
reciprocal_nmfbmadipognidbk.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the return of a borrowed thing by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Congo in Paradise Lost, Book XI, 401–406.

reciprocal_annpcoopkdofdhpi.label: as far as the old promise ran in return of a borrowed thing · by inherited custom
reciprocal_annpcoopkdofdhpi.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Congo in Paradise Lost, Book XI, 401–406.

reciprocal_kjefehebgogpjloa.label: conspiracy at second hand
reciprocal_kjefehebgogpjloa.meaning: The substance of conspiracy passed on by a hearer who can vouch for hearing it but cannot vouch for the underlying claim.

reciprocal_baepnjaphbnocoln.label: conspire put to use
reciprocal_baepnjaphbnocoln.meaning: An understanding of conspire that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_kpohogpdhkonnfkb.label: answerable conspiracy
reciprocal_kpohogpdhkonnfkb.meaning: conspiracy — An utterance of this kind given in circumstances where its speaker can be called back to clarify it. It carries a different weight from a rumour with identical words.

reciprocal_hbpdlollnfcglleh.label: Identify by its company · tending a sickbed · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_hbpdlollnfcglleh.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the tending of a sickbed by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Constantine in Leviathan, Chapter 45, Hobbes_0161_1259.3.

reciprocal_ldhncecglbbhacog.label: up to the point of parting in tending of a sickbed · in the wrong season
reciprocal_ldhncecglbbhacog.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Constantine in Leviathan, Chapter 45, Hobbes_0161_1259.3.

reciprocal_fohkmgbjhjggmdio.label: recover the old edge of tending of a sickbed · pending a challenge
reciprocal_fohkmgbjhjggmdio.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Names a provisional arrangement that stands until someone brings a specific objection. Allusion to Constantinople in The Prince, Chapter XIII, 1276.

reciprocal_elfmlclpcbkhklin.label: By retracing the last sure mark · keeping a child’s confidence · at a distance
reciprocal_elfmlclpcbkhklin.meaning: In a manner that retraces the keeping of a child's confidence from the last point one can still positively identify. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to Constantinople in The Prince, Chapter XIII, 1276.

reciprocal_pindengcnciblikd.label: A surviving thread one can work from · keeping seed · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_pindengcnciblikd.meaning: What remains of the keeping of seed that can still carry a practice or memory after the original whole is gone. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Constance in King John 00257a.

reciprocal_idiekpnfcooeccbh.label: Hold a place for the absent · keeping seed · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_idiekpnfcooeccbh.meaning: To leave a practical place for someone's part in the keeping of seed during uncertainty about their return. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Constance in King John 00257a.

reciprocal_keliigcggpkgdiie.label: bracket the uncertainty in keeping of a ferry · by inherited custom
reciprocal_keliigcggpkgdiie.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Conception in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter II, 243.2.

reciprocal_dcbbldmongkleppp.label: By retracing the last sure mark · running a ferry · before a witness
reciprocal_dcbbldmongkleppp.meaning: In a manner that retraces the keeping of a ferry from the last point one can still positively identify. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Conception in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter II, 243.2.

reciprocal_kelffmkgbgobapgp.label: chosen consort
reciprocal_kelffmkgbgobapgp.meaning: An instance of consort that someone deliberately undertakes and can answer for. The outward act may look the same when it happens by accident.

reciprocal_elmkfpklhlobcnho.label: trained consort
reciprocal_elmkfpklhlobcnho.meaning: An instance of consort performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_ebkmkbealolhjaai.label: do consort on another's account
reciprocal_ebkmkbealolhjaai.meaning: consort — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_lakidafokchlgfnp.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · making a mould · by a trace
reciprocal_lakidafokchlgfnp.meaning: To give a judgment about the making of a mould temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to considium in Leviathan, Chapter 30, Hobbes_0161_813.2.

reciprocal_ljjjeidpjecngmjn.label: duty that survives the key in making of a mould · after loss of the original
reciprocal_ljjjeidpjecngmjn.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to considium in Leviathan, Chapter 30, Hobbes_0161_813.2.

reciprocal_kpnakbipgnnmgngh.label: conscience by local measure
reciprocal_kpnakbipgnnmgngh.meaning: The quality called conscience as judged against the things actually available for comparison here.

reciprocal_acbblkkfhdeejfhj.label: conscience under strain
reciprocal_acbblkkfhdeejfhj.meaning: The degree of conscience that remains when the quality is put under an adverse condition.

reciprocal_inmolcchijccgmoh.label: conscience to the practical threshold
reciprocal_inmolcchijccgmoh.meaning: conscience — Having the quality in question to the degree required for the immediate work. Further degrees may be perceptible yet irrelevant to the present choice.

reciprocal_afmgfijcafflofah.label: distinguish an inherited fault in division of a household · by private agreement
reciprocal_afmgfijcafflofah.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Coniah in Jeremiah 22:24.

reciprocal_lgdipfcldfoicemf.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · recording descent · between generations
reciprocal_lgdipfcldfoicemf.meaning: The share of a decision about the record of a descent that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Coniah in Jeremiah 22:24.

reciprocal_kaohpgjdmiepacbe.label: coney sign
reciprocal_kaohpgjdmiepacbe.meaning: The presence of coney inferred from a fresh trace, while the creature itself remains out of sight.

reciprocal_oeiiiokffijbnfak.label: coney refuge
reciprocal_oeiiiokffijbnfak.meaning: A place the observer leaves undisturbed because coney repeatedly returns to it for cover. One sighting alone gives no such claim.

reciprocal_mhchokdonfpmdmkm.label: site-faithful coney
reciprocal_mhchokdonfpmdmkm.meaning: coney — An individual of this kind whose repeated returns to one place are reliable enough for someone to recognize or await it there. The word describes one animal's habits and carries no claim that it is tame.

reciprocal_hggofngcpanfpakb.label: read the gap in laying down of an office · between generations
reciprocal_hggofngcpanfpakb.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to cononiah in 2 Chronicles 31:12.

reciprocal_pkpcmmhfhnbfejhk.label: up to the point of parting in laying down of an office · out of public sight
reciprocal_pkpcmmhfhnbfejhk.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to cononiah in 2 Chronicles 31:12.

reciprocal_ejfiodcklegkjohh.label: trace the hand behind record of a descent · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_ejfiodcklegkjohh.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to Cosam in Luke 3:28.

reciprocal_jcdajhmdfjhgecdj.label: exact at the fork of record of a descent · under shared liability
reciprocal_jcdajhmdfjhgecdj.meaning: Said of knowledge that can distinguish two lines at the moment they parted, even if their subsequent history is obscure. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to Cosam in Luke 3:28.

reciprocal_ddljahgpkefgbmjm.label: recover the old edge of division of a catch · for another's benefit
reciprocal_ddljahgpkefgbmjm.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Costa Rica in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter III, 367.10.

reciprocal_oaapeknhhigjkhco.label: By what the hand can actually fit · sharing a catch · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_oaapeknhhigjkhco.meaning: With the tolerance that matters in the daily handling of the division of a catch, even when a finer distinction exists on paper. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to Costa Rica in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter III, 367.10.

reciprocal_fbolklikekkiejmf.label: unmix two accounts of counting of sleepers · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_fbolklikekkiejmf.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to cosmo in All's Well That Ends Well, passage 0888.

reciprocal_jhlalcdbmojloofi.label: up to the point of parting in counting of sleepers · by inherited custom
reciprocal_jhlalcdbmojloofi.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to cosmo in All's Well That Ends Well, passage 0888.

reciprocal_egpiacbhlehbidaa.label: Distinguish by the smaller sign · telling a voyage · after consent
reciprocal_egpiacbhlehbidaa.meaning: To distinguish two instances within the telling of a voyage bearing the same public sign by a smaller mark meaningful to the people who deal with it. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to Coint in Richard II 00180a.

reciprocal_cfigjpcabkbmohdn.label: Counted without a hearing · placing a mooring · on first use
reciprocal_cfigjpcabkbmohdn.meaning: A member or instance of the placing of a mooring counted in a total but never called individually. It has numerical presence without an individual hearing. Applies on a first attempt, while those involved still have no local precedent of their own. Allusion to Coint in Richard II 00180a.

reciprocal_ndnhbhfoomppcjog.label: read the gap in making of a mould · without a common tongue
reciprocal_ndnhbhfoomppcjog.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Used when a shared word is unavailable and meaning must pass through gesture, example, or an object. Allusion to Coos in Acts 21:1.

reciprocal_jglcdbbndgjfohnk.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · making a mould · under divided authority
reciprocal_jglcdbbndgjfohnk.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the making of a mould at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Coos in Acts 21:1.

reciprocal_mjmoogjepolldkof.label: cowslip season-sign
reciprocal_mjmoogjepolldkof.meaning: The stage of cowslip that local people watch to tell when other seasonal work can begin.

reciprocal_nliklofbhlpapcia.label: cowslip reserve-stock
reciprocal_nliklofbhlpapcia.meaning: A living part of cowslip set aside so that next season's stock survives the present harvest.

reciprocal_pklkileipjkidkdp.label: volunteer cowslip
reciprocal_pklkileipjkidkdp.meaning: cowslip — A plant of this kind that establishes itself where nobody in the present season planted it. Said when its appearance matters as evidence of earlier growth.

reciprocal_lpkkpffdcpehmlam.label: lecture at second hand
reciprocal_lpkkpffdcpehmlam.meaning: The substance of lecture passed on by a hearer who can vouch for hearing it but cannot vouch for the underlying claim.

reciprocal_bjhfpibcnpdmpejb.label: practical force of lecture
reciprocal_bjhfpibcnpdmpejb.meaning: What a hearer reasonably takes lecture to commit the speaker to doing.

reciprocal_fncnoabpmncpeglb.label: answerable lecture
reciprocal_fncnoabpmncpeglb.meaning: lecture — An utterance of this kind given in circumstances where its speaker can be called back to clarify it. It carries a different weight from a rumour with identical words.

reciprocal_ephgnjkpjphmpakn.label: reach of than
reciprocal_ephgnjkpjphmpakn.meaning: The stretch of speech to which than applies in a particular utterance. Moving the boundary can change who or what is included.

reciprocal_eodlhpeknaofcofi.label: echoed than
reciprocal_eodlhpeknaofcofi.meaning: An occurrence of than taken over from another speaker whose framing the present speaker need not endorse.

reciprocal_naanbljpofajcjad.label: than carried over
reciprocal_naanbljpofajcjad.meaning: than — An occurrence of this grammatical form whose interpretation depends on a preceding speaker's wording. Taken alone, it leaves a question of scope or reference open.

reciprocal_hamilhlbadcamgjg.label: according-to with narrow reach
reciprocal_hamilhlbadcamgjg.meaning: Restricts “according-to” to the nearest named participant or condition. Someone hearing a wider connection can use this reading to ask for a correction.

reciprocal_ojnpmlbacagiejgf.label: according-to with carried reach
reciprocal_ojnpmlbacagiejgf.meaning: Extends “according-to” over a following group without requiring each member to repeat the relation. The grouping must be recoverable from the utterance.

reciprocal_mgppojmcbccbajhg.label: according-to in another's terms
reciprocal_mgppojmcbccbajhg.meaning: Reports another person's use of “according-to” while reserving judgment about whether the proposed connection holds. The distinction matters when the relation is contested.

reciprocal_ahmbilnmocgepckp.label: compare intimation
reciprocal_ahmbilnmocgepckp.meaning: A first grasp of compare sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_jhompnnmeloikcio.label: compared put to use
reciprocal_jhompnnmeloikcio.meaning: An understanding of compared that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_ogfimcbohamgeknp.label: compare held on trial
reciprocal_ogfimcbohamgeknp.meaning: compare — A thought or belief of this kind deliberately entertained until a particular question can decide whether to keep it. The speaker owns the test as well as the idea.

reciprocal_ooblhbbimijgjbdc.label: how, asking for what happened
reciprocal_ooblhbbimijgjbdc.meaning: Uses “how” to request an answer grounded in what someone witnessed. An inference belongs in a different reply.

reciprocal_fnmmgphhjdohhila.label: how, asking for an account
reciprocal_fnmmgphhjdohhila.meaning: Uses “how” to invite an explanation linking known things, even when nobody witnessed every step.

reciprocal_dhlcdfankpocmonf.label: how, asking to repair a misunderstanding
reciprocal_dhlcdfankpocmonf.meaning: Reopens the specific part asked by “how” because the first reply answered a different question. Often quieter than repeating the original interrogation.

reciprocal_nbnabljijnijjcle.label: foursquare by local measure
reciprocal_nbnabljijnijjcle.meaning: The quality called foursquare as judged against the things actually available for comparison here.

reciprocal_cidjbbmgljbfdahm.label: foursquare under strain
reciprocal_cidjbbmgljbfdahm.meaning: The degree of foursquare that remains when the quality is put under an adverse condition.

reciprocal_dhdgpknoojjnjaln.label: foursquare to the practical threshold
reciprocal_dhdgpknoojjnjaln.meaning: foursquare — Having the quality in question to the degree required for the immediate work. Further degrees may be perceptible yet irrelevant to the present choice.

reciprocal_clekopemgdcabjpf.label: recover the old edge of drawing of a chart · out of public sight
reciprocal_clekopemgdcabjpf.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to Quantung in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XV, 1571.1.

reciprocal_diolcockpihhpfdo.label: by the point of last agreement in drawing of a chart · at the second attempt
reciprocal_diolcockpihhpfdo.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Quantung in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XV, 1571.1.

reciprocal_hhejgbcpabhhpjke.label: quail courtesy-portion
reciprocal_hhejgbcpabhhpjke.meaning: A share of quail held back for someone who has yet to arrive, even when everyone at table could eat more.

reciprocal_jobkomoacpnkfomj.label: quail lingering taste
reciprocal_jobkomoacpnkfomj.meaning: The taste by which quail can still be recognized after it has been swallowed or taken away.

reciprocal_ancbgckmifkajdii.label: household-owed quail
reciprocal_ancbgckmifkajdii.meaning: quail — Food of this kind already owed to someone at the table before it is served. Offering it to a guest would spend another person's welcome.

reciprocal_ionpineinklmffla.label: Identify by its company · weighing shares · at one's own cost
reciprocal_ionpineinklmffla.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the weighing of a share by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to Quercetanus in The Sceptical Chymist, Part III, 266.18.

reciprocal_nhmbalhbfdinloif.label: up to the point of parting in measuring of a fever · between generations
reciprocal_nhmbalhbfdinloif.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Quercetanus in The Sceptical Chymist, Part III, 266.18.

reciprocal_lmfkmpglcdkckodk.label: quern hand-wear
reciprocal_lmfkmpglcdkckodk.meaning: The polish or hollow left by repeated handling of quern, valued as evidence of who used it or how.

reciprocal_hcphojonaemagkbj.label: quern stand-in
reciprocal_hcphojonaemagkbj.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of quern during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_oecfabnngmpijpjp.label: quern kept in service
reciprocal_oecfabnngmpijpjp.meaning: quern — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_gjlabcdpdpnfpieh.label: read the gap in mending of a net · with a reserve
reciprocal_gjlabcdpdpnfpieh.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Queubus in Twelfth Night 00277a.

reciprocal_fcppbnffllplapeb.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · learning a dance · for another's benefit
reciprocal_fcppbnffllplapeb.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the learning of a dance at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Queubus in Twelfth Night 00277a.

reciprocal_ncjchfcddlhmgknj.label: apparent quell
reciprocal_ncjchfcddlhmgknj.meaning: A change described as quell from its outward signs that reverses when its immediate cause is removed.

reciprocal_fgjnlmkmflhmfghg.label: settled quell
reciprocal_fgjnlmkmflhmfghg.meaning: A change of the kind described by quell that holds after the conditions that produced it have gone.

reciprocal_fhaooaipkdliidld.label: undergo quell past the turning point
reciprocal_fhaooaipkdliidld.meaning: quell — To undergo the change in question far enough that removing its first cause no longer restores the earlier state.

reciprocal_jnnjjdmjkkdklijl.label: stone witness-piece
reciprocal_jnnjjdmjkkdklijl.meaning: A small piece of stone kept to show what the material was like before it was worked or changed.

reciprocal_cfnkhmandjmhbkfb.label: stone trace
reciprocal_cfnkhmandjmhbkfb.meaning: A quantity of stone too small to recover as a useful portion, yet sufficient to change the material that holds it.

reciprocal_epbgefegblmiffio.label: recovered stone
reciprocal_epbgefegblmiffio.meaning: stone — Material of this kind recovered from an earlier use and accepted for another on the strength of what it can still do.

reciprocal_babiafhicpgjiffb.label: A stone with teeth as a deed
reciprocal_babiafhicpgjiffb.meaning: The act or lived situation pictured by the idiom “A stone with teeth”, recognized in a particular case before anyone gives it a name.
reciprocal_babiafhicpgjiffb.origin: productive contrast from kwesta rãnth kerun

reciprocal_dleekkbllnpggigg.label: A stone with teeth turned towards someone
reciprocal_dleekkbllnpggigg.meaning: A pointed use of “A stone with teeth” as an intervention in another person's situation. The addressee can accept or resist that reading.
reciprocal_dleekkbllnpggigg.origin: productive contrast from kwesta rãnth kerun

reciprocal_bnclliglihnkmfnp.label: the second occasion for A stone with teeth
reciprocal_bnclliglihnkmfnp.meaning: A stone with teeth — A recurrence of the situation pictured in this idiom that those involved recognize in time to respond differently.
reciprocal_bnclliglihnkmfnp.origin: narrower alternative from kwesta rãnth kerun

reciprocal_gaceeaedkbhkildi.label: inward The stone you could lift under water
reciprocal_gaceeaedkbhkildi.meaning: The inward experience caught by “The stone you could lift under water” while the person living through it has yet to tell anyone.
reciprocal_gaceeaedkbhkildi.origin: productive contrast from kwesta chetib grel yemsē onega’jwünizya ne

reciprocal_hmdiheikmlfadgfa.label: recognized The stone you could lift under water
reciprocal_hmdiheikmlfadgfa.meaning: A moment of recognizing in another's account the experience that “The stone you could lift under water” had named only privately.
reciprocal_hmdiheikmlfadgfa.origin: productive contrast from kwesta chetib grel yemsē onega’jwünizya ne

reciprocal_lmhjjbnbafankeib.label: The stone you could lift under water spoken back
reciprocal_lmhjjbnbafankeib.meaning: The stone you could lift under water — The experience pictured by the idiom when someone else puts it into words before the person feeling it has been able to do so.
reciprocal_lmhjjbnbafankeib.origin: narrower alternative from kwesta chetib grel yemsē onega’jwünizya ne

reciprocal_idhigedmbeofamjo.label: A stone for the return as a deed
reciprocal_idhigedmbeofamjo.meaning: The act or lived situation pictured by the idiom “A stone for the return”, recognized in a particular case before anyone gives it a name.
reciprocal_idhigedmbeofamjo.origin: productive contrast from kwesta tē sezifãjzh

reciprocal_kjhbmnhokenbdego.label: A stone for the return turned towards someone
reciprocal_kjhbmnhokenbdego.meaning: A pointed use of “A stone for the return” as an intervention in another person's situation. The addressee can accept or resist that reading.
reciprocal_kjhbmnhokenbdego.origin: productive contrast from kwesta tē sezifãjzh

reciprocal_fhkhahdjchiehojg.label: the second occasion for A stone for the return
reciprocal_fhkhahdjchiehojg.meaning: A stone for the return — A recurrence of the situation pictured in this idiom that those involved recognize in time to respond differently.
reciprocal_fhkhahdjchiehojg.origin: narrower alternative from kwesta tē sezifãjzh

reciprocal_npkekldmknclabfl.label: The stone still has your heat as a deed
reciprocal_npkekldmknclabfl.meaning: The act or lived situation pictured by the idiom “The stone still has your heat”, recognized in a particular case before anyone gives it a name.
reciprocal_npkekldmknclabfl.origin: productive contrast from kwesta velin nel’hersh sãfowya

reciprocal_fbmfnppciidcfbld.label: The stone still has your heat turned towards someone
reciprocal_fbmfnppciidcfbld.meaning: A pointed use of “The stone still has your heat” as an intervention in another person's situation. The addressee can accept or resist that reading.
reciprocal_fbmfnppciidcfbld.origin: productive contrast from kwesta velin nel’hersh sãfowya

reciprocal_ckfgegjghomecgkh.label: the second occasion for The stone still has your heat
reciprocal_ckfgegjghomecgkh.meaning: The stone still has your heat — A recurrence of the situation pictured in this idiom that those involved recognize in time to respond differently.
reciprocal_ckfgegjghomecgkh.origin: narrower alternative from kwesta velin nel’hersh sãfowya

reciprocal_mijincgbdbpplodd.label: The unthrown stone wins as a deed
reciprocal_mijincgbdbpplodd.meaning: The act or lived situation pictured by the idiom “The unthrown stone wins”, recognized in a particular case before anyone gives it a name.
reciprocal_mijincgbdbpplodd.origin: productive contrast from kwesta ma’tarnimowfu ziftowya

reciprocal_ebmnjhckfkljfjjj.label: The unthrown stone wins turned towards someone
reciprocal_ebmnjhckfkljfjjj.meaning: A pointed use of “The unthrown stone wins” as an intervention in another person's situation. The addressee can accept or resist that reading.
reciprocal_ebmnjhckfkljfjjj.origin: productive contrast from kwesta ma’tarnimowfu ziftowya

reciprocal_pokkmappecpfnbjg.label: the second occasion for The unthrown stone wins

reciprocal_olbnffpclmecjcbd.label: Leave someone the means to continue · returning a loan · by private agreement

reciprocal_ialhlcceinfiefnk.label: Time made free by a prior gift · returning a loan · in the wrong season

reciprocal_dclflclbhlnflnpn.label: stay to see relief of a night watch take hold · by inherited custom

Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to Archibald in Henry IV, Part I 00006a.

reciprocal_knfodlmfljlkmjlc.label: distinguish an inherited fault in division of a household · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_knfodlmfljlkmjlc.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to Ard in Numbers 26:40.

reciprocal_aamfihjakeipcfnd.label: By retracing the last sure mark · taking testimony · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_aamfihjakeipcfnd.meaning: In a manner that retraces the taking of testimony from the last point one can still positively identify. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Arde in Henry VIII 00008a.

reciprocal_fjhefppnpecechgf.label: bracket the uncertainty in setting of a trap · after consent
reciprocal_fjhefppnpecechgf.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to Arden in As You Like It 00205a.

reciprocal_ginipdhnlggbpjhe.label: By retracing the last sure mark · setting traps · after a handover
reciprocal_ginipdhnlggbpjhe.meaning: In a manner that retraces the setting of a trap from the last point one can still positively identify. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to Arden in As You Like It 00205a.

reciprocal_likcobniicojcffb.label: Stay past the handover · laying down office · out of public sight
reciprocal_likcobniicojcffb.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the laying down of an office after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to Ardea in Lucrece 00005b.

reciprocal_fbfbgohoahbkcndn.label: Common ground that still bears work · collecting tolls · on first use
reciprocal_fbfbgohoahbkcndn.meaning: The portion of the collection of a toll that remains jointly workable during a dispute. Its scope is measured by what both parties still actually do. Applies on a first attempt, while those involved still have no local precedent of their own. Allusion to Ardea in Lucrece 00005b.

reciprocal_ilfelhhlfojnofmm.label: trace the hand behind keeping of a hearth · after loss of the original
reciprocal_ilfelhhlfojnofmm.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to ardon in 1 Chronicles 2:18.

reciprocal_oflenkcdfchnjonh.label: share left without a voice in keeping of a hearth · in the wrong season
reciprocal_oflenkcdfchnjonh.meaning: A part included in the total for which nobody present has authority to speak. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to ardon in 1 Chronicles 2:18.

reciprocal_ncplmmbnnjjdijjj.label: read the gap in return of a borrowed thing · after consent
reciprocal_ncplmmbnnjjdijjj.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to Argestes in Paradise Lost, Book X, 699–703.

reciprocal_hflpcnpcimfhjbgf.label: so far as the hand remembers in sealing of a letter · under divided authority
reciprocal_hflpcnpcimfhjbgf.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Argestes in Paradise Lost, Book X, 699–703.

reciprocal_gijahlmndkgmhkfm.label: Identify by its company · placing a mooring · after a failed trial
reciprocal_gijahlmndkgmhkfm.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the placing of a mooring by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to Argo in Paradise Lost, Book II, 1017–1020.

reciprocal_kmiompdejbabcflo.label: up to the point of parting in placing of a mooring · between strangers
reciprocal_kmiompdejbabcflo.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to Argo in Paradise Lost, Book II, 1017–1020.

reciprocal_fhfiedllgbdbalib.label: trace the hand behind laying out of a boundary · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_fhfiedllgbdbalib.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. reciprocal_papgogmkmpgkbmje.label: By retracing the last sure mark · taking testimony · with a reserve
reciprocal_papgogmkmpgkbmje.meaning: In a manner that retraces the taking of testimony from the last point one can still positively identify. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Argob in Paradise Lost, Book I, 397–399.

reciprocal_bfhbmfjebpjjjifb.label: Identify by its company · returning a loan · at the second attempt
reciprocal_bfhbmfjebpjjjifb.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the return of a borrowed thing by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Argonautica in The Sceptical Chymist, Part II, 192.1.

reciprocal_paimgmgifpkigpgi.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · sealing a letter · at the second attempt
reciprocal_paimgmgifpkigpgi.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the sealing of a letter at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Argonautica in The Sceptical Chymist, Part II, 192.1.

reciprocal_elimohimfbenbcap.label: Identify by its company · tending a shared lamp · between generations

reciprocal_kjplkidhdabmhghc.label: so far as the hand remembers in relief of a night watch · between strangers

reciprocal_okgblekalihhachg.label: read the gap in selection of a witness · in company with a novice

reciprocal_mcpeidhgcoeceffj.label: so far as the hand remembers in naming of a child · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_mcpeidhgcoeceffj.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to arpad in Isaiah 10:9.

reciprocal_bnmcbdoelmlokljp.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · handing over a key · pending a challenge

reciprocal_pklhfaljgeonmapn.label: duty that survives the key in laying down of an office · after a handover

reciprocal_cgnoagmklnpeffoc.label: read the gap in handover of a key · for another's benefit

reciprocal_mjopndjepgoakhgo.label: up to the point of parting in collection of a toll · after a disputed account

reciprocal_celiejobkjhjfehm.label: up to the point of parting in timing of a departure · at the point of commitment

reciprocal_gpkmikbhokahgaka.label: A voice recognizable in the retelling · passing messages · pending a challenge

reciprocal_fgmjlghpbbjlobli.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · laying down office · by a trace

reciprocal_kngbhjieldpoploj.label: affection held in check

reciprocal_fmamnmkfhlmbchbb.label: affection borne for someone else

reciprocal_odmoedecklblbjpe.label: lover by practice

reciprocal_bpejdameeleenkfb.label: trusted working lover

reciprocal_afckponepgldjaee.label: trained woo

reciprocal_dooadgjcihghbgpi.label: A voice recognizable in the retelling · naming a child · after consent

reciprocal_bhilcjgodhohfdde.label: restore the order of taking of soundings · before a witness

reciprocal_kgjffikcnadlphkc.label: restore the order of making of a mould · after loss of the original

reciprocal_aefbagekfigcoeog.label: Hold a place for the absent · recovering strays · with a reserve

reciprocal_lncbkmekadmckfad.label: By retracing the last sure mark · keeping seed · on independent confirmation

reciprocal_hdakdkeadeknjdie.label: hyssop season-sign

reciprocal_gfkbfiilioleicho.label: hyssop reserve-stock

reciprocal_hmfngdbnohdbneig.label: volunteer hyssop

reciprocal_oefcckmdgggiliob.meaning: The taste by which fat-collop can still be recognized after it has been swallowed or taken away.

reciprocal_jbbknfjjhhfpepip.label: household-owed fat-collop
reciprocal_jbbknfjjhhfpepip.meaning: fat-collop — Food of this kind already owed to someone at the table before it is served. Offering it to a guest would spend another person's welcome.

reciprocal_ebegombellpelnki.label: Identify by its company · recording descent · with a reserve

reciprocal_plghcmiefcoeeipc.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · recording descent · in the owner's absence

reciprocal_abmhjpcjogkbehkh.label: recover the old edge of teaching of a route · by a trace

reciprocal_mkleafmggbkhimpl.label: by the point of last agreement in teaching of a route · against the tally
reciprocal_mkleafmggbkhimpl.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. reciprocal_moembjnpdhpngaga.label: stay to see telling of a voyage take hold · on independent confirmation

reciprocal_jmdmjklhiomgnobg.label: up to the point of parting in telling of a voyage · by inherited custom

reciprocal_piigjpeeneolpfjj.label: Stand by within reach · learning a dance · under divided authority

reciprocal_nakhblnkgncpbini.label: A difficulty deliberately left to the learner · learning a dance · after consent

reciprocal_cjldjlkmbgckgphn.label: unmix two accounts of dividing of inherited tools · under shared liability

reciprocal_pmanijklkchbgdcj.label: so far as the hand remembers in dividing of inherited tools · under divided authority

reciprocal_abafpjniffgpomci.label: recover the old edge of teaching of a route · for another's benefit

reciprocal_plicmekddldcnndo.label: by the point of last agreement in drawing of a chart · on independent confirmation

reciprocal_kepjmocoedeflfdo.label: up to the point of parting in keeping of a hearth · by inherited custom

reciprocal_cnakhojlialhcfpk.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · giving a pledge · by a trace

reciprocal_agpojgjfkhkimkkg.label: Backed by an identifiable bearer of loss · changing the night watch · after consent

reciprocal_ejkkmcekegkpgobn.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · telling a voyage · with a reserve

reciprocal_lggbmnefiaeebdbm.label: chosen botch

reciprocal_nnjemkbcokhkfmld.meaning: A living part of cherry set aside so that next season's stock survives the present harvest.

reciprocal_kbpccmlehiegfpkl.label: volunteer cherry
reciprocal_kbpccmlehiegfpkl.meaning: cherry — A plant of this kind that establishes itself where nobody in the present season planted it. Said when its appearance matters as evidence of earlier growth.

reciprocal_fmojfccepgdeijon.label: recover the old edge of teaching of a route · with a reserve
reciprocal_fmojfccepgdeijon.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Chepelio in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VII, 805.2.

reciprocal_degjfnanpoeochhi.label: duty that survives the key in teaching of a route · after consent
reciprocal_degjfnanpoeochhi.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to Chepelio in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VII, 805.2.

reciprocal_fckajhhkldkdojdf.label: chapped by local measure
reciprocal_fckajhhkldkdojdf.meaning: The quality called chapped as judged against the things actually available for comparison here.

reciprocal_jcpanopioodekakh.label: chink trace
reciprocal_jcpanopioodekakh.meaning: A quantity of chink too small to recover as a useful portion, yet sufficient to change the material that holds it.

reciprocal_ajipahffohbcodfm.label: chapped to the practical threshold
reciprocal_ajipahffohbcodfm.meaning: chapped — Having the quality in question to the degree required for the immediate work. Further degrees may be perceptible yet irrelevant to the present choice.

reciprocal_kkhiglghjapedpei.label: Keep the cracked voice as a deed
reciprocal_kkhiglghjapedpei.meaning: The act or lived situation pictured by the idiom “Keep the cracked voice”, recognized in a particular case before anyone gives it a name.
reciprocal_kkhiglghjapedpei.origin: productive contrast from chiril’mū giktenvējėren jemoie

reciprocal_iofnkmeabneehphe.label: Keep the cracked voice turned towards someone
reciprocal_iofnkmeabneehphe.meaning: A pointed use of “Keep the cracked voice” as an intervention in another person's situation. The addressee can accept or resist that reading.
reciprocal_iofnkmeabneehphe.origin: productive contrast from chiril’mū giktenvējėren jemoie

reciprocal_iijlbojahmplfjoa.label: the second occasion for Keep the cracked voice
reciprocal_iijlbojahmplfjoa.meaning: Keep the cracked voice — A recurrence of the situation pictured in this idiom that those involved recognize in time to respond differently.
reciprocal_iijlbojahmplfjoa.origin: narrower alternative from chiril’mū giktenvējėren jemoie

reciprocal_ifnmgdkoocokkbno.label: church hand-wear
reciprocal_ifnmgdkoocokkbno.meaning: The polish or hollow left by repeated handling of church, valued as evidence of who used it or how.

reciprocal_bmlgleigfpajgpho.label: church stand-in
reciprocal_bmlgleigfpajgpho.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of church during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_kadapdkgkhabocbl.label: church kept in service
reciprocal_kadapdkgkhabocbl.meaning: church — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_fnikeahpcfekejjb.label: church-keeper by practice
reciprocal_fnikeahpcfekejjb.meaning: Someone recognized as church-keeper by the work they repeatedly perform before anyone grants a title.

reciprocal_eggoiiddecgcfiee.label: acting church-keeper
reciprocal_eggoiiddecgcfiee.meaning: Someone who carries the obligations of church-keeper for an absence with a definite end.

reciprocal_dbpljdpbhagebimh.label: trusted working church-keeper
reciprocal_dbpljdpbhagebimh.meaning: church-keeper — Someone in this role to whom a community actually brings the difficult cases. Title or seniority alone does not confer the distinction.

reciprocal_iceckhkngbicojaj.label: indulgence by local measure
reciprocal_iceckhkngbicojaj.meaning: The quality called indulgence as judged against the things actually available for comparison here.

reciprocal_cpadkdlekcgcgpld.label: indulgence under strain
reciprocal_cpadkdlekcgcgpld.meaning: The degree of indulgence that remains when the quality is put under an adverse condition.

reciprocal_hlapghcikmjnjkjo.label: indulgence to the practical threshold
reciprocal_hlapghcikmjnjkjo.meaning: indulgence — Having the quality in question to the degree required for the immediate work. Further degrees may be perceptible yet irrelevant to the present choice.

reciprocal_donaemjhjpcmnlfg.label: chide at second hand
reciprocal_donaemjhjpcmnlfg.meaning: The substance of chide passed on by a hearer who can vouch for hearing it but cannot vouch for the underlying claim.

reciprocal_dkfcgpppecoddlni.label: practical force of chide
reciprocal_dkfcgpppecoddlni.meaning: What a hearer reasonably takes chide to commit the speaker to doing.

reciprocal_dfaklmiihabjjbjj.label: answerable chide
reciprocal_dfaklmiihabjjbjj.meaning: chide — An utterance of this kind given in circumstances where its speaker can be called back to clarify it. It carries a different weight from a rumour with identical words.

reciprocal_kihopkgidlchgcde.label: read the gap in counting of sleepers · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_kihopkgidlchgcde.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to chitopher in All's Well That Ends Well, passage 0888.

reciprocal_bahpndmhldijoohj.label: so far as the hand remembers in counting of sleepers · with a reserve
reciprocal_bahpndmhldijoohj.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to chitopher in All's Well That Ends Well, passage 0888.

reciprocal_opejjonimioalfmh.label: Identify by its company · keeping a promise · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_opejjonimioalfmh.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the keeping of a promise by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to China in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XIV, 1485.4.

reciprocal_blmimhkebfhlnehb.label: so far as the hand remembers in setting of a trap · after a disputed account
reciprocal_blmimhkebfhlnehb.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Used in response to an actual difference between people's accounts of what happened. Allusion to China in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XIV, 1485.4.

reciprocal_lipfjeembbjifohj.label: chough sign
reciprocal_lipfjeembbjifohj.meaning: The presence of chough inferred from a fresh trace, while the creature itself remains out of sight.

reciprocal_fgonkinkapmcmece.label: chough refuge
reciprocal_fgonkinkapmcmece.meaning: A place the observer leaves undisturbed because chough repeatedly returns to it for cover. One sighting alone gives no such claim.

reciprocal_pfogljphbbdknlpp.label: site-faithful chough
reciprocal_pfogljphbbdknlpp.meaning: chough — An individual of this kind whose repeated returns to one place are reliable enough for someone to recognize or await it there. The word describes one animal's habits and carries no claim that it is tame.

reciprocal_ijedkmnifpnjcapl.label: chosen choke
reciprocal_ijedkmnifpnjcapl.meaning: An instance of choke that someone deliberately undertakes and can answer for. The outward act may look the same when it happens by accident.

reciprocal_ephkeapogeolkocb.label: trained choke
reciprocal_ephkeapogeolkocb.meaning: An instance of choke performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_nphfopiljbpcfhdn.label: do choke on another's account
reciprocal_nphfopiljbpcfhdn.meaning: choke — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_lbdnibgfnbhgmgdo.label: Restore a neglected voice · caring for graves · by inherited custom
reciprocal_lbdnibgfnbhgmgdo.meaning: To bring a disregarded account of the care of a grave into hearing without taking credit for originating it. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Chaucer in The Two Noble Kinsmen 00002b.

reciprocal_jnhdgdegledopodk.label: Time made free by a prior gift · rehearsing a song · after loss of the original
reciprocal_jnhdgdegledopodk.meaning: Said of a period of freedom in which an earlier provision of the rehearsal of a song allows someone else to choose a course without immediate dependence. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to Chaucer in The Two Noble Kinsmen 00002b.

reciprocal_dbpfedlaifljkbbd.label: recover the old edge of placing of a mooring · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_dbpfedlaifljkbbd.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to Chuche in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VIII, 825.2.

reciprocal_ehlpbpjpcfbnceao.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · drawing charts · for another's benefit
reciprocal_ehlpbpjpcfbnceao.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the drawing of a chart at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Chuche in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VIII, 825.2.

reciprocal_nkkeblbpjbjnglcl.label: restore the order of taking of testimony · in the wrong season
reciprocal_nkkeblbpjbjnglcl.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Chartham in Henry VI, Part 2 00603a.

reciprocal_ninflpefolnbeihd.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · taking testimony · by private agreement
reciprocal_ninflpefolnbeihd.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the taking of testimony at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Chartham in Henry VI, Part 2 00603a.

reciprocal_nahoggigldpbifmp.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · handing over a key · for another's benefit
reciprocal_nahoggigldpbifmp.meaning: To give a judgment about the handover of a key temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Charles in Henry VI, Part 1 00573a.

reciprocal_clmhjgdpbecmigjk.label: duty that survives the key in calling of a council · after a handover
reciprocal_clmhjgdpbecmigjk.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to Charles in Henry VI, Part 1 00573a.

reciprocal_kccnoaemoggfecdb.label: read the gap in marking of a season · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_kccnoaemoggfecdb.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to Charles Cotton in A New Voyage Round the World, Bookseller’s catalogue, 2259.1.

reciprocal_clpobdjfnkgodfeb.label: as far as the old promise ran in marking of a season · at one's own cost
reciprocal_clpobdjfnkgodfeb.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to Charles Cotton in A New Voyage Round the World, Bookseller’s catalogue, 2259.1.

reciprocal_adnfaneaikmmlohc.label: Identify by its company · keeping a child’s confidence · pending a challenge
reciprocal_adnfaneaikmmlohc.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the keeping of a child's confidence by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Names a provisional arrangement that stands until someone brings a specific objection. Allusion to Charmian in Antony and Cleopatra 00028a.

reciprocal_lncacfdkojnohmng.label: so far as the hand remembers in keeping of a child's confidence · as the sole available course
reciprocal_lncacfdkojnohmng.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Charmian in Antony and Cleopatra 00028a.

reciprocal_njnpllifookgnonh.label: Identify by its company · weighing shares · for another's benefit
reciprocal_njnpllifookgnonh.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the weighing of a share by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Charing in Henry IV, Part I 00146a.

reciprocal_ogfplkdaknedcdak.label: so far as the hand remembers in measuring of a fever · at a distance
reciprocal_ogfplkdaknedcdak.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to Charing in Henry IV, Part I 00146a.

reciprocal_mcefdbcfnecjkjah.label: Locate between known limits · running a ferry · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_mcefdbcfnecjkjah.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the keeping of a ferry by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Chagra in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter III, 309.1.

reciprocal_edepmooflmedmmao.label: duty that survives the key in keeping of a ferry · in company with a novice
reciprocal_edepmooflmedmmao.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to Chagra in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter III, 309.1.

reciprocal_cpahkpnjkmkjkppp.label: bracket the uncertainty in drawing of a chart · before a witness
reciprocal_cpahkpnjkmkjkppp.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Chambongo in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XIV, 1425.3.

reciprocal_kpkgbeoiddmfnjnm.label: By retracing the last sure mark · drawing charts · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_kpkgbeoiddmfnjnm.meaning: In a manner that retraces the drawing of a chart from the last point one can still positively identify. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Chambongo in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XIV, 1425.3.

reciprocal_eepneidjpobanchk.label: bracket the uncertainty in selection of a witness · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_eepneidjpobanchk.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Champa in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XIV, 1427.3.

reciprocal_eomaeeknjbdalnkk.label: by the point of last agreement in selection of a witness · after consent
reciprocal_eomaeeknjbdalnkk.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to Champa in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XIV, 1427.3.

reciprocal_anlbpdkkgafckdcl.label: Stay past the handover · teaching a route · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_anlbpdkkgafckdcl.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the teaching of a route after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Chametly in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter IX, 959.8.

reciprocal_mijolcifcbmlfdko.label: By retracing the last sure mark · teaching a route · out of public sight
reciprocal_mijolcifcbmlfdko.meaning: In a manner that retraces the teaching of a route from the last point one can still positively identify. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to Chametly in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter IX, 959.8.

reciprocal_dkeeljgjilkpnamg.label: unmix two accounts of placing of a mooring · by inherited custom
reciprocal_dkeeljgjilkpnamg.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Chandy in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VI, 623.2.

reciprocal_ooobikkljjegnmbe.label: so far as the hand remembers in placing of a mooring · between generations
reciprocal_ooobikkljjegnmbe.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Chandy in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VI, 623.2.

reciprocal_abaphbdaklkkegld.label: read the gap in dyeing of cloth · by inherited custom
reciprocal_abaphbdaklkkegld.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Chau in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XV, 1581.4.

reciprocal_dffmckcpmkdlekai.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · keeping seed · before a witness
reciprocal_dffmckcpmkdlekai.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the keeping of seed at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Chau in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XV, 1581.4.

reciprocal_kcindbglmcicbble.label: chosen enjoy
reciprocal_kcindbglmcicbble.meaning: An instance of enjoy that someone deliberately undertakes and can answer for. The outward act may look the same when it happens by accident.

reciprocal_blaomebjaomlihge.label: estate free to spend
reciprocal_blaomebjaomlihge.meaning: The share of estate left at someone's disposal after the claims of others have been met.

reciprocal_ajdbjfdccfadcgdm.label: do enjoy on another's account
reciprocal_ajdbjfdccfadcgdm.meaning: enjoy — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_gfahiohgimhhacfl.label: chosen possession
reciprocal_gfahiohgimhhacfl.meaning: An instance of possession that someone deliberately undertakes and can answer for. The outward act may look the same when it happens by accident.

reciprocal_afoilcfeokmjkhil.label: trained possession
reciprocal_afoilcfeokmjkhil.meaning: An instance of possession performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_iifbdogiiokkpkhj.label: do possession on another's account
reciprocal_iifbdogiiokkpkhj.meaning: possession — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_mjhoiopjfegjemlg.label: peculiar by local measure
reciprocal_mjhoiopjfegjemlg.meaning: The quality called peculiar as judged against the things actually available for comparison here.

reciprocal_beokhjlokkngiefj.label: peculiar under strain
reciprocal_beokhjlokkngiefj.meaning: The degree of peculiar that remains when the quality is put under an adverse condition.

reciprocal_ijfbejhhlmpcngda.label: peculiar to the practical threshold
reciprocal_ijfbejhhlmpcngda.meaning: peculiar — Having the quality in question to the degree required for the immediate work. Further degrees may be perceptible yet irrelevant to the present choice.

reciprocal_dockbdaledkpigdd.label: dispossess in trust
reciprocal_dockbdaledkpigdd.meaning: dispossess held under a duty to return it or account for it. Physical control and entitlement can belong to different people.

reciprocal_hmebnajpcdaofjbi.label: dispossess free to spend
reciprocal_hmebnajpcdaofjbi.meaning: The share of dispossess left at someone's disposal after the claims of others have been met.

reciprocal_jilakjhoaonagjed.label: encumbered dispossess
reciprocal_jilakjhoaonagjed.meaning: dispossess — A holding of this kind that comes with an existing claim on it. Someone may receive the whole thing and still have only part of it to dispose of.

reciprocal_mcailaapjanbgmnc.label: chosen lay
reciprocal_mcailaapjanbgmnc.meaning: An instance of lay that someone deliberately undertakes and can answer for. The outward act may look the same when it happens by accident.

reciprocal_kgooidaglbdebjhh.label: trained lay
reciprocal_kgooidaglbdebjhh.meaning: An instance of lay performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_mpanifgodjmangla.label: do lay on another's account
reciprocal_mpanifgodjmangla.meaning: lay — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_ehgfblbhpmhcocfd.label: reach of the (French article)
reciprocal_ehgfblbhpmhcocfd.meaning: The stretch of speech to which the (French article) applies in a particular utterance. Moving the boundary can change who or what is included.

reciprocal_odfdkhilmjgmbnlc.label: echoed the (French article)
reciprocal_odfdkhilmjgmbnlc.meaning: An occurrence of the (French article) taken over from another speaker whose framing the present speaker need not endorse.

reciprocal_dmnjlengfbbfnpae.label: the (French article) carried over
reciprocal_dmnjlengfbbfnpae.meaning: the (French article) — An occurrence of this grammatical form whose interpretation depends on a preceding speaker's wording. Taken alone, it leaves a question of scope or reference open.

reciprocal_eiohlmgeeffjolpd.label: Locate between known limits · landing a boat · by private agreement
reciprocal_eiohlmgeeffjolpd.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the landing of a boat by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Chequetan in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter IX, 905.6.

reciprocal_pbjnoampnehafocg.label: by the point of last agreement in placing of a mooring · by private agreement
reciprocal_pbjnoampnehafocg.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. reciprocal_pfhepmgiaidalani.label: Identify by its company · choosing witnesses · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_pfhepmgiaidalani.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the selection of a witness by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. reciprocal_klmhcpgdcjgdgdep.label: up to the point of parting in naming of a child · as the sole available course
reciprocal_klmhcpgdcjgdgdep.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Cecco Guinigi in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3069.

reciprocal_laegaakbbekbnlij.label: restore the order of care of a shared lamp · by a trace
reciprocal_laegaakbbekbnlij.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. reciprocal_joodfgeaplfikhfj.label: so far as the hand remembers in mending of a net · after a disputed account

reciprocal_ilcaecciohaidlhn.label: recover the old edge of keeping of a ferry · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_ilcaecciohaidlhn.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Cheapo in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter II, 237.1.

reciprocal_fbkhoijkgiccegme.label: By retracing the last sure mark · building bridges · by private agreement
reciprocal_fbkhoijkgiccegme.meaning: In a manner that retraces the placing of a bridge from the last point one can still positively identify. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Cheapo in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter II, 237.1.

reciprocal_mmmdngajffncnkfc.label: trace the hand behind care of a shared lamp · between generations
reciprocal_mmmdngajffncnkfc.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Cheran in Genesis 36:26.

reciprocal_hajlblmfhgoegkjm.label: share left without a voice in marking of a season · between generations
reciprocal_hajlblmfhgoegkjm.meaning: A part included in the total for which nobody present has authority to speak. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Cheran in Genesis 36:26.

reciprocal_apibblalmkbcmhgj.label: unmix two accounts of naming of a child · out of public sight
reciprocal_apibblalmkbcmhgj.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to Cheriquanas in Two Treatises of Government, Second Treatise, Chapter VIII, 800.3.

reciprocal_ippjljiiammaeepg.label: so far as the hand remembers in selection of a witness · after a disputed account
reciprocal_ippjljiiammaeepg.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Used in response to an actual difference between people's accounts of what happened. Allusion to Cheriquanas in Two Treatises of Government, Second Treatise, Chapter VIII, 800.3.

reciprocal_dcialakjedbedeeg.label: unmix two accounts of handover of a key · after consent
reciprocal_dcialakjedbedeeg.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to Cherith in 1 Kings 17:3.

reciprocal_mhhacehchdkefnoo.label: as far as the old promise ran in collection of a toll · by a trace
reciprocal_mhhacehchdkefnoo.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to Cherith in 1 Kings 17:3.

reciprocal_akncodngkfpdjafh.label: those, as I point
reciprocal_akncodngkfpdjafh.meaning: The deictic “those” resolved by a present gesture. The expression depends on the speaker showing the hearer where to look.

reciprocal_acncdooiinbhnpkj.label: those, as we both remember
reciprocal_acncdooiinbhnpkj.meaning: The deictic “those” used for something absent from sight but identifiable through a particular shared experience.

reciprocal_plfjnlmjffgcpfkf.label: those, as just introduced
reciprocal_plfjnlmjffgcpfkf.meaning: Directs attention back to the immediately preceding account, even when another object in sight would otherwise be a natural referent.

reciprocal_jagiifkdkinpccpo.label: object intimation
reciprocal_jagiifkdkinpccpo.meaning: A first grasp of object sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_loellmbgkbliajfa.label: thing stand-in
reciprocal_loellmbgkbliajfa.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of thing during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_jnajpnlcanahodam.label: object held on trial

reciprocal_cdkifihljldmkaen.label: accusative at second hand

reciprocal_ehlfjegndbpohedj.label: practical force of accusative

reciprocal_hgabmddafkbaihcp.label: answerable accusative

reciprocal_embfeljmcojpfjnd.label: what, asking for what happened
reciprocal_embfeljmcojpfjnd.meaning: Uses “what” to request an answer grounded in what someone witnessed. An inference belongs in a different reply.

reciprocal_nnbapchlnlcdiakp.label: what, asking for an account
reciprocal_nnbapchlnlcdiakp.meaning: Uses “what” to invite an explanation linking known things, even when nobody witnessed every step.

reciprocal_gmcijldpehiclbmf.label: what, asking to repair a misunderstanding
reciprocal_gmcijldpehiclbmf.meaning: Reopens the specific part asked by “what” because the first reply answered a different question. Often quieter than repeating the original interrogation.

reciprocal_iegnpgecchpmncii.label: Ask which end of the blanket as a deed

reciprocal_dbnjjbmnolbgjajg.label: the second occasion for Ask which end of the blanket

reciprocal_pagmbdanfmdnmmfk.label: manna courtesy-portion

reciprocal_hghmopehbooponnh.label: manna lingering taste
reciprocal_hghmopehbooponnh.meaning: The taste by which manna can still be recognized after it has been swallowed or taken away.

reciprocal_eoelnbndhoocpjne.label: household-owed manna
reciprocal_eoelnbndhoocpjne.meaning: manna — Food of this kind already owed to someone at the table before it is served. Offering it to a guest would spend another person's welcome.

reciprocal_hmldbmdlekhfepgp.label: What comes up on the lead as a deed

reciprocal_jeondbfamiagfede.label: What comes up on the lead turned towards someone

reciprocal_glihddmkpjpcohkm.label: the second occasion for What comes up on the lead

reciprocal_oecjaccbnllcjegn.label: whatever by local measure

reciprocal_abagecooifipmmia.label: whatever under strain
reciprocal_abagecooifipmmia.meaning: The degree of whatever that remains when the quality is put under an adverse condition.

reciprocal_mjnalmedajbndlkj.label: whatever to the practical threshold
reciprocal_mjnalmedajbndlkj.meaning: whatever — Having the quality in question to the degree required for the immediate work. Further degrees may be perceptible yet irrelevant to the present choice.

reciprocal_kbnfiekfokldpjod.label: what (as spoken), asking for what happened
reciprocal_kbnfiekfokldpjod.meaning: Uses “what (as spoken)” to request an answer grounded in what someone witnessed. An inference belongs in a different reply.

reciprocal_akjhhiojbomjfdde.label: what (as spoken), asking for an account

reciprocal_bkfkcpiambnkmheh.label: what (as spoken), asking to repair a misunderstanding

reciprocal_bgepicajnfdlhmac.label: reach of the (lesson)

reciprocal_bnlbamihibiljgab.label: this put to use
reciprocal_bnlbamihibiljgab.meaning: An understanding of this that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_kdhkeepbhhmhihoe.label: the (lesson) carried over
reciprocal_kdhkeepbhhmhihoe.meaning: the (lesson) — An occurrence of this grammatical form whose interpretation depends on a preceding speaker's wording. Taken alone, it leaves a question of scope or reference open.

reciprocal_gjdkpmhgjngebbhb.label: opening of tonight
reciprocal_gjdkpmhgjngebbhb.meaning: The earliest part of tonight in which an action becomes possible, even if a reckoning on paper puts its beginning earlier.

reciprocal_eiekcghjdfidhpjp.label: grace of tonight
reciprocal_eiekcghjdfidhpjp.meaning: The unofficial tail of tonight during which a person is still received as being in time.

reciprocal_mefacopbellgofdi.label: tonight reckoned together
reciprocal_mefacopbellgofdi.meaning: tonight — An interval of this kind reckoned from an event shared by the people involved, so that each can identify its beginning without consulting a clock.

reciprocal_iiobhhcagaficacc.label: restore the order of care of a grave · between generations
reciprocal_iiobhhcagaficacc.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. reciprocal_bilihoifbhelndcm.label: as far as the old promise ran in care of a grave · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_bilihoifbhelndcm.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. reciprocal_bbkpfobeedbfaodl.label: unmix two accounts of measuring of a fever · in the owner's absence

reciprocal_gfgbddhdodbnfbii.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · keeping a promise · without a common tongue
reciprocal_gfgbddhdodbnfbii.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the keeping of a promise at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. reciprocal_bnblbcocdepcjeie.label: unmix two accounts of telling of a voyage · between generations

reciprocal_odadnanedhfeneea.label: Locate between known limits · sharing inherited tools · as the sole available course

reciprocal_lmgilbgikppgaggi.label: by the point of last agreement in making of a mould · by private agreement
reciprocal_lmgilbgikppgaggi.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Chepharhaammonai in Joshua 18:24.

reciprocal_ddfhaancpifaloke.label: recover the old edge of giving of a pledge · without a common tongue

reciprocal_fnncgdngbmlmnhlj.label: learned well enough to reverse in giving of a pledge · between generations
reciprocal_fnncgdngbmlmnhlj.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. reciprocal_jgkkfdcbfjccclci.label: these, as I point
reciprocal_jgkkfdcbfjccclci.meaning: The deictic “these” resolved by a present gesture. The expression depends on the speaker showing the hearer where to look.

reciprocal_afpdfakfblcbnkci.label: these, as we both remember
reciprocal_afpdfakfblcbnkci.meaning: The deictic “these” used for something absent from sight but identifiable through a particular shared experience.

reciprocal_kahlakpiaadlopom.label: these, as just introduced
reciprocal_kahlakpiaadlopom.meaning: Directs attention back to the immediately preceding account, even when another object in sight would otherwise be a natural referent.

reciprocal_biidfbiingheloan.label: unmix two accounts of rehearsal of a song · after loss of the original

reciprocal_gcomnnlkadbglabb.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · rehearsing a song · after loss of the original

reciprocal_mjenomfobpnbpofa.label: thatone, as I point
reciprocal_mjenomfobpnbpofa.meaning: The deictic “thatone” resolved by a present gesture. The expression depends on the speaker showing the hearer where to look.

reciprocal_nhmkhecofaoplfok.label: thatone, as we both remember
reciprocal_nhmkhecofaoplfok.meaning: The deictic “thatone” used for something absent from sight but identifiable through a particular shared experience.

reciprocal_neickmmddacboclp.label: thatone, as just introduced
reciprocal_neickmmddacboclp.meaning: Directs attention back to the immediately preceding account, even when another object in sight would otherwise be a natural referent.

reciprocal_bpkhomcmdgeohnhl.label: bracket the uncertainty in making of a mould · against the tally

reciprocal_pmekdjdblcibfpkd.label: by the point of last agreement in dividing of inherited tools · between generations
reciprocal_pmekdjdblcibfpkd.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Chesalon in Joshua 15:10.

reciprocal_cgbbfeojpbmdjihc.label: Locate between known limits · teaching a route · between strangers

reciprocal_nkffgajecnefibjh.label: By retracing the last sure mark · choosing witnesses · by a trace

reciprocal_kdmkemjiocgpggoa.label: bracket the uncertainty in drawing of a chart · after a failed trial

reciprocal_bgliidbodkiflddf.label: recover the old edge of placing of a bridge · by private agreement

reciprocal_aikooicjhfcifkdj.meaning: A member or instance of the return of a borrowed thing counted in a total but never called individually. It has numerical presence without an individual hearing. reciprocal_hojpfamkigofippg.meaning: The substance of loophole passed on by a hearer who can vouch for hearing it but cannot vouch for the underlying claim.

reciprocal_epdoebfeajlhoihl.label: answerable loophole
reciprocal_epdoebfeajlhoihl.meaning: loophole — An utterance of this kind given in circumstances where its speaker can be called back to clarify it. It carries a different weight from a rumour with identical words.

reciprocal_cjaedhchpihnciie.label: Trace through successive hands · handing over a key · after a handover
reciprocal_cjaedhchpihnciie.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the handover of a key by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry.
