reciprocal_ocikpgnpgdhdgfij.label: taught within one line of laying down of an office · by inherited custom
reciprocal_ocikpgnpgdhdgfij.meaning: Said of a skill transmitted within one line of teachers. Outsiders may perform the same work by a recognizably different sequence. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Darda in 1 Kings 4:31.

reciprocal_icjjjdkihoaclkhh.label: Bound a disagreement · running a ferry · for another's benefit
reciprocal_icjjjdkihoaclkhh.meaning: To isolate the disputed part of the keeping of a ferry so that the people involved can still work together on the rest. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Dardan in Lucrece 00212.

reciprocal_ooefjidanddcigec.label: By retracing the last sure mark · running a ferry · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_ooefjidanddcigec.meaning: In a manner that retraces the keeping of a ferry from the last point one can still positively identify. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Dardan in Lucrece 00212.

reciprocal_kifkhhnlladcpnkg.label: Transmit beyond the written record · choosing witnesses · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_kifkhhnlladcpnkg.meaning: To transmit a practice of the selection of a witness beyond the last person or occasion named in its written record. The practice may continue on different terms. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to Dardanus in Julius Caesar 00830a.

reciprocal_bligpdoffelgmmkc.label: up to the point of parting in measuring of a fever · before a witness

reciprocal_ceafgmhcdlnkknek.label: mouldy to the practical threshold

reciprocal_iponhafaodihdlme.label: board witness-piece

reciprocal_hendkojghaajbeaf.label: board trace
reciprocal_hendkojghaajbeaf.meaning: A quantity of board too small to recover as a useful portion, yet sufficient to change the material that holds it.

reciprocal_kgfkncepfgddgdjp.label: recovered board
reciprocal_kgfkncepfgddgdjp.meaning: board — Material of this kind recovered from an earlier use and accepted for another on the strength of what it can still do.

reciprocal_ibombikeagdhakfa.label: Restore a neglected voice · handing over a key · at the second attempt
reciprocal_ibombikeagdhakfa.meaning: To bring a disregarded account of the handover of a key into hearing without taking credit for originating it. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to de Cassado in Henry VIII 00491a.

reciprocal_ncmpglndhjaadkmj.label: Shared in sign alone · handing over a key · out of public sight
reciprocal_ncmpglndhjaadkmj.meaning: Said of a sign of the handover of a key used by different people whose connection cannot be inferred from the sign alone. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to de Cassado in Henry VIII 00491a.

reciprocal_djgkchpkljnobhdj.label: unmix two accounts of storage of water · in the wrong season
reciprocal_djgkchpkljnobhdj.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. reciprocal_inalmdddedfnahdl.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · landing a boat · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_inalmdddedfnahdl.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the landing of a boat at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to de-Rochas in The Sceptical Chymist, Part II, 202.41.

reciprocal_kdlaalbmcihaiadn.label: Restore a neglected voice · dividing a household · after loss of the original
reciprocal_kdlaalbmcihaiadn.meaning: To bring a disregarded account of the division of a household into hearing without taking credit for originating it. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to de la Car in Henry VIII 00058a.

reciprocal_mbjdiedlkhjcfhjl.label: voice of the first correction in division of a household · by a trace
reciprocal_mbjdiedlkhjcfhjl.meaning: A small change in a repeated account which identifies the person who first corrected it. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to de la Car in Henry VIII 00058a.

reciprocal_hklpkfklnahdflki.label: distinguish an inherited fault in collection of a toll · out of public sight

reciprocal_jmakdoejhhmbiifi.label: taught within one line of collection of a toll · under divided authority

reciprocal_okglhchkgbfkhecm.label: Locate between known limits · setting prices · between generations

reciprocal_cbhfbmclcdlkohml.label: share left without a voice in drawing of a chart · before a witness
reciprocal_cbhfbmclcdlkohml.meaning: A part included in the total for which nobody present has authority to speak. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to decapolis in Mark 5:20.

reciprocal_kncpdgcdblgdplle.label: so far as the hand remembers in drying of a harvest · before a witness

reciprocal_gdcecomgbkkjcccm.label: nine threshold
reciprocal_gdcecomgbkkjcccm.meaning: nine taken as the least quantity that makes a difference to a decision.

reciprocal_pnfgbagpljoiineo.label: short of nine

reciprocal_nbmnnamklkcaofpk.label: usable nine

reciprocal_bcenjcboaamgfanb.label: usable nine gross
reciprocal_bcenjcboaamgfanb.meaning: nine gross — An amount reckoned in this unit after what cannot actually be delivered has been taken out. The nominal amount may be greater.

reciprocal_dnlbkaemganenedm.label: opening of September

reciprocal_bibdopnkbofneimi.label: September reckoned together
reciprocal_bibdopnkbofneimi.meaning: September — An interval of this kind reckoned from an event shared by the people involved, so that each can identify its beginning without consulting a clock.

reciprocal_caehphkkdncjfbgj.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · changing the night watch · on first use

reciprocal_kiclnablpappdpdl.label: recover the old edge of laying out of a boundary · by private agreement

reciprocal_aejigfjegjdfjnpm.label: stay to see placing of a bridge take hold · under divided authority

reciprocal_meaehmceaphgcppi.meaning: In a manner that retraces the placing of a bridge from the last point one can still positively identify. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Debir in Joshua 15:7.

reciprocal_iplemnkbopkehaph.label: Hold a place for the absent · caring for graves · at a distance

reciprocal_lpofhbepgnmddamc.label: Trace through successive hands · taking testimony · by a trace

reciprocal_lfljhpadkgjjiloi.label: Learned down one branch · recording descent · by a trace

reciprocal_mdfphmclegifpfoa.label: Trace through successive hands · setting traps · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_mdfphmclegifpfoa.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the setting of a trap by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. reciprocal_jbmjjbmjokpgiojf.label: learned well enough to reverse in record of a descent · as the sole available course

reciprocal_aafigklbefcmbkck.label: stay to see telling of a voyage take hold · by private agreement

reciprocal_iefchpminajbnegp.label: restore the order of passing of a message · under a closing opportunity

reciprocal_hfjbfhlcblojpcmk.label: so far as the hand remembers in passing of a message · with a reserve
reciprocal_hfjbfhlcblojpcmk.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Devonshire in Richard III 01049a.

reciprocal_ojndmleikjkggbck.label: Leave someone the means to continue · making a mould · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_ojndmleikjkggbck.meaning: To give someone the means to continue with the making of a mould once immediate assistance ends. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Desdemon in Othello 00448a.

reciprocal_egalhfnoogclokcc.label: Time made free by a prior gift · making a mould · after consent

reciprocal_kdococfdghdeilac.label: restore the order of division of a household · on independent confirmation

reciprocal_gmjjbljckncbgoai.label: up to the point of parting in division of a household · with a reserve
reciprocal_gmjjbljckncbgoai.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Desdemona in Othello 00258a.

reciprocal_lbfmokcbiempmnde.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · telling a voyage · in the owner's absence

reciprocal_iklmfageofbghdlc.label: Learned well enough to retrace · telling a voyage · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_iklmfageofbghdlc.meaning: Said of a route, habit, or piece of knowledge of the telling of a voyage which can be retraced independently after learning it in someone else's company. reciprocal_ecjkkknabhgeokdi.label: Distinguish by the smaller sign · calling a council · at one's own cost

reciprocal_jjanmebmediiakcb.label: Shared in sign alone · calling a council · on first use

reciprocal_hkgieglbdbpkolcb.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · marking a boundary · as the sole available course

reciprocal_klmibnfbcekdjgeh.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · keeping a child’s confidence · under a closing opportunity

reciprocal_hnmlhdjejjmihdef.label: trace the hand behind choice of a guardian · at the point of commitment

reciprocal_cflacnaccdgnmlpg.label: Learned down one branch · naming a child · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_cflacnaccdgnmlpg.meaning: Said of knowledge of the naming of a child that is exact on one line of descent or transmission while adjacent lines remain undocumented. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to Delaiah in Nehemiah 6:10.

reciprocal_ijbgbnmhienibmed.label: Restore a neglected voice · timing a departure · in the wrong season
reciprocal_ijbgbnmhienibmed.meaning: To bring a disregarded account of the timing of a departure into hearing without taking credit for originating it. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Delphi in Paradise Lost, Book I, 514–518.

reciprocal_kjkfaabifonjafcn.label: A voice recognizable in the retelling · taking testimony · by private agreement
reciprocal_kjkfaabifonjafcn.meaning: A remembered turn of phrase that discloses whose account of the taking of testimony is being repeated even after the speaker's name has dropped out. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Delphi in Paradise Lost, Book I, 514–518.

reciprocal_kgfljlobjmnccefh.label: recover the old edge of drawing of a chart · between generations
reciprocal_kgfljlobjmnccefh.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Delphos in Leviathan, Chapter 12, Hobbes_0161_341.2.

reciprocal_nfhajfjpgmopopff.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · drawing charts · without a common tongue
reciprocal_nfhajfjpgmopopff.meaning: The share of a decision about the drawing of a chart that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Used when a shared word is unavailable and meaning must pass through gesture, example, or an object. Allusion to Delphos in Leviathan, Chapter 12, Hobbes_0161_341.2.

reciprocal_nigmllkpjmpkenhm.label: Restore a neglected voice · rehearsing a song · pending a challenge
reciprocal_nigmllkpjmpkenhm.meaning: To bring a disregarded account of the rehearsal of a song into hearing without taking credit for originating it. Names a provisional arrangement that stands until someone brings a specific objection. Allusion to Delia in Paradise Lost, Book IX, 385–392.

reciprocal_nimldahidokdleha.label: A difficulty deliberately left to the learner · rehearsing a song · after a handover
reciprocal_nimldahidokdleha.meaning: The margin of difficulty in the rehearsal of a song a helper leaves untouched so the learner can discover their own reach. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to Delia in Paradise Lost, Book IX, 385–392.

reciprocal_mbihimknjlalelid.label: Identify by its company · telling a voyage · in the wrong season
reciprocal_mbihimknjlalelid.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the telling of a voyage by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Delilah in Judges 16:4.

reciprocal_ljdlmiclcpbadnlg.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · telling a voyage · after consent
reciprocal_ljdlmiclcpbadnlg.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the telling of a voyage at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to Delilah in Judges 16:4.

reciprocal_chadocopkcepanlj.label: Locate between known limits · drawing charts · after a disputed account
reciprocal_chadocopkcepanlj.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the drawing of a chart by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. Used in response to an actual difference between people's accounts of what happened. Allusion to Delos in Leviathan, Chapter 12, Hobbes_0161_341.2.

reciprocal_oeficmaahndbgbjk.label: duty that survives the key in drawing of a chart · out of public sight
reciprocal_oeficmaahndbgbjk.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to Delos in Leviathan, Chapter 12, Hobbes_0161_341.2.

reciprocal_lbcbjndhafcellgm.label: Stand by within reach · naming a child · under divided authority
reciprocal_lbcbjndhafcellgm.meaning: To remain close enough to help with the naming of a child while leaving the person concerned free to finish the act. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Demas in Colossians 4:14.

reciprocal_jmlpinieahjohnpn.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · choosing witnesses · at the second attempt
reciprocal_jmlpinieahjohnpn.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the selection of a witness at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Demas in Colossians 4:14.

reciprocal_adjcbnjencobdmck.label: restore the order of keeping of a child's confidence · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_adjcbnjencobdmck.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Demetrius in Antony and Cleopatra 00002a.

reciprocal_cgpjdlkiphbmapaj.label: so far as the hand remembers in keeping of a child's confidence · pending a challenge
reciprocal_cgpjdlkiphbmapaj.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Names a provisional arrangement that stands until someone brings a specific objection. Allusion to Demetrius in Antony and Cleopatra 00002a.

reciprocal_egiebcnaflabcoka.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · learning a dance · in the wrong season
reciprocal_egiebcnaflabcoka.meaning: To give a judgment about the learning of a dance temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Demetrius in 3 John 1:12.

reciprocal_fjmbbgenobieelhn.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · learning a dance · under divided authority
reciprocal_fjmbbgenobieelhn.meaning: The share of a decision about the learning of a dance that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Demetrius in 3 John 1:12.

reciprocal_jgacihphlbjbneeo.label: Identify by its company · choosing witnesses · before a witness
reciprocal_jgacihphlbjbneeo.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the selection of a witness by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Democritus in The Sceptical Chymist, Part II, 202.13.

reciprocal_eibojjlbnjflhlnf.label: up to the point of parting in selection of a witness · for another's benefit
reciprocal_eibojjlbnjflhlnf.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Democritus in The Sceptical Chymist, Part II, 202.13.

reciprocal_fjjdcpfjnnhlfkpi.label: Identify by its company · drawing charts · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_fjjdcpfjnnhlfkpi.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the drawing of a chart by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to Demogorgon in Paradise Lost, Book II, 959–967.

reciprocal_idinddabbnjpjpmc.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · weighing shares · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_idinddabbnjpjpmc.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the weighing of a share at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Demogorgon in Paradise Lost, Book II, 959–967.

reciprocal_kihlalnhgmpkhona.label: impression intimation
reciprocal_kihlalnhgmpkhona.meaning: A first grasp of impression sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_gecdkdfbnkjhfndo.meaning: What a hearer reasonably takes figure/sign to commit the speaker to doing.

reciprocal_peloedcnlncmlngh.label: impression held on trial

reciprocal_pdeadmgcmmfnkhgm.label: imprese put to use
reciprocal_pdeadmgcmmfnkhgm.meaning: An understanding of imprese that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_ddjjcknpbanijfcn.label: short of case

reciprocal_eddfdkgnjokdkegk.label: exact at the fork of handover of a key · against the tally

reciprocal_koobfpablhjngmbn.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · telling a voyage · after a handover

reciprocal_inacffjbjonhjboo.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · naming a child · at the second attempt

reciprocal_emnegedillpcnfef.label: octavo by local measure
reciprocal_emnegedillpcnfef.meaning: The quality called octavo as judged against the things actually available for comparison here.

reciprocal_jkeagkdokijedkff.label: octavo under strain
reciprocal_jkeagkdokijedkff.meaning: The degree of octavo that remains when the quality is put under an adverse condition.

reciprocal_phlpaopflpbjifbn.label: octavo to the practical threshold
reciprocal_phlpaopflpbjifbn.meaning: octavo — Having the quality in question to the degree required for the immediate work. Further degrees may be perceptible yet irrelevant to the present choice.

reciprocal_efhimedjhlkdckac.label: duodecimo intimation
reciprocal_efhimedjhlkdckac.meaning: A first grasp of duodecimo sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_jifgcjpndaokaefj.label: duodecimo put to use
reciprocal_jifgcjpndaokaefj.meaning: An understanding of duodecimo that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_onlceklbjmdjbemh.label: duodecimo held on trial
reciprocal_onlceklbjmdjbemh.meaning: duodecimo — A thought or belief of this kind deliberately entertained until a particular question can decide whether to keep it. The speaker owns the test as well as the idea.

reciprocal_ohbmjgfolcgdlpdo.label: quarto by local measure
reciprocal_ohbmjgfolcgdlpdo.meaning: The quality called quarto as judged against the things actually available for comparison here.

reciprocal_bcmbbinbmjcnopmi.label: quarto under strain
reciprocal_bcmbbinbmjcnopmi.meaning: The degree of quarto that remains when the quality is put under an adverse condition.

reciprocal_kpccmjlonjbldbca.label: quarto to the practical threshold
reciprocal_kpccmjlonjbldbca.meaning: quarto — Having the quality in question to the degree required for the immediate work. Further degrees may be perceptible yet irrelevant to the present choice.

reciprocal_alogekppmebnjpfj.label: Locate between known limits · running a ferry · at the second attempt
reciprocal_alogekppmebnjpfj.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the keeping of a ferry by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to gozan in 2 Kings 19:12.

reciprocal_hnjbpbdoicdbalde.label: by the point of last agreement in keeping of a ferry · after a failed trial
reciprocal_hnjbpbdoicdbalde.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to gozan in 2 Kings 19:12.

reciprocal_oijjpmmbhjbfpamn.label: Bound a disagreement · sharing inherited tools · out of public sight
reciprocal_oijjpmmbhjbfpamn.meaning: To isolate the disputed part of the dividing of inherited tools so that the people involved can still work together on the rest. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to Gough in Henry VI, Part 2 00696a.

reciprocal_djkcicdgpplfoicb.label: Common ground that still bears work · sharing inherited tools · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_djkcicdgpplfoicb.meaning: The portion of the dividing of inherited tools that remains jointly workable during a dispute. Its scope is measured by what both parties still actually do. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Gough in Henry VI, Part 2 00696a.

reciprocal_nalnebfpcikgpfem.label: gopher sign
reciprocal_nalnebfpcikgpfem.meaning: The presence of gopher inferred from a fresh trace, while the creature itself remains out of sight.

reciprocal_lkheaghlnkjhkjob.label: gopher refuge
reciprocal_lkheaghlnkjhkjob.meaning: A place the observer leaves undisturbed because gopher repeatedly returns to it for cover. One sighting alone gives no such claim.

reciprocal_ahmknekmcjjeefah.label: site-faithful gopher
reciprocal_ahmknekmcjjeefah.meaning: gopher — An individual of this kind whose repeated returns to one place are reliable enough for someone to recognize or await it there. The word describes one animal's habits and carries no claim that it is tame.

reciprocal_fhfofhkdkgjbiikh.label: Identify by its company · repairing a roof · as the sole available course
reciprocal_fhfofhkdkgjbiikh.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the repair of a roof by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Gaul in The Merry Wives of Windsor 00528a.

reciprocal_kkkcafkjeelkblph.label: as far as the old promise ran in repair of a roof · after consent
reciprocal_kkkcafkjeelkblph.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to Gaul in The Merry Wives of Windsor 00528a.

reciprocal_cgfabnpcpglpddga.label: Locate between known limits · calling a council · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_cgfabnpcpglpddga.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the calling of a council by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Golan in Deuteronomy 4:43.

reciprocal_npepgdmlbcaaifgm.label: exact at the fork of calling of a council · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_npepgdmlbcaaifgm.meaning: Said of knowledge that can distinguish two lines at the moment they parted, even if their subsequent history is obscure. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to Golan in Deuteronomy 4:43.

reciprocal_mkinmaicojmbnjnj.label: Identify by its company · choosing witnesses · as the sole available course
reciprocal_mkinmaicojmbnjnj.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the selection of a witness by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to golgotha in Matthew 27:33.

reciprocal_fjnjbjofddnegbak.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · naming a child · in the wrong season
reciprocal_fjnjbjofddnegbak.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the naming of a child at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to golgotha in Matthew 27:33.

reciprocal_cpidfmhjknkhalbe.label: Bound a disagreement · setting traps · by private agreement
reciprocal_cpidfmhjknkhalbe.meaning: To isolate the disputed part of the setting of a trap so that the people involved can still work together on the rest. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Gaultree in Henry IV, Part 2 00601a.

reciprocal_gnnenkjoldbpokdo.label: Common ground that still bears work · setting traps · after a handover
reciprocal_gnnenkjoldbpokdo.meaning: The portion of the setting of a trap that remains jointly workable during a dispute. Its scope is measured by what both parties still actually do. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to Gaultree in Henry IV, Part 2 00601a.

reciprocal_cooliohlkeocicnb.label: restore the order of settling of a quarrel · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_cooliohlkeocicnb.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Goliath in The Prince, Chapter XIII, 1312.

reciprocal_dcjlmbjojbcemjeg.label: as far as the old promise ran in settling of a quarrel · as the sole available course
reciprocal_dcjlmbjojbcemjeg.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Goliath in The Prince, Chapter XIII, 1312.

reciprocal_lfhkjmjflbdjcfdp.label: distinguish an inherited fault in taking of testimony · in the wrong season
reciprocal_lfhkjmjflbdjcfdp.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Gomer in 1 Chronicles 1:6.

reciprocal_bpmahpeffplfkeda.label: exact at the fork of telling of a voyage · between generations
reciprocal_bpmahpeffplfkeda.meaning: Said of knowledge that can distinguish two lines at the moment they parted, even if their subsequent history is obscure. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Gomer in 1 Chronicles 1:6.

reciprocal_fhmafljjbhkhpacf.label: distinguish an inherited fault in selection of a witness · after a handover
reciprocal_fhmafljjbhkhpacf.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to Gomorrah in Genesis 19:24.

reciprocal_cgchajmdihaffeda.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · making a mould · on first use
reciprocal_cgchajmdihaffeda.meaning: The share of a decision about the making of a mould that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Applies on a first attempt, while those involved still have no local precedent of their own. Allusion to Gomorrha in Romans 9:29.

reciprocal_jlpcpalcefmkmbfp.label: Identify by its company · drawing charts · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_jlpcpalcefmkmbfp.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the drawing of a chart by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Gong in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XII, 1299.1.

reciprocal_cpigbppffnbdblog.label: as far as the old promise ran in drawing of a chart · by a trace
reciprocal_cpigbppffnbdblog.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to Gong in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XII, 1299.1.

reciprocal_njppbekcgidimalb.label: read the gap in learning of a dance · in company with a novice
reciprocal_njppbekcgidimalb.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to Gonzago in Hamlet 00474a.

reciprocal_amdbkffimbfmeogb.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · learning a dance · in company with a novice
reciprocal_amdbkffimbfmeogb.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the learning of a dance at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to Gonzago in Hamlet 00474a.

reciprocal_bngngbfhfgpeeidp.label: The gift that preserves a calling
reciprocal_bngngbfhfgpeeidp.meaning: A provision for someone driven from home that allows their life's work to continue after the immediate danger. From Gonzalo setting books among the supplies for Prospero.

reciprocal_opkdipdailncolic.label: Help from within an order one cannot reverse
reciprocal_opkdipdailncolic.meaning: To protect someone subject to a decision one lacks power to undo by changing what that person goes away with.

reciprocal_jmfdklclmeekjdaj.label: Stand by within reach · naming a child · on first use
reciprocal_jmfdklclmeekjdaj.meaning: To remain close enough to help with the naming of a child while leaving the person concerned free to finish the act. Applies on a first attempt, while those involved still have no local precedent of their own. Allusion to Goneril in King Lear 00088a.

reciprocal_kffbblejmgnhjkof.label: A difficulty deliberately left to the learner · naming a child · at the second attempt
reciprocal_kffbblejmgnhjkof.meaning: The margin of difficulty in the naming of a child a helper leaves untouched so the learner can discover their own reach. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Goneril in King Lear 00088a.

reciprocal_cfkchdkaffgdlghb.label: chosen gun
reciprocal_cfkchdkaffgdlghb.meaning: An instance of gun that someone deliberately undertakes and can answer for. The outward act may look the same when it happens by accident.

reciprocal_epgdbdekinmdhlbh.label: trained gun
reciprocal_epgdbdekinmdhlbh.meaning: An instance of gun performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_knebpncckemhgjfn.label: do gun on another's account
reciprocal_knebpncckemhgjfn.meaning: gun — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_pcephdhlhnllenjp.label: chosen gunshot
reciprocal_pcephdhlhnllenjp.meaning: An instance of gunshot that someone deliberately undertakes and can answer for. The outward act may look the same when it happens by accident.

reciprocal_phdidclcncgiiibk.label: trained gunshot
reciprocal_phdidclcncgiiibk.meaning: An instance of gunshot performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_ejodgcgbghcdjefp.label: do gunshot on another's account
reciprocal_ejodgcgbghcdjefp.meaning: gunshot — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_hijghcheiloagaco.label: carbine hand-wear
reciprocal_hijghcheiloagaco.meaning: The polish or hollow left by repeated handling of carbine, valued as evidence of who used it or how.

reciprocal_macfdbgebipjfnkh.label: carbine stand-in
reciprocal_macfdbgebipjfnkh.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of carbine during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_dlofgelblkibabmd.label: carbine kept in service
reciprocal_dlofgelblkibabmd.meaning: carbine — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_hooeaaceddajjbbj.label: gun-platform approach
reciprocal_hooeaaceddajjbbj.meaning: The approach from which a traveller first recognizes gun-platform before reaching the place itself.

reciprocal_ipkiiakafkoodblf.label: gun-platform meeting-ground
reciprocal_ipkiiakafkoodblf.meaning: The part of gun-platform people use to meet or change hands, identified by what happens there.

reciprocal_ioacfbofknchdode.label: gun-platform known as shelter
reciprocal_ioacfbofknchdode.meaning: gun-platform — A place of this kind that someone knows how to reach for safety from experience, even if it has never been formally set aside as a refuge.

reciprocal_lefdmodgpagnjkbl.label: trace the hand behind telling of a voyage · by inherited custom
reciprocal_lefdmodgpagnjkbl.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Goshen in Exodus 9:26.

reciprocal_igkogjblebgcmnbe.label: exact at the fork of telling of a voyage · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_igkogjblebgcmnbe.meaning: Said of knowledge that can distinguish two lines at the moment they parted, even if their subsequent history is obscure. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Goshen in Exodus 9:26.

reciprocal_jhkbclbmgfbicole.label: stay to see relief of a night watch take hold · by a trace
reciprocal_jhkbclbmgfbicole.meaning: To accompany a person far enough beyond a handover to see whether they can actually continue alone. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to Gower in Henry V 00289a.

reciprocal_cgigahogcgifmafi.label: duty that survives the key in relief of a night watch · as the sole available course
reciprocal_cgigahogcgifmafi.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Gower in Henry V 00289a.

reciprocal_bclikeefkpoghnfj.label: unmix two accounts of distribution of bread · by private agreement
reciprocal_bclikeefkpoghnfj.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Gawsey in Henry IV, Part I 00825a.

reciprocal_epbcleaaoafmgngg.label: up to the point of parting in measuring of a fever · at the second attempt
reciprocal_epbcleaaoafmgngg.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Gawsey in Henry IV, Part I 00825a.

reciprocal_cbcfhecgjafjhdkk.label: fragile by local measure
reciprocal_cbcfhecgjafjhdkk.meaning: The quality called fragile as judged against the things actually available for comparison here.

reciprocal_ehbaonniilfdeaec.label: fragile under strain
reciprocal_ehbaonniilfdeaec.meaning: The degree of fragile that remains when the quality is put under an adverse condition.

reciprocal_ceolnmhecodldcfa.label: fragile to the practical threshold
reciprocal_ceolnmhecodldcfa.meaning: fragile — Having the quality in question to the degree required for the immediate work. Further degrees may be perceptible yet irrelevant to the present choice.

reciprocal_nlkcomnedpgdggnp.label: bracket the uncertainty in drawing of a chart · after loss of the original
reciprocal_nlkcomnedpgdggnp.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to Guahon in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter X, 1137.1.

reciprocal_nijfpopnjcblgdll.label: Time made free by a prior gift · teaching a route · at a distance
reciprocal_nijfpopnjcblgdll.meaning: Said of a period of freedom in which an earlier provision of the teaching of a route allows someone else to choose a course without immediate dependence. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to Guahon in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter X, 1137.1.

reciprocal_kchonmcdegdcihpp.label: Locate between known limits · marking a boundary · by private agreement
reciprocal_kchonmcdegdcihpp.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the laying out of a boundary by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Guatimala in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XV, 1635.7.

reciprocal_opaclaecckglhlhd.label: By retracing the last sure mark · marking a boundary · under shared liability
reciprocal_opaclaecckglhlhd.meaning: In a manner that retraces the laying out of a boundary from the last point one can still positively identify. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to Guatimala in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XV, 1635.7.

reciprocal_bmpnpdjkoeebbmbc.label: Stay past the handover · telling a voyage · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_bmpnpdjkoeebbmbc.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the telling of a voyage after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Guatulco in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter IX, 905.1.

reciprocal_hnnnmfailbcdmijb.label: Learned well enough to retrace · telling a voyage · after consent
reciprocal_hnnnmfailbcdmijb.meaning: Said of a route, habit, or piece of knowledge of the telling of a voyage which can be retraced independently after learning it in someone else's company. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to Guatulco in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter IX, 905.1.

reciprocal_ddaglmnfmfpgefgk.label: recover the old edge of drawing of a chart · as the sole available course
reciprocal_ddaglmnfmfpgefgk.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Gualata in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter IV, 411.1.

reciprocal_kfejgnpihehpjnjj.label: by the point of last agreement in drawing of a chart · under divided authority
reciprocal_kfejgnpihehpjnjj.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. reciprocal_aaahcpmcoafjekmf.label: Leave someone the means to continue · landing a boat · under shared liability
reciprocal_aaahcpmcoafjekmf.meaning: To give someone the means to continue with the landing of a boat once immediate assistance ends. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to Gualtier in Henry VI, Part 2 00531a.

reciprocal_fhjedjieafgadfli.label: Time made free by a prior gift · landing a boat · in the wrong season
reciprocal_fhjedjieafgadfli.meaning: Said of a period of freedom in which an earlier provision of the landing of a boat allows someone else to choose a course without immediate dependence. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Gualtier in Henry VI, Part 2 00531a.

reciprocal_bocoobfjpjahmkcj.label: Stay past the handover · teaching a route · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_bocoobfjpjahmkcj.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the teaching of a route after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Guam in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter X, 1039.4.

reciprocal_mejnnpofcfdanbmg.label: By retracing the last sure mark · choosing witnesses · without a common tongue
reciprocal_mejnnpofcfdanbmg.meaning: In a manner that retraces the selection of a witness from the last point one can still positively identify. Used when a shared word is unavailable and meaning must pass through gesture, example, or an object. Allusion to Guam in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter X, 1039.4.

reciprocal_iplcmkjijpkpklek.label: Settle the matter by the fit · placing a mooring · under divided authority
reciprocal_iplcmkjijpkpklek.meaning: To settle a disputed description of the placing of a mooring by trying an actual fit or repeated use. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Guanchaquo in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter V, 495.6.

reciprocal_mijnmmgbpblaagdc.label: By what the hand can actually fit · placing a mooring · in the wrong season
reciprocal_mijnmmgbpblaagdc.meaning: With the tolerance that matters in the daily handling of the placing of a mooring, even when a finer distinction exists on paper. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Guanchaquo in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter V, 495.6.

reciprocal_pjhmcjabbeeailac.label: bracket the uncertainty in collection of a toll · with a reserve
reciprocal_pjhmcjabbeeailac.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Guasco in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VI, 595.2.

reciprocal_pojfmlokhlmggcbc.label: By retracing the last sure mark · collecting tolls · under divided authority
reciprocal_pojfmlokhlmggcbc.meaning: In a manner that retraces the collection of a toll from the last point one can still positively identify. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Guasco in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VI, 595.2.

reciprocal_npicooicmikblghj.label: stay to see teaching of a route take hold · after a handover
reciprocal_npicooicmikblghj.meaning: To accompany a person far enough beyond a handover to see whether they can actually continue alone. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to Guiaquil in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter I, 129.5.

reciprocal_eofgkpmpofpginll.label: by the point of last agreement in teaching of a route · without a common tongue
reciprocal_eofgkpmpofpginll.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Used when a shared word is unavailable and meaning must pass through gesture, example, or an object. Allusion to Guiaquil in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter I, 129.5.

reciprocal_maemdkdbdkbbdccg.label: read the gap in repair of a roof · as the sole available course
reciprocal_maemdkdbdkbbdccg.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Guelph in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3192.

reciprocal_mfnmndnlpdfegbjb.label: so far as the hand remembers in setting of a price · under shared liability
reciprocal_mfnmndnlpdfegbjb.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to Guelph in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3192.

reciprocal_ldnjafppajedambg.label: Stay past the handover · setting prices · between strangers
reciprocal_ldnjafppajedambg.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the setting of a price after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to Guido Ubaldo in The Prince, Chapter XX, 2149.

reciprocal_ppfgilchpfldeofh.label: learned well enough to reverse in fitting of a hinge · against the tally
reciprocal_ppfgilchpfldeofh.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to Guido Ubaldo in The Prince, Chapter XX, 2149.

reciprocal_gbjmobomeedbanjd.label: trace the hand behind timing of a departure · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_gbjmobomeedbanjd.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. reciprocal_decjndeicfckfmid.label: by the point of last agreement in division of a household · before a witness
reciprocal_decjndeicfckfmid.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Guinigi in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 2963.

reciprocal_epjmpfimcblnjfkd.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · choosing witnesses · by a trace
reciprocal_epjmpfimcblnjfkd.meaning: To give a judgment about the selection of a witness temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to Guinover in Love's Labor's Lost 00448a.

reciprocal_hglgjclnoomogipl.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · choosing witnesses · without a common tongue
reciprocal_hglgjclnoomogipl.meaning: The share of a decision about the selection of a witness that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Used when a shared word is unavailable and meaning must pass through gesture, example, or an object. Allusion to Guinover in Love's Labor's Lost 00448a.

reciprocal_gkhmjkdodadbaapo.label: Identify by its company · naming a child · before a witness
reciprocal_gkhmjkdodadbaapo.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the naming of a child by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Guaxaca in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VIII, 877.9.

reciprocal_kmonbccebgiffjff.label: as far as the old promise ran in selection of a witness · under shared liability
reciprocal_kmonbccebgiffjff.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to Guaxaca in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VIII, 877.9.

reciprocal_gdajcckmlkclojkh.label: group intimation
reciprocal_gdajcckmlkclojkh.meaning: A first grasp of group sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_nppippmlalakgckm.label: group put to use
reciprocal_nppippmlalakgckm.meaning: An understanding of group that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_bncfcioeoapjpojb.label: group held on trial
reciprocal_bncfcioeoapjpojb.meaning: group — A thought or belief of this kind deliberately entertained until a particular question can decide whether to keep it. The speaker owns the test as well as the idea.

reciprocal_ichchjahfobdijbf.label: restore the order of weighing of a share · after consent
reciprocal_ichchjahfobdijbf.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. reciprocal_ioolafphfppcdoon.label: so far as the hand remembers in keeping of seed · under a closing opportunity

reciprocal_padcncclignemhgd.label: heap threshold
reciprocal_padcncclignemhgd.meaning: heap taken as the least quantity that makes a difference to a decision.

reciprocal_hpnckcpaleempamc.label: pile reach

reciprocal_pkaggnabckmnccea.label: usable heap

reciprocal_kkonobpfmpnfhlbe.label: chosen riot
reciprocal_kkonobpfmpnfhlbe.meaning: An instance of riot that someone deliberately undertakes and can answer for. The outward act may look the same when it happens by accident.

reciprocal_cmkkadccjgldomjf.label: trained riot
reciprocal_cmkkadccjgldomjf.meaning: An instance of riot performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_khmfjafoandllnkp.label: do riot on another's account
reciprocal_khmfjafoandllnkp.meaning: riot — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_gccccadkocgfgagi.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · telling a voyage · in the wrong season
reciprocal_gccccadkocgfgagi.meaning: To give a judgment about the telling of a voyage temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Gurry in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XVI, 1847.5.

reciprocal_ahildknpocpiohpi.label: as far as the old promise ran in telling of a voyage · by inherited custom
reciprocal_ahildknpocpiohpi.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Gurry in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XVI, 1847.5.

reciprocal_ahcldeegjepefkhn.label: among from the traveller's position
reciprocal_ahcldeegjepefkhn.meaning: Uses “among” relative to the position occupied by the moving observer at the moment in question.

reciprocal_mhiglllpgibfhiag.label: among by a fixed landmark
reciprocal_mhiglllpgibfhiag.meaning: Uses “among” from a landmark on which the speakers have agreed. The relation stays put when either speaker turns around.

reciprocal_nnbkjlddijnkpfkf.label: among on the inherited route
reciprocal_nnbkjlddijnkpfkf.meaning: Uses “among” in the directions of someone else's journey or description. The speaker temporarily takes over that traveller's frame of reference.

reciprocal_jhmdbnfhohfcghob.label: read the gap in placing of a bridge · against the tally
reciprocal_jhmdbnfhohfcghob.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to Goodrich in Henry VI, Part 1 00585a.

reciprocal_eiikbmicggonlifb.label: so far as the hand remembers in taking of soundings · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_eiikbmicggonlifb.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to Goodrich in Henry VI, Part 1 00585a.

reciprocal_hbokkdmodlmklmmd.label: Stay past the handover · running a ferry · by a trace
reciprocal_hbokkdmodlmklmmd.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the keeping of a ferry after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to Gudgodah in Deuteronomy 10:7.

reciprocal_nokadldndocilmmd.label: by the point of last agreement in storage of water · between generations
reciprocal_nokadldndocilmmd.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Gudgodah in Deuteronomy 10:7.

reciprocal_jnafpbgeoihcjgeo.label: stay to see telling of a voyage take hold · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_jnafpbgeoihcjgeo.meaning: To accompany a person far enough beyond a handover to see whether they can actually continue alone. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Goodlud in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XIII, 1357.3.

reciprocal_knobpjmmncmnelga.label: By retracing the last sure mark · telling a voyage · after consent
reciprocal_knobpjmmncmnelga.meaning: In a manner that retraces the telling of a voyage from the last point one can still positively identify. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to Goodlud in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XIII, 1357.3.

reciprocal_kpegjlomiooimfdf.label: Stand by within reach · dividing a household · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_kpegjlomiooimfdf.meaning: To remain close enough to help with the division of a household while leaving the person concerned free to finish the act. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Goodman in Henry VI, Part 2 00066a.

reciprocal_jhkincnefgnknjei.label: A difficulty deliberately left to the learner · dividing a household · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_jhkincnefgnknjei.meaning: The margin of difficulty in the division of a household a helper leaves untouched so the learner can discover their own reach. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Goodman in Henry VI, Part 2 00066a.

reciprocal_ogdmdnicapgeedij.label: unmix two accounts of repair of a roof · before a witness
reciprocal_ogdmdnicapgeedij.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Goodwin in King John 00556a.

reciprocal_giafjfcjoldgchen.label: up to the point of parting in keeping of a promise · with a reserve
reciprocal_giafjfcjoldgchen.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Goodwin in King John 00556a.

reciprocal_ekhpcdgaakjmhbim.label: lump acting together
reciprocal_ekhpcdgaakjmhbim.meaning: lump understood as acting with an agreed voice. Mere co-presence gives no one authority to speak for the group.

reciprocal_bbfmcbmfckkgmhjl.label: edge of lump
reciprocal_bbfmcbmfckkgmhjl.meaning: Those whose connection with lump matters in practice although their membership is disputed or left unrecorded.

reciprocal_bndelejaobihehbm.label: freely assembled lump
reciprocal_bndelejaobihehbm.meaning: lump — A group of this kind whose members have had a real opportunity to leave and have chosen to remain together for this purpose.

reciprocal_knbmipobolbjjbjm.label: gross threshold
reciprocal_knbmipobolbjjbjm.meaning: gross taken as the least quantity that makes a difference to a decision.

reciprocal_efopilchjeoepnib.label: grossness under strain
reciprocal_efopilchjeoepnib.meaning: The degree of grossness that remains when the quality is put under an adverse condition.

reciprocal_jllpomjceobndhkh.label: usable gross
reciprocal_jllpomjceobndhkh.meaning: gross — An amount reckoned in this unit after what cannot actually be delivered has been taken out. The nominal amount may be greater.

reciprocal_pnnhpldlnlnmboko.label: apparent coagulate
reciprocal_pnnhpldlnlnmboko.meaning: A change described as coagulate from its outward signs that reverses when its immediate cause is removed.

reciprocal_nebnncjooipbddib.label: settled coagulate
reciprocal_nebnncjooipbddib.meaning: A change of the kind described by coagulate that holds after the conditions that produced it have gone.

reciprocal_gnkfhkidmffnjnmc.label: undergo coagulate past the turning point
reciprocal_gnkfhkidmffnjnmc.meaning: coagulate — To undergo the change in question far enough that removing its first cause no longer restores the earlier state.

reciprocal_ifmgdipmapcnnmgo.label: Identify by its company · taking testimony · under shared liability
reciprocal_ifmgdipmapcnnmgo.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the taking of testimony by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to Gunther in The Sceptical Chymist, Part I, 128.70.

reciprocal_igdjadldjchinfbd.label: up to the point of parting in taking of testimony · out of public sight
reciprocal_igdjadldjchinfbd.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to Gunther in The Sceptical Chymist, Part I, 128.70.

reciprocal_afjbgkdgjejbbfoa.label: distinguish an inherited fault in telling of a voyage · in the wrong season
reciprocal_afjbgkdgjejbbfoa.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Guni in Genesis 46:24.

reciprocal_lopcdkfeiplmbeon.label: Learned well enough to retrace · telling a voyage · by private agreement
reciprocal_lopcdkfeiplmbeon.meaning: Said of a route, habit, or piece of knowledge of the telling of a voyage which can be retraced independently after learning it in someone else's company. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Guni in Genesis 46:24.

reciprocal_iogepcbepgijljjm.label: bracket the uncertainty in laying out of a boundary · after a handover
reciprocal_iogepcbepgijljjm.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to Gusciana in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3213.

reciprocal_jmnfiljffpgemmck.label: by the point of last agreement in keeping of a ferry · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_jmnfiljffpgemmck.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Gusciana in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3213.

reciprocal_hdbhpppkbpdhfakf.label: restore the order of record of a descent · between generations
reciprocal_hdbhpppkbpdhfakf.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Guiderius in Cymbeline 00740a.

reciprocal_elkmpkgkemcmchki.label: up to the point of parting in record of a descent · after a handover
reciprocal_elkmpkgkemcmchki.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to Guiderius in Cymbeline 00740a.

reciprocal_hbeaanhcdjlhmejn.label: restore the order of sealing of a letter · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_hbeaanhcdjlhmejn.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to Guiana in The Merry Wives of Windsor 00184a.

reciprocal_bcibegmfcdeicglj.label: up to the point of parting in sealing of a letter · after a failed trial
reciprocal_bcibegmfcdeicglj.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to Guiana in The Merry Wives of Windsor 00184a.

reciprocal_bnpbeekgbpedopep.label: stop by a chosen course
reciprocal_bnpbeekgbpedopep.meaning: The part of a movement described by stop that can be steered; drift or recoil may account for the rest.

reciprocal_pcgempecmjbdikmo.label: stop under momentum
reciprocal_pcgempecmjbdikmo.meaning: Movement of the kind described by stop that continues after the initiating effort has stopped.

reciprocal_dapacmbpglmljfpn.label: guide a movement of stop
reciprocal_dapacmbpglmljfpn.meaning: stop — To make the movement in question while continually correcting the course from what one sees or feels along the way.

reciprocal_ffalgnlocmdfelea.label: restore the order of teaching of a route · at a distance

reciprocal_dpdplafhmnigfocp.label: up to the point of parting in teaching of a route · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_dpdplafhmnigfocp.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to Giah in 2 Samuel 2:24.

reciprocal_jhdkhkdfkglemkbp.label: recover the old edge of sealing of a letter · at the second attempt

reciprocal_dfanpoocnngapbfk.label: By retracing the last sure mark · sealing a letter · with a right to withdraw

reciprocal_endpbiinoihhahpe.label: unmix two accounts of record of a descent · with a reserve

reciprocal_debdchmknkgflaeo.label: so far as the hand remembers in record of a descent · with a right to withdraw

reciprocal_klkdcjcokdcppafk.label: bah intimation
reciprocal_klkdcjcokdcppafk.meaning: A first grasp of bah sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_lgbgdpjdcopeaban.label: bah put to use
reciprocal_lgbgdpjdcopeaban.meaning: An understanding of bah that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_apnhijggmmcignfc.label: bah held on trial
reciprocal_apnhijggmmcignfc.meaning: bah — A thought or belief of this kind deliberately entertained until a particular question can decide whether to keep it. The speaker owns the test as well as the idea.

reciprocal_oflpekambbanfemc.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · keeping a promise · pending a challenge

reciprocal_bnonngfignajcplp.label: Backed by an identifiable bearer of loss · naming a child · before a witness

reciprocal_gaboblpfipalknfc.label: unmix two accounts of reckoning of a debt · in the wrong season

reciprocal_epdegnonmknnpleb.label: as far as the old promise ran in giving of a pledge · for another's benefit

reciprocal_iilhccffjnhcjcbb.label: Transmit beyond the written record · taking soundings · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_iilhccffjnhcjcbb.meaning: To transmit a practice of the taking of soundings beyond the last person or occasion named in its written record. The practice may continue on different terms. reciprocal_olcfckpdoekddfod.label: so far as the hand remembers in division of a catch · at a distance
reciprocal_olcfckpdoekddfod.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. reciprocal_emophkebohnlnbpi.label: paradise approach

reciprocal_pbpkbcccbakiojmc.meaning: The part of paradise people use to meet or change hands, identified by what happens there.

reciprocal_epfenjffdicedbgc.label: paradise known as shelter
reciprocal_epfenjffdicedbgc.meaning: paradise — A place of this kind that someone knows how to reach for safety from experience, even if it has never been formally set aside as a refuge.

reciprocal_cemfdkbapnfdbccm.label: paramour by practice
reciprocal_cemfdkbapnfdbccm.meaning: Someone recognized as paramour by the work they repeatedly perform before anyone grants a title.

reciprocal_empibajclkmefcmi.label: acting paramour
reciprocal_empibajclkmefcmi.meaning: Someone who carries the obligations of paramour for an absence with a definite end.

reciprocal_pdiafjgknofocekb.label: trusted working paramour
reciprocal_pdiafjgknofocekb.meaning: paramour — Someone in this role to whom a community actually brings the difficult cases. Title or seniority alone does not confer the distinction.

reciprocal_bbcolkgpikbgoedl.label: Identify by its company · tending a sickbed · before a witness

reciprocal_opjjciobimabphfg.label: up to the point of parting in tending of a sickbed · in company with a novice
reciprocal_opjjciobimabphfg.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to Paran in Genesis 21:21.

reciprocal_geblnaoadkpiphgg.label: Identify by its company · teaching a route · under shared liability
reciprocal_geblnaoadkpiphgg.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the teaching of a route by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. reciprocal_kofilcfiegcphbel.label: as far as the old promise ran in placing of a bridge · at a distance

reciprocal_plmlfkcdikihmich.label: as far as the old promise ran in timing of a departure · at one's own cost
reciprocal_plmlfkcdikihmich.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to Paarai in 2 Samuel 23:35.

reciprocal_amjnlfciohaknche.label: count the absent into tending of a sickbed · before a witness
reciprocal_amjnlfciohaknche.meaning: To recognize a missing participant by a part of the work which otherwise has no one to perform it. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to parbar in 1 Chronicles 26:18.

reciprocal_dnojemdcpbnfjgjb.label: share left without a voice in tending of a sickbed · under divided authority
reciprocal_dnojemdcpbnfjgjb.meaning: A part included in the total for which nobody present has authority to speak. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to parbar in 1 Chronicles 26:18.

reciprocal_gamhcpanbpgjofph.label: leopard witness-piece
reciprocal_gamhcpanbpgjofph.meaning: A small piece of leopard kept to show what the material was like before it was worked or changed.

reciprocal_abcckmhhpbombpbk.label: leopard trace
reciprocal_abcckmhhpbombpbk.meaning: A quantity of leopard too small to recover as a useful portion, yet sufficient to change the material that holds it.

reciprocal_dafoalladedejgnl.label: recovered leopard
reciprocal_dafoalladedejgnl.meaning: leopard — Material of this kind recovered from an earlier use and accepted for another on the strength of what it can still do.

reciprocal_ampbpfndnljbnpei.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · taking testimony · without a common tongue

reciprocal_kofnlkcaboamnakg.label: voice of the first correction in taking of testimony · on first use
reciprocal_kofnlkcaboamnakg.meaning: A small change in a repeated account which identifies the person who first corrected it. Applies on a first attempt, while those involved still have no local precedent of their own. Allusion to parthian-acts in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, Acts 2:9.

reciprocal_nmbfiajjjjeomfnf.label: Identify by its company · reckoning a debt · after a failed trial
reciprocal_nmbfiajjjjeomfnf.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the reckoning of a debt by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. reciprocal_npcghbeebbdplkcd.label: up to the point of parting in preservation of a recipe · with a reserve
reciprocal_npcghbeebbdplkcd.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Partlet in Henry IV, Part I 00564a.

reciprocal_njbflihoofonmhka.label: Detect an omission by the count · taking testimony · without a common tongue

reciprocal_pkmkhjlilfmlmgaf.label: Counted without a hearing · taking testimony · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_pkmkhjlilfmlmgaf.meaning: A member or instance of the taking of testimony counted in a total but never called individually. It has numerical presence without an individual hearing. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Parthian in Acts 2:9.

reciprocal_ljnngdfeplpjmlei.label: unmix two accounts of selection of a witness · between generations
reciprocal_ljnngdfeplpjmlei.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Parthia in Antony and Cleopatra 00088a.

reciprocal_bpihepoebngnacli.label: so far as the hand remembers in selection of a witness · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_bpihepoebngnacli.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. reciprocal_jfcjeflohjcbnpji.label: Parthian at second hand
reciprocal_jfcjeflohjcbnpji.meaning: The substance of Parthian passed on by a hearer who can vouch for hearing it but cannot vouch for the underlying claim.

reciprocal_fcdnpkefgbmlccpi.label: practical force of Parthian
reciprocal_fcdnpkefgbmlccpi.meaning: What a hearer reasonably takes Parthian to commit the speaker to doing.

reciprocal_pgbgbpileoolbcaj.label: answerable Parthian
reciprocal_pgbgbpileoolbcaj.meaning: Parthian — An utterance of this kind given in circumstances where its speaker can be called back to clarify it. It carries a different weight from a rumour with identical words.

reciprocal_ffekhkjnmgelhnac.label: partridge sign
reciprocal_ffekhkjnmgelhnac.meaning: The presence of partridge inferred from a fresh trace, while the creature itself remains out of sight.

reciprocal_bhkjmjhgfapagmlh.label: partridge refuge
reciprocal_bhkjmjhgfapagmlh.meaning: A place the observer leaves undisturbed because partridge repeatedly returns to it for cover. One sighting alone gives no such claim.

reciprocal_nakgmpkpkfdgdido.label: site-faithful partridge
reciprocal_nakgmpkpkfdgdido.meaning: partridge — An individual of this kind whose repeated returns to one place are reliable enough for someone to recognize or await it there. The word describes one animal's habits and carries no claim that it is tame.

reciprocal_gophpiaamokkelfm.label: chosen partition
reciprocal_gophpiaamokkelfm.meaning: An instance of partition that someone deliberately undertakes and can answer for. The outward act may look the same when it happens by accident.

reciprocal_cohmicfgjnflmcii.label: trained partition
reciprocal_cohmicfgjnflmcii.meaning: An instance of partition performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_kblkkpclbjpmmbae.label: do partition on another's account
reciprocal_kblkkpclbjpmmbae.meaning: partition — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_kokicmkcjemjcfed.label: unmix two accounts of naming of a child · after consent

reciprocal_mgjkmjejmjccfanm.label: Leave someone the means to continue · settling quarrels · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_mgjkmjejmjccfanm.meaning: To give someone the means to continue with the settling of a quarrel once immediate assistance ends. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Pedro in Much Ado About Nothing 00079a.

reciprocal_odpahbfhnihlfijb.label: Learned well enough to retrace · settling quarrels · at one's own cost
reciprocal_odpahbfhnihlfijb.meaning: Said of a route, habit, or piece of knowledge of the settling of a quarrel which can be retraced independently after learning it in someone else's company. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to Pedro in Much Ado About Nothing 00079a.

reciprocal_bojpeaojdddamajm.label: Identify by its company · building bridges · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_bojpeaojdddamajm.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the placing of a bridge by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Peg-a-Ramsey in Twelfth Night 00302a.

reciprocal_pmphcnmjpkmbickm.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · building bridges · at a distance
reciprocal_pmphcnmjpkmbickm.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the placing of a bridge at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to Peg-a-Ramsey in Twelfth Night 00302a.

reciprocal_kjnngcninkembmkn.label: Stay past the handover · fitting hinges · by inherited custom
reciprocal_kjnngcninkembmkn.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the fitting of a hinge after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Pegasus in Paradise Lost, Book VII, 1–7.

reciprocal_ilinklnlpobjoflm.label: Learned well enough to retrace · recovering strays · after a disputed account
reciprocal_ilinklnlpobjoflm.meaning: Said of a route, habit, or piece of knowledge of the rescue of a stray animal which can be retraced independently after learning it in someone else's company. Used in response to an actual difference between people's accounts of what happened. Allusion to Pegasus in Paradise Lost, Book VII, 1–7.

reciprocal_bdnokceanlickmbc.label: Settle the matter by the fit · reckoning a debt · without a common tongue
reciprocal_bdnokceanlickmbc.meaning: To settle a disputed description of the reckoning of a debt by trying an actual fit or repeated use. Used when a shared word is unavailable and meaning must pass through gesture, example, or an object. Allusion to Pegasus in The Taming of the Shrew 00733a.

reciprocal_dekajhiklgninppj.label: By what the hand can actually fit · reckoning a debt · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_dekajhiklgninppj.meaning: With the tolerance that matters in the daily handling of the reckoning of a debt, even when a finer distinction exists on paper. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to Pegasus in The Taming of the Shrew 00733a.

reciprocal_gdfgkedafmapiajd.label: read the gap in naming of a child · between strangers
reciprocal_gdfgkedafmapiajd.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. reciprocal_jicljgfjioaojcad.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · choosing witnesses · by a trace
reciprocal_jicljgfjioaojcad.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the selection of a witness at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to Pegu in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XIV, 1525.3.

reciprocal_halfcdgpdccjglka.label: Identify by its company · collecting tolls · at the point of commitment

reciprocal_blngkbbdokffbjpg.label: up to the point of parting in collection of a toll · as the sole available course
reciprocal_blngkbbdokffbjpg.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Pepin in Love's Labor's Lost 00447a.

reciprocal_gkgoofokjplkokob.label: Stay past the handover · choosing witnesses · by a trace
reciprocal_gkgoofokjplkokob.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the selection of a witness after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended.
