reciprocal_appkbliiiiojcick.label: By retracing the last sure mark · naming a child · between strangers
reciprocal_appkbliiiiojcick.meaning: In a manner that retraces the naming of a child from the last point one can still positively identify. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to Petaplan in A New Voyage Round the World, Contents, 63.1.

reciprocal_jblccjfhgdnlckmh.label: Restore a neglected voice · fitting hinges · on first use
reciprocal_jblccjfhgdnlckmh.meaning: To bring a disregarded account of the fitting of a hinge into hearing without taking credit for originating it. Applies on a first attempt, while those involved still have no local precedent of their own. Allusion to Petrarch in The Prince, Chapter XXVI, 2667.

reciprocal_afibiagjciahjpek.label: By what the hand can actually fit · sharing inherited tools · at a distance
reciprocal_afibiagjciahjpek.meaning: With the tolerance that matters in the daily handling of the dividing of inherited tools, even when a finer distinction exists on paper. reciprocal_chhkgnkiacjknjij.label: Identify by its company · making a mould · out of public sight

reciprocal_gjoodkjmjakoneil.label: so far as the hand remembers in making of a mould · on first use

reciprocal_ieopbckbbipjfnbn.label: Stand by within reach · opening roads · between generations

reciprocal_gdhikjhjpmhkgdmi.label: A difficulty deliberately left to the learner · opening roads · between strangers
reciprocal_gdhikjhjpmhkgdmi.meaning: The margin of difficulty in the opening of a road a helper leaves untouched so the learner can discover their own reach. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to Petruchio in Romeo and Juliet 00516a.

reciprocal_hjkpcaldemlgjbfn.label: read the gap in timing of a departure · on first use
reciprocal_hjkpcaldemlgjbfn.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Applies on a first attempt, while those involved still have no local precedent of their own. Allusion to Petruchio in The Taming of the Shrew 00221a.

reciprocal_cfipddihfmpcgbdm.label: as far as the old promise ran in keeping of a hearth · between strangers
reciprocal_cfipddihfmpcgbdm.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to Petruchio in The Taming of the Shrew 00221a.

reciprocal_jaimignkhdiamoag.label: restore the order of preservation of a recipe · by private agreement
reciprocal_jaimignkhdiamoag.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. reciprocal_odflcaoneoklkeii.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · keeping a promise · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_odflcaoneoklkeii.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the keeping of a promise at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. reciprocal_iemcmplalegookaa.label: read the gap in handover of a key · after a disputed account

reciprocal_ljfmnkkomglfndie.label: A voice recognizable in the retelling · learning a dance · before a witness

reciprocal_jnmjghljapnfebnp.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · telling a voyage · without a common tongue
reciprocal_jnmjghljapnfebnp.meaning: To give a judgment about the telling of a voyage temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. reciprocal_peincjbdgkcmhfej.label: Learned well enough to retrace · telling a voyage · out of public sight
reciprocal_peincjbdgkcmhfej.meaning: Said of a route, habit, or piece of knowledge of the telling of a voyage which can be retraced independently after learning it in someone else's company. reciprocal_jkpfmnglnfcoacfi.label: by the point of last agreement in sealing of a letter · in the wrong season

reciprocal_bhaigpakadpcldol.label: Locate between known limits · changing the night watch · under shared liability

reciprocal_ailpmpgfmklbeici.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · changing the night watch · between generations

reciprocal_jfnjckklfcihgplm.label: A difficulty deliberately left to the learner · marking seasons · with a right to withdraw

reciprocal_gfedbahiciijlngk.label: count the absent into return of a borrowed thing · at the point of commitment

reciprocal_mdmbmhppjjcfklin.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · dividing a household · after a disputed account

reciprocal_anlabkjhanginkog.label: Trace through successive hands · collecting tolls · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_anlabkjhanginkog.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the collection of a toll by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. reciprocal_ljlpphloidlcaepc.label: Learned down one branch · dividing a household · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_ljlpphloidlcaepc.meaning: Said of knowledge of the division of a household that is exact on one line of descent or transmission while adjacent lines remain undocumented. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Pethahiah in Nehemiah 11:24.

reciprocal_efmaoheihbgpjjbg.label: trace the hand behind settling of a quarrel · in company with a novice
reciprocal_efmaoheihbgpjjbg.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to Pethor in Deuteronomy 23:4.

reciprocal_kcflhgjipibbjmmo.label: Learned down one branch · naming a child · after consent
reciprocal_kcflhgjipibbjmmo.meaning: Said of knowledge of the naming of a child that is exact on one line of descent or transmission while adjacent lines remain undocumented. reciprocal_ojhlpdkiemcoenkh.label: distinguish an inherited fault in keeping of a child's confidence · out of public sight

reciprocal_dcnngnjfmnpbphln.label: as far as the old promise ran in selection of a witness · under divided authority

reciprocal_fmncoolihgobhfdl.label: child by practice
reciprocal_fmncoolihgobhfdl.meaning: Someone recognized as child by the work they repeatedly perform before anyone grants a title.

reciprocal_fidmgceohdbibdpm.label: acting descendant
reciprocal_fidmgceohdbibdpm.meaning: Someone who carries the obligations of descendant for an absence with a definite end.

reciprocal_edofbdbkdlibgpmo.label: trusted working child
reciprocal_edofbdbkdlibgpmo.meaning: child — Someone in this role to whom a community actually brings the difficult cases. Title or seniority alone does not confer the distinction.

reciprocal_lmpdfbjaodjpbnmk.label: inward The child who holds the roof

reciprocal_debdgkdodhijchnd.label: the second occasion for To hear the dough rise

reciprocal_gpjnhkmmmebgbcke.label: leaven by a chosen course
reciprocal_gpjnhkmmmebgbcke.meaning: The part of a movement described by leaven that can be steered; drift or recoil may account for the rest.

reciprocal_cmlphccnbjpjbojj.label: leaven under momentum
reciprocal_cmlphccnbjpjbojj.meaning: Movement of the kind described by leaven that continues after the initiating effort has stopped.

reciprocal_dbgaljcccekimchp.label: chosen knead

reciprocal_jcjdfjiagakckfgg.label: trained knead

reciprocal_omifbelkhpcjkhbm.label: do knead on another's account

reciprocal_dpelkgcfkgcbekam.label: kneading-trough sign

reciprocal_ddfnohbikmpiohcb.label: acting tutor
reciprocal_ddfnohbikmpiohcb.meaning: Someone who carries the obligations of tutor for an absence with a definite end.

reciprocal_bgphlclgnlidkfdc.label: trusted working tutor
reciprocal_bgphlclgnlidkfdc.meaning: tutor — Someone in this role to whom a community actually brings the difficult cases. Title or seniority alone does not confer the distinction.

reciprocal_jmaggeminfppmlac.label: distinguish an inherited fault in selection of a witness · on first use
reciprocal_jmaggeminfppmlac.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. reciprocal_johimjmblopimggi.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to pelaliah-neh-adaiah-line in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.283, Nehemiah 11:12.

reciprocal_jnoioaklaohcfffi.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. reciprocal_bpdndgdlcpolpbkd.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to Piero Buonaccorsi in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3083.

reciprocal_npleebnfahpbcipb.label: Transmit beyond the written record · naming a child · after a handover
reciprocal_npleebnfahpbcipb.meaning: To transmit a practice of the naming of a child beyond the last person or occasion named in its written record. The practice may continue on different terms. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to Pieve in The Prince, Duke Valentino, 2857.

reciprocal_ejbanopedddieinl.label: up to the point of parting in telling of a voyage · at the second attempt
reciprocal_ejbanopedddieinl.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Pieve in The Prince, Duke Valentino, 2857.

reciprocal_fmfllgdmlddhncpc.label: Stand by within reach · choosing witnesses · in the wrong season
reciprocal_fmfllgdmlddhncpc.meaning: To remain close enough to help with the selection of a witness while leaving the person concerned free to finish the act. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Piombino in The Prince, Chapter VII, 727.

reciprocal_knimllfjkooalcgf.label: A difficulty deliberately left to the learner · choosing witnesses · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_knimllfjkooalcgf.meaning: The margin of difficulty in the selection of a witness a helper leaves untouched so the learner can discover their own reach. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to Piombino in The Prince, Chapter VII, 727.

reciprocal_lafbjneahgmabocd.label: Locate between known limits · drawing charts · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_lafbjneahgmabocd.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the drawing of a chart by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Piñas in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VII, 765.4.

reciprocal_maopngmmgcjgbblk.label: By retracing the last sure mark · drawing charts · pending a challenge
reciprocal_maopngmmgcjgbblk.meaning: In a manner that retraces the drawing of a chart from the last point one can still positively identify. Names a provisional arrangement that stands until someone brings a specific objection. Allusion to Piñas in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VII, 765.4.

reciprocal_bielnofengcbgkad.label: recover the old edge of laying out of a boundary · with a reserve
reciprocal_bielnofengcbgkad.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Pisco in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VII, 655.6.

reciprocal_ccdlkfjlpmbpgcca.label: By retracing the last sure mark · telling a voyage · after loss of the original
reciprocal_ccdlkfjlpmbpgcca.meaning: In a manner that retraces the telling of a voyage from the last point one can still positively identify. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to Pisco in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VII, 655.6.

reciprocal_cnpilfchbefbakmk.label: reach of it
reciprocal_cnpilfchbefbakmk.meaning: The stretch of speech to which it applies in a particular utterance. Moving the boundary can change who or what is included.

reciprocal_gmfaefdaiojcigad.label: echoed it
reciprocal_gmfaefdaiojcigad.meaning: An occurrence of it taken over from another speaker whose framing the present speaker need not endorse.

reciprocal_mjfhjhenhfdbgdii.label: it carried over
reciprocal_mjfhjhenhfdbgdii.meaning: it — An occurrence of this grammatical form whose interpretation depends on a preceding speaker's wording. Taken alone, it leaves a question of scope or reference open.

reciprocal_bnadgdccidlhcjia.label: Count it in blisters as a deed
reciprocal_bnadgdccidlhcjia.meaning: The act or lived situation pictured by the idiom “Count it in blisters”, recognized in a particular case before anyone gives it a name.
reciprocal_bnadgdccidlhcjia.origin: productive contrast from po ni shalemniragumun taren’en

reciprocal_jeckehailacnnonj.label: Count it in blisters turned towards someone
reciprocal_jeckehailacnnonj.meaning: A pointed use of “Count it in blisters” as an intervention in another person's situation. The addressee can accept or resist that reading.
reciprocal_jeckehailacnnonj.origin: productive contrast from po ni shalemniragumun taren’en

reciprocal_pfalbkgnbmohpipm.label: the second occasion for Count it in blisters
reciprocal_pfalbkgnbmohpipm.meaning: Count it in blisters — A recurrence of the situation pictured in this idiom that those involved recognize in time to respond differently.
reciprocal_pfalbkgnbmohpipm.origin: narrower alternative from po ni shalemniragumun taren’en

reciprocal_hfgneibkbfmieakc.label: bracket the uncertainty in division of a household · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_hfgneibkbfmieakc.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Poggio in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3101.

reciprocal_fgildipdnhjbbhho.label: by the point of last agreement in division of a household · against the tally
reciprocal_fgildipdnhjbbhho.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to Poggio in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3101.

reciprocal_ecodpgdieihkepif.label: first stir of pox
reciprocal_ecodpgdieihkepif.meaning: The earliest observable part of pox, identifiable before its full course can be known.

reciprocal_hhgdbldafdclgkba.label: wake of pox
reciprocal_hhgdbldafdclgkba.meaning: The changes left behind by pox after the event itself has come to an end.

reciprocal_cnkpkcbhmcfiklea.label: witnessed pox
reciprocal_cnkpkcbhmcfiklea.meaning: pox — An occurrence of this kind someone can date or place from their own presence. The word marks what that witness can vouch for.

reciprocal_jeogbknaamgbgdke.label: first stir of smallpox
reciprocal_jeogbknaamgbgdke.meaning: The earliest observable part of smallpox, identifiable before its full course can be known.

reciprocal_pbjipgicnbgkblpo.label: wake of smallpox
reciprocal_pbjipgicnbgkblpo.meaning: The changes left behind by smallpox after the event itself has come to an end.

reciprocal_pgafmcgldlbnhpkj.label: witnessed smallpox
reciprocal_pgafmcgldlbnhpkj.meaning: smallpox — An occurrence of this kind someone can date or place from their own presence. The word marks what that witness can vouch for.

reciprocal_ohelkpgkibnpcggb.label: read the gap in naming of a child · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_ohelkpgkibnpcggb.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Porcius-Festus in Acts 24:27.

reciprocal_hcbfbghjgaddacpm.label: as far as the old promise ran in selection of a witness · against the tally
reciprocal_hcbfbghjgaddacpm.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to Porcius-Festus in Acts 24:27.

reciprocal_mndipijoimljilmn.label: boar sign
reciprocal_mndipijoimljilmn.meaning: The presence of boar inferred from a fresh trace, while the creature itself remains out of sight.

reciprocal_fakapjfcbobcocbk.label: boar refuge
reciprocal_fakapjfcbobcocbk.meaning: A place the observer leaves undisturbed because boar repeatedly returns to it for cover. One sighting alone gives no such claim.

reciprocal_ijkakaiedbbpfkag.label: site-faithful boar
reciprocal_ijkakaiedbbpfkag.meaning: boar — An individual of this kind whose repeated returns to one place are reliable enough for someone to recognize or await it there. The word describes one animal's habits and carries no claim that it is tame.

reciprocal_pkacgbiolamobbgo.label: tusk witness-piece
reciprocal_pkacgbiolamobbgo.meaning: A small piece of tusk kept to show what the material was like before it was worked or changed.

reciprocal_mekeiogckfcnnege.label: tusk trace
reciprocal_mekeiogckfcnnege.meaning: A quantity of tusk too small to recover as a useful portion, yet sufficient to change the material that holds it.

reciprocal_fdejfihbpkjpcamc.label: recovered tusk
reciprocal_fdejfihbpkjpcamc.meaning: tusk — Material of this kind recovered from an earlier use and accepted for another on the strength of what it can still do.

reciprocal_dedlefedpcckolek.label: elephant at second hand
reciprocal_dedlefedpcckolek.meaning: The substance of elephant passed on by a hearer who can vouch for hearing it but cannot vouch for the underlying claim.

reciprocal_jobolcojkginkicj.label: practical force of elephant
reciprocal_jobolcojkginkicj.meaning: What a hearer reasonably takes elephant to commit the speaker to doing.

reciprocal_iaegahfogbngagfa.label: answerable elephant
reciprocal_iaegahfogbngagfa.meaning: elephant — An utterance of this kind given in circumstances where its speaker can be called back to clarify it. It carries a different weight from a rumour with identical words.

reciprocal_hcnlbhijjogipfag.label: snout sign
reciprocal_hcnlbhijjogipfag.meaning: The presence of snout inferred from a fresh trace, while the creature itself remains out of sight.

reciprocal_mbehmjpnhipfdjgh.label: snout refuge
reciprocal_mbehmjpnhipfdjgh.meaning: A place the observer leaves undisturbed because snout repeatedly returns to it for cover. One sighting alone gives no such claim.

reciprocal_hignapdncbjklhfd.label: site-faithful snout
reciprocal_hignapdncbjklhfd.meaning: snout — An individual of this kind whose repeated returns to one place are reliable enough for someone to recognize or await it there. The word describes one animal's habits and carries no claim that it is tame.

reciprocal_cfopokookjgldmof.label: distinguish an inherited fault in counting of sleepers · after loss of the original
reciprocal_cfopokookjgldmof.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to poratha in Esther 9:8.

reciprocal_egjmehmfpbcgamid.label: Counted without a hearing · naming a child · at the second attempt
reciprocal_egjmehmfpbcgamid.meaning: A member or instance of the naming of a child counted in a total but never called individually. It has numerical presence without an individual hearing. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to poratha in Esther 9:8.

reciprocal_hgmanhgbdmilegkd.label: restore the order of telling of a voyage · by inherited custom
reciprocal_hgmanhgbdmilegkd.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Port-Royal in A New Voyage Round the World, Introduction, 99.4.

reciprocal_jghommjamddlfeoa.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · telling a voyage · between generations
reciprocal_jghommjamddlfeoa.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the telling of a voyage at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Port-Royal in A New Voyage Round the World, Introduction, 99.4.

reciprocal_knphbmgnaaedafme.label: recover the old edge of drawing of a chart · after loss of the original
reciprocal_knphbmgnaaedafme.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to Porta-Nova in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XIV, 1487.2.

reciprocal_hioikhaclljonfbe.label: learned well enough to reverse in drawing of a chart · pending a challenge
reciprocal_hioikhaclljonfbe.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. Names a provisional arrangement that stands until someone brings a specific objection. Allusion to Porta-Nova in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XIV, 1487.2.

reciprocal_njloceddkmcdcgem.label: recover the old edge of drawing of a chart · at a distance
reciprocal_njloceddkmcdcgem.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to Portsmouth in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XX, 2175.5.

reciprocal_fbjmgmfcailhmkni.label: learned well enough to reverse in drawing of a chart · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_fbjmgmfcailhmkni.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Portsmouth in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XX, 2175.5.

reciprocal_ghijdglbddolmkff.label: Underwrite another's risk · naming a child · as the sole available course
reciprocal_ghijdglbddolmkff.meaning: To undertake a cost personally if the proposed arrangement for the naming of a child fails, whether or not the result can be predicted. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Portia in The Merchant of Venice 00349a.

reciprocal_nkmephjfbmoolkeh.label: Backed by an identifiable bearer of loss · dividing a household · under shared liability
reciprocal_nkmephjfbmoolkeh.meaning: Said of an assurance about the division of a household whose hearer can identify who will actually bear a loss. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to Portia in The Merchant of Venice 00349a.

reciprocal_kabelpjekhdojomf.label: recognize intimation
reciprocal_kabelpjekhdojomf.meaning: A first grasp of recognize sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_ecdfimddnikinmpd.label: recognize put to use
reciprocal_ecdfimddnikinmpd.meaning: An understanding of recognize that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_hkolhickfofpohhn.label: recognize held on trial
reciprocal_hkolhickfofpohhn.meaning: recognize — A thought or belief of this kind deliberately entertained until a particular question can decide whether to keep it. The speaker owns the test as well as the idea.

reciprocal_elcbjlidbdnomhcm.label: Settle the matter by the fit · setting prices · at the second attempt
reciprocal_elcbjlidbdnomhcm.meaning: To settle a disputed description of the setting of a price by trying an actual fit or repeated use. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Porto Rico in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VIII, 875.9.

reciprocal_ijfmapgiaekimnce.label: By retracing the last sure mark · setting prices · in company with a novice
reciprocal_ijfmapgiaekimnce.meaning: In a manner that retraces the setting of a price from the last point one can still positively identify. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to Porto Rico in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VIII, 875.9.

reciprocal_plgkddkflcajcjne.label: stay to see telling of a voyage take hold · after a failed trial
reciprocal_plgkddkflcajcjne.meaning: To accompany a person far enough beyond a handover to see whether they can actually continue alone. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to Portobel in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VII, 731.7.

reciprocal_cfamiofdahcjkoef.label: Learned well enough to retrace · telling a voyage · as the sole available course
reciprocal_cfamiofdahcjkoef.meaning: Said of a route, habit, or piece of knowledge of the telling of a voyage which can be retraced independently after learning it in someone else's company. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Portobel in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VII, 731.7.

reciprocal_eibgpmhakcbabeof.label: bracket the uncertainty in placing of a mooring · after a handover
reciprocal_eibgpmhakcbabeof.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to Portugal in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XIV, 1485.3.

reciprocal_kihgonmlefkcbiaj.label: By what the hand can actually fit · placing a mooring · for another's benefit
reciprocal_kihgonmlefkcbiaj.meaning: With the tolerance that matters in the daily handling of the placing of a mooring, even when a finer distinction exists on paper. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Portugal in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XIV, 1485.3.

reciprocal_iiagpafenbmjjbcj.label: charneco intimation
reciprocal_iiagpafenbmjjbcj.meaning: A first grasp of charneco sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_hpgbfoafdghjolfo.label: charneco put to use
reciprocal_hpgbfoafdghjolfo.meaning: An understanding of charneco that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_kafejapkpgopglcc.label: charneco held on trial
reciprocal_kafejapkpgopglcc.meaning: charneco — A thought or belief of this kind deliberately entertained until a particular question can decide whether to keep it. The speaker owns the test as well as the idea.

reciprocal_mjflmnjbccanejop.label: Portuguese by declaration
reciprocal_mjflmnjbccanejop.meaning: The status expressed by “Portuguese” when it rests on a person's own declaration. The hearer must still ask what practices, ties, or duties the speaker includes.

reciprocal_ndijfnligkmocjfi.label: Portuguese in practice
reciprocal_ndijfnligkmocjfi.meaning: The practical ties or obligations through which the term “Portuguese” matters to the people involved. A label alone gives no measure of them.

reciprocal_godmoenmkpcpninn.label: Portuguese by sustained participation
reciprocal_godmoenmkpcpninn.meaning: Portuguese — Bearing the relation in question through continuing participation, as distinct from an isolated appearance or a one-time claim.

reciprocal_njcjlfjbijcoicek.label: hog by practice
reciprocal_njcjlfjbijcoicek.meaning: Someone recognized as hog by the work they repeatedly perform before anyone grants a title.

reciprocal_mjlnofbpgepnbikn.label: acting hog
reciprocal_mjlnofbpgepnbikn.meaning: Someone who carries the obligations of hog for an absence with a definite end.

reciprocal_cccfcokpfiemomei.label: trusted working hog
reciprocal_cccfcokpfiemomei.meaning: hog — Someone in this role to whom a community actually brings the difficult cases. Title or seniority alone does not confer the distinction.

reciprocal_dmekmkjpjkcjnkcc.label: hogshead hand-wear
reciprocal_dmekmkjpjkcjnkcc.meaning: The polish or hollow left by repeated handling of hogshead, valued as evidence of who used it or how.

reciprocal_hpepcdmmlnllbhed.label: hogshead stand-in
reciprocal_hpepcdmmlnllbhed.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of hogshead during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_klmfihcdpcapmkok.label: hogshead kept in service
reciprocal_klmfihcdpcapmkok.meaning: hogshead — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_pfnfmeniihigicpg.label: pork courtesy-portion
reciprocal_pfnfmeniihigicpg.meaning: A share of pork held back for someone who has yet to arrive, even when everyone at table could eat more.

reciprocal_pegfcjecamlgijlo.label: pork lingering taste
reciprocal_pegfcjecamlgijlo.meaning: The taste by which pork can still be recognized after it has been swallowed or taken away.

reciprocal_kkocbcmmdbfnngfl.label: household-owed pork
reciprocal_kkocbcmmdbfnngfl.meaning: pork — Food of this kind already owed to someone at the table before it is served. Offering it to a guest would spend another person's welcome.

reciprocal_apkaemcfodampjak.label: its-roar intimation
reciprocal_apkaemcfodampjak.meaning: A first grasp of its-roar sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_oplgkjchpagdfaco.label: its-roar put to use
reciprocal_oplgkjchpagdfaco.meaning: An understanding of its-roar that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_kpndheoapmapkbbk.label: its-roar held on trial
reciprocal_kpndheoapmapkbbk.meaning: its-roar — A thought or belief of this kind deliberately entertained until a particular question can decide whether to keep it. The speaker owns the test as well as the idea.

reciprocal_haamfmdjdkoheebm.label: read the gap in drying of a harvest · without a common tongue
reciprocal_haamfmdjdkoheebm.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Used when a shared word is unavailable and meaning must pass through gesture, example, or an object. Allusion to pop’rin in Romeo and Juliet 00269a.

reciprocal_dhogelcbkmolimhh.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · drying grain · at a distance
reciprocal_dhogelcbkmolimhh.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the drying of a harvest at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to pop’rin in Romeo and Juliet 00269a.

reciprocal_bdnlojkenncmcbgj.label: poplar season-sign
reciprocal_bdnlojkenncmcbgj.meaning: The stage of poplar that local people watch to tell when other seasonal work can begin.

reciprocal_bdeamfmngnbdonim.label: poplar reserve-stock
reciprocal_bdeamfmngnbdonim.meaning: A living part of poplar set aside so that next season's stock survives the present harvest.

reciprocal_fkfebcjjndaoeioe.label: volunteer poplar
reciprocal_fkfebcjjndaoeioe.meaning: poplar — A plant of this kind that establishes itself where nobody in the present season planted it. Said when its appearance matters as evidence of earlier growth.

reciprocal_illfbbkmbbjfjcgd.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · keeping a child’s confidence · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_illfbbkmbbjfjcgd.meaning: To give a judgment about the keeping of a child's confidence temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Popilius in Julius Caesar 00323a.

reciprocal_eandndjpillnihnm.label: duty that survives the key in keeping of a child's confidence · in company with a novice
reciprocal_eandndjpillnihnm.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to Popilius in Julius Caesar 00323a.

reciprocal_codlbdgglkpcibgn.label: Identify by its company · choosing witnesses · after consent
reciprocal_codlbdgglkpcibgn.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the selection of a witness by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to Poppius in The Sceptical Chymist, Part VI, 532.4.

reciprocal_lmimdgaeghbegbjh.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · choosing witnesses · under divided authority
reciprocal_lmimdgaeghbegbjh.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the selection of a witness at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Poppius in The Sceptical Chymist, Part VI, 532.4.

reciprocal_hdfphokieaapdbia.label: pot hand-wear
reciprocal_hdfphokieaapdbia.meaning: The polish or hollow left by repeated handling of pot, valued as evidence of who used it or how.

reciprocal_fielmdldioklkjig.label: pot stand-in
reciprocal_fielmdldioklkjig.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of pot during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_aagganclopalfiid.label: pot kept in service
reciprocal_aagganclopalfiid.meaning: pot — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_phihccbfihlfooji.label: pot-range intimation
reciprocal_phihccbfihlfooji.meaning: A first grasp of pot-range sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_fcfefliedfdconjf.label: pot-range put to use
reciprocal_fcfefliedfdconjf.meaning: An understanding of pot-range that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_pngmbempehlncknf.label: pot-range held on trial
reciprocal_pngmbempehlncknf.meaning: pot-range — A thought or belief of this kind deliberately entertained until a particular question can decide whether to keep it. The speaker owns the test as well as the idea.

reciprocal_adcgkkodocpdlkod.label: potsherd hand-wear
reciprocal_adcgkkodocpdlkod.meaning: The polish or hollow left by repeated handling of potsherd, valued as evidence of who used it or how.

reciprocal_fcjhecfdgpaoiici.label: potsherd stand-in
reciprocal_fcjhecfdgpaoiici.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of potsherd during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_fmbpojbmkhbfoocd.label: potsherd kept in service
reciprocal_fmbpojbmkhbfoocd.meaning: potsherd — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_bkimapooicaelobl.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · telling a voyage · under divided authority
reciprocal_bkimapooicaelobl.meaning: To give a judgment about the telling of a voyage temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Potiphar in Genesis 37:36.

reciprocal_jiboafahaacpjlej.label: duty that survives the key in telling of a voyage · after a failed trial
reciprocal_jiboafahaacpjlej.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to Potiphar in Genesis 37:36.

reciprocal_gfcbbjaomhkdmeoh.label: trace the hand behind taking of testimony · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_gfcbbjaomhkdmeoh.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Potipherah in Genesis 46:20.

reciprocal_ihgoljgcjdgidbig.label: duty that survives the key in taking of testimony · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_ihgoljgcjdgidbig.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to Potipherah in Genesis 46:20.

reciprocal_bangabmfnlfklajl.label: recover the old edge of teaching of a route · in the wrong season
reciprocal_bangabmfnlfklajl.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. reciprocal_apccmjdllnkfojhc.label: by the point of last agreement in telling of a voyage · as a rehearsal

reciprocal_cnbjjpmhkljjdglb.label: Learned well enough to retrace · handing over a key · after loss of the original

reciprocal_lhopkapchcjmappo.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · collecting tolls · after a handover

reciprocal_mhcnabemghdlekeo.label: Stay past the handover · dividing a household · at the second attempt

reciprocal_lfppemjcbofocknc.label: Learned well enough to retrace · dividing a household · by a trace

reciprocal_gcbmonohjobknfkj.label: Trace through successive hands · collecting tolls · for another's benefit

reciprocal_fpigbkcadbeemjfc.label: exact at the fork of collection of a toll · against the tally

reciprocal_ckbkholgmlmginam.meaning: A first grasp of coranto-dance sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_oechkeidnlebkoff.label: coranto-dance put to use
reciprocal_oechkeidnlebkoff.meaning: An understanding of coranto-dance that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_cepdbpkdkajkcjhj.label: coranto-dance held on trial
reciprocal_cepdbpkdkajkcjhj.meaning: coranto-dance — A thought or belief of this kind deliberately entertained until a particular question can decide whether to keep it. The speaker owns the test as well as the idea.

reciprocal_ngddemgnofidccpm.label: frisk by a chosen course
reciprocal_ngddemgnofidccpm.meaning: The part of a movement described by frisk that can be steered; drift or recoil may account for the rest.

reciprocal_oileahdikmefpbpg.label: frisk under momentum
reciprocal_oileahdikmefpbpg.meaning: Movement of the kind described by frisk that continues after the initiating effort has stopped.

reciprocal_homjmlkmfmcihhll.label: guide a movement of frisk
reciprocal_homjmlkmfmcihhll.meaning: frisk — To make the movement in question while continually correcting the course from what one sees or feels along the way.

reciprocal_ejfjcpapmaadhbng.label: trace the hand behind telling of a voyage · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_ejfjcpapmaadhbng.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to Talmai in Joshua 15:14.

reciprocal_nbdlbonpflblejoe.label: taught within one line of division of a household · after a failed trial
reciprocal_nbdlbonpflblejoe.meaning: Said of a skill transmitted within one line of teachers. Outsiders may perform the same work by a recognizably different sequence. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to Talmai in Joshua 15:14.

reciprocal_aihnmfakjfpgjmpk.label: Detect an omission by the count · dividing a household · before a witness
reciprocal_aihnmfakjfpgjmpk.meaning: To detect a gap in the division of a household because the count or pattern expects another occurrence before it can close. There need be no surviving mark in the missing place. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Talmon in Nehemiah 11:19.

reciprocal_locmenncoinpbkoe.label: share left without a voice in division of a household · at the second attempt
reciprocal_locmenncoinpbkoe.meaning: A part included in the total for which nobody present has authority to speak. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Talmon in Nehemiah 11:19.

reciprocal_ecblcobjkddnnkno.label: reach of Talitha
reciprocal_ecblcobjkddnnkno.meaning: The stretch of speech to which Talitha applies in a particular utterance. Moving the boundary can change who or what is included.

reciprocal_lglbepmifhaclldb.label: echoed Talitha
reciprocal_lglbepmifhaclldb.meaning: An occurrence of Talitha taken over from another speaker whose framing the present speaker need not endorse.

reciprocal_jgjmpgkjaonkdnnf.label: Talitha carried over
reciprocal_jgjmpgkjaonkdnnf.meaning: Talitha — An occurrence of this grammatical form whose interpretation depends on a preceding speaker's wording. Taken alone, it leaves a question of scope or reference open.

reciprocal_hhokbbbhiloegikl.label: grasshopper sign
reciprocal_hhokbbbhiloegikl.meaning: The presence of grasshopper inferred from a fresh trace, while the creature itself remains out of sight.

reciprocal_afmilkjbkkonibfo.label: grasshopper refuge
reciprocal_afmilkjbkkonibfo.meaning: A place the observer leaves undisturbed because grasshopper repeatedly returns to it for cover. One sighting alone gives no such claim.

reciprocal_napdledcbpjoegkb.label: site-faithful grasshopper
reciprocal_napdledcbpjoegkb.meaning: grasshopper — An individual of this kind whose repeated returns to one place are reliable enough for someone to recognize or await it there. The word describes one animal's habits and carries no claim that it is tame.

reciprocal_kbhmjmgbbcgcnipg.label: stay to see division of a household take hold · in company with a novice
reciprocal_kbhmjmgbbcgcnipg.meaning: To accompany a person far enough beyond a handover to see whether they can actually continue alone. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to tamah in Nehemiah 7:55.

reciprocal_ejgmjghdkfipkpdd.label: Learned well enough to retrace · dividing a household · for another's benefit
reciprocal_ejgmjghdkfipkpdd.meaning: Said of a route, habit, or piece of knowledge of the division of a household which can be retraced independently after learning it in someone else's company. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to tamah in Nehemiah 7:55.

reciprocal_ppjfkmfidpeeklfp.label: read the gap in telling of a voyage · against the tally
reciprocal_ppjfkmfidpeeklfp.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to Tamar in Genesis 38:6.

reciprocal_kfpolhimenoccofb.label: as far as the old promise ran in telling of a voyage · between strangers
reciprocal_kfpolhimenoccofb.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to Tamar in Genesis 38:6.

reciprocal_lmialgaopdbkbkjn.label: Stay past the handover · changing the night watch · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_lmialgaopdbkbkjn.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the relief of a night watch after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to tamarind in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XIX, 2077.1.

reciprocal_deigalcdijndfocl.label: duty that survives the key in relief of a night watch · after a disputed account
reciprocal_deigalcdijndfocl.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Used in response to an actual difference between people's accounts of what happened. Allusion to tamarind in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XIX, 2077.1.

reciprocal_kmhknhhldgcofhgg.label: read the gap in learning of a dance · after loss of the original
reciprocal_kmhknhhldgcofhgg.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to tammuz in Paradise Lost, Book I, 451–454.

reciprocal_apefnfkhplhngmpk.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · learning a dance · pending a challenge
reciprocal_apefnfkhplhngmpk.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the learning of a dance at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Names a provisional arrangement that stands until someone brings a specific objection. Allusion to tammuz in Paradise Lost, Book I, 451–454.

reciprocal_mihdaebnhkdodmgm.label: restore the order of care of a grave · at a distance
reciprocal_mihdaebnhkdodmgm.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to Tamyris in Henry VI, Part 1 00212a.

reciprocal_kiclkemhbajpgpie.label: voice of the first correction in rehearsal of a song · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_kiclkemhbajpgpie.meaning: A small change in a repeated account which identifies the person who first corrected it. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Thamyris in Paradise Lost, Book III, 33–36.

reciprocal_japllgafjklbkdba.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · keeping a child’s confidence · by private agreement
reciprocal_japllgafjklbkdba.meaning: To give a judgment about the keeping of a child's confidence temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Tamora in Titus Andronicus 00536a.

reciprocal_hjepdegcjillphcb.label: A difficulty deliberately left to the learner · keeping a child’s confidence · with a reserve
reciprocal_hjepdegcjillphcb.meaning: The margin of difficulty in the keeping of a child's confidence a helper leaves untouched so the learner can discover their own reach. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Tamora in Titus Andronicus 00536a.

reciprocal_gpfjpjoccenmding.label: restore the order of carrying of a burden · against the tally
reciprocal_gpfjpjoccenmding.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. reciprocal_jimfhfipiodhjicg.label: so far as the hand remembers in carrying of a burden · without a common tongue
reciprocal_jimfhfipiodhjicg.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Used when a shared word is unavailable and meaning must pass through gesture, example, or an object. Allusion to Tamworth in Richard III 01078b.

reciprocal_pihkgihcpopemklo.label: Locate between known limits · telling a voyage · before a witness
reciprocal_pihkgihcpopemklo.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the telling of a voyage by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Tanach in Joshua 21:25.

reciprocal_clifhihjcppmlmjk.label: share left without a voice in laying out of a boundary · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_clifhihjcppmlmjk.meaning: A part included in the total for which nobody present has authority to speak. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to Tanach in Joshua 21:25.

reciprocal_caggkhjglcoakbpp.label: distinguish an inherited fault in repair of a roof · by a trace
reciprocal_caggkhjglcoakbpp.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to tanhumeth in Jeremiah 40:8.

reciprocal_eacbkhebhnlmdiag.label: exact at the fork of division of a household · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_eacbkhebhnlmdiag.meaning: Said of knowledge that can distinguish two lines at the moment they parted, even if their subsequent history is obscure. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to tanhumeth in Jeremiah 40:8.

reciprocal_hmmockcecdmjfhdm.label: bracket the uncertainty in landing of a boat · after a disputed account
reciprocal_hmmockcecdmjfhdm.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. reciprocal_chboellnpngamdja.label: Learned well enough to retrace · placing a mooring · by private agreement
reciprocal_chboellnpngamdja.meaning: Said of a route, habit, or piece of knowledge of the placing of a mooring which can be retraced independently after learning it in someone else's company. reciprocal_idbeganokgkbjobb.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · making a mould · in company with a novice

reciprocal_idnljjefaokmbomc.label: tache put to use

reciprocal_ghgbkkhmlnbceccb.label: as far as the old promise ran in counting of sleepers · after consent

reciprocal_enkbeifdgfdpmnjo.label: unmix two accounts of keeping of a ferry · between generations

reciprocal_pdilecjbehjlnpio.label: up to the point of parting in setting of a price · on independent confirmation

reciprocal_iolgncjcehfmgphg.label: Stand by within reach · tending a sickbed · under divided authority

reciprocal_lebbhpodlabogiae.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · tending a sickbed · against the tally

reciprocal_emlkcghhimhgnbfc.label: restore the order of learning of a dance · at one's own cost

reciprocal_ffimbcefjhppfkii.label: up to the point of parting in learning of a dance · at one's own cost

reciprocal_mjgndnlfplienfak.label: Leave someone the means to continue · naming a child · at the second attempt
reciprocal_mjgndnlfplienfak.meaning: To give someone the means to continue with the naming of a child once immediate assistance ends. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Timnite in Judges 15:6.

reciprocal_poomhjmhnnlmkion.label: A difficulty deliberately left to the learner · naming a child · under divided authority
reciprocal_poomhjmhnnlmkion.meaning: The margin of difficulty in the naming of a child a helper leaves untouched so the learner can discover their own reach. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Timnite in Judges 15:6.

reciprocal_mfllfhdpooofafhe.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · telling a voyage · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_mfllfhdpooofafhe.meaning: To give a judgment about the telling of a voyage temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Timnite in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, Judges 15:6.

reciprocal_hpdeeignkgecgglk.label: voice of the first correction in naming of a child · at one's own cost
reciprocal_hpdeeignkgecgglk.meaning: A small change in a repeated account which identifies the person who first corrected it. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to Timnite in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, Judges 15:6.

reciprocal_mhiehnidbbhaekmd.label: Locate between known limits · placing a mooring · under divided authority
reciprocal_mhiehnidbbhaekmd.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the placing of a mooring by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Timor in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XVI, 1807.6.

reciprocal_cfdfoemhpfcjeebi.label: By retracing the last sure mark · placing a mooring · after consent
reciprocal_cfdfoemhpfcjeebi.meaning: In a manner that retraces the placing of a mooring from the last point one can still positively identify. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to Timor in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XVI, 1807.6.

reciprocal_cpmjkjmhidnijnkl.label: trace the hand behind keeping of a child's confidence · for another's benefit
reciprocal_cpmjkjmhidnijnkl.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Timotheus in Colossians 1:1.

reciprocal_kakmfnkeaajjflmk.label: exact at the fork of keeping of a child's confidence · under divided authority
reciprocal_kakmfnkeaajjflmk.meaning: Said of knowledge that can distinguish two lines at the moment they parted, even if their subsequent history is obscure. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Timotheus in Colossians 1:1.

reciprocal_bghhcenpolhdbcbn.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · sharing inherited tools · by a trace
reciprocal_bghhcenpolhdbcbn.meaning: To give a judgment about the dividing of inherited tools temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to Timothy in Philemon 1:1.

reciprocal_jpjkjpekfkjphjnh.label: duty that survives the key in dividing of inherited tools · between strangers
reciprocal_jpjkjpekfkjphjnh.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to Timothy in Philemon 1:1.

reciprocal_hkhcnkilcjphjanc.label: Leave someone the means to continue · sealing a letter · in company with a novice
reciprocal_hkhcnkilcjphjanc.meaning: To give someone the means to continue with the sealing of a letter once immediate assistance ends. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to 1 Timothy in Two Treatises of Government, Second Treatise, Chapter V, 650.3.

reciprocal_edibkdbkfpmcfaid.label: as far as the old promise ran in handover of a key · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_edibkdbkfpmcfaid.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Timothy in Leviathan, Chapter 36, Hobbes_0161_940-margin-2.1.

reciprocal_iinopjjemclohjcc.label: unmix two accounts of naming of a child · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_iinopjjemclohjcc.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to Timon in Acts 6:5.

reciprocal_ccfhchlbcgkdpcpl.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · naming a child · as the sole available course
reciprocal_ccfhchlbcgkdpcpl.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the naming of a child at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Timon in Acts 6:5.

reciprocal_gendahhblfdcddaf.label: drop by a chosen course
reciprocal_gendahhblfdcddaf.meaning: The part of a movement described by drop that can be steered; drift or recoil may account for the rest.

reciprocal_nnaabbgcefabbgbk.label: tin trace
reciprocal_nnaabbgcefabbgbk.meaning: A quantity of tin too small to recover as a useful portion, yet sufficient to change the material that holds it.

reciprocal_dibnbhijncnlboom.label: guide a movement of drop
reciprocal_dibnbhijncnlboom.meaning: drop — To make the movement in question while continually correcting the course from what one sees or feels along the way.

reciprocal_mepchamknpaakeoj.label: receiver by practice
reciprocal_mepchamknpaakeoj.meaning: Someone recognized as receiver by the work they repeatedly perform before anyone grants a title.

reciprocal_pllccepjofpmgebc.label: acting receiver
reciprocal_pllccepjofpmgebc.meaning: Someone who carries the obligations of receiver for an absence with a definite end.

reciprocal_dmakamaakmiolkln.label: trusted working receiver
reciprocal_dmakamaakmiolkln.meaning: receiver — Someone in this role to whom a community actually brings the difficult cases. Title or seniority alone does not confer the distinction.

reciprocal_odpgefbcgpjniacf.label: restore the order of choice of a guardian · under divided authority
reciprocal_odpgefbcgpjniacf.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Drop-heir in Measure for Measure 00706c.

reciprocal_gchkbeaadigdonff.label: as far as the old promise ran in choice of a guardian · before a witness
reciprocal_gchkbeaadigdonff.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Drop-heir in Measure for Measure 00706c.

reciprocal_eaahfdgnngfdoide.label: chosen instil
reciprocal_eaahfdgnngfdoide.meaning: An instance of instil that someone deliberately undertakes and can answer for. The outward act may look the same when it happens by accident.

reciprocal_nelmiinmhdhdomlm.label: trained instil
reciprocal_nelmiinmhdhdomlm.meaning: An instance of instil performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_nbfbdekckjnlelme.label: do instil on another's account
reciprocal_nbfbdekckjnlelme.meaning: instil — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_bahkpcfnkfdjhfpc.label: chosen spatter
reciprocal_bahkpcfnkfdjhfpc.meaning: An instance of spatter that someone deliberately undertakes and can answer for. The outward act may look the same when it happens by accident.

reciprocal_fpkmfhcigmpopmfp.label: trained spatter
reciprocal_fpkmfhcigmpopmfp.meaning: An instance of spatter performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_dilkbpgkejfchibi.label: do spatter on another's account
reciprocal_dilkbpgkejfchibi.meaning: spatter — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_dlohpfagcjhlmicc.label: Tishbite intimation
reciprocal_dlohpfagcjhlmicc.meaning: A first grasp of Tishbite sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_pbfibdomimmnjodn.label: Tishbite put to use
reciprocal_pbfibdomimmnjodn.meaning: An understanding of Tishbite that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_jolbaoedgggngfni.label: Tishbite held on trial
reciprocal_jolbaoedgggngfni.meaning: Tishbite — A thought or belief of this kind deliberately entertained until a particular question can decide whether to keep it. The speaker owns the test as well as the idea.

reciprocal_dfhnifplgefpeajc.label: Tishbite intimation
reciprocal_dfhnifplgefpeajc.meaning: A first grasp of Tishbite sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_hecoehhfeacbmppn.label: Tishbite put to use
reciprocal_hecoehhfeacbmppn.meaning: An understanding of Tishbite that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_empjoglkmpahbnja.label: Tishbite held on trial
reciprocal_empjoglkmpahbnja.meaning: Tishbite — A thought or belief of this kind deliberately entertained until a particular question can decide whether to keep it. The speaker owns the test as well as the idea.

reciprocal_cpooakpbhembbmii.label: recover the old edge of laying out of a boundary · by inherited custom
reciprocal_cpooakpbhembbmii.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Tewkesbury in Henry IV, Part 2 00386a.

reciprocal_kejcpidpdfmbpjkh.label: by the point of last agreement in laying out of a boundary · by a trace
reciprocal_kejcpidpdfmbpjkh.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to Tewkesbury in Henry IV, Part 2 00386a.

reciprocal_ekbdmnjjobilmmnn.label: stay to see telling of a voyage take hold · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_ekbdmnjjobilmmnn.meaning: To accompany a person far enough beyond a handover to see whether they can actually continue alone. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to Teat in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VII, 709.5.

reciprocal_elmggfafjblkapdh.label: duty that survives the key in telling of a voyage · on first use
reciprocal_elmggfafjblkapdh.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Applies on a first attempt, while those involved still have no local precedent of their own. Allusion to Teat in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VII, 709.5.

reciprocal_jdobeikfjcolmndc.label: restore the order of dyeing of cloth · under divided authority

reciprocal_knomabejfpfllaao.label: as far as the old promise ran in placing of a bridge · out of public sight

reciprocal_epipbchakdohakcl.label: reach of Letter name tīel
reciprocal_epipbchakdohakcl.meaning: The stretch of speech to which Letter name tīel applies in a particular utterance. Moving the boundary can change who or what is included.

reciprocal_mepanobnfkklhjhc.label: echoed Letter name tīel
reciprocal_mepanobnfkklhjhc.meaning: An occurrence of Letter name tīel taken over from another speaker whose framing the present speaker need not endorse.

reciprocal_iilpmiocicmlhmod.label: Letter name tīel carried over
reciprocal_iilpmiocicmlhmod.meaning: Letter name tīel — An occurrence of this grammatical form whose interpretation depends on a preceding speaker's wording. Taken alone, it leaves a question of scope or reference open.

reciprocal_hicgmkhcjdboakce.label: restore the order of selection of a witness · under a closing opportunity

reciprocal_micakeejhdfbdblm.label: so far as the hand remembers in naming of a child · under divided authority

reciprocal_blbhilhahmohemlf.label: Leave someone the means to continue · passing messages · under divided authority
reciprocal_blbhilhahmohemlf.meaning: To give someone the means to continue with the passing of a message once immediate assistance ends. reciprocal_imlhaedonfiolohh.label: Time made free by a prior gift · weighing shares · without a common tongue
reciprocal_imlhaedonfiolohh.meaning: Said of a period of freedom in which an earlier provision of the weighing of a share allows someone else to choose a course without immediate dependence. reciprocal_ppbfijcfceclbemc.label: Locate between known limits · making a mould · at a distance

reciprocal_acmmenimahecncbo.label: by the point of last agreement in making of a mould · pending a challenge

reciprocal_onlmmeikacmjknop.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · learning a dance · after loss of the original

reciprocal_jmknccgelmfkgoke.label: exact at the fork of learning of a dance · in the wrong season
reciprocal_jmknccgelmfkgoke.meaning: Said of knowledge that can distinguish two lines at the moment they parted, even if their subsequent history is obscure. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to toah in 1 Chronicles 6:34.

reciprocal_kphjpnplkjjncpbc.label: A surviving thread one can work from · measuring a fever · as the sole available course
reciprocal_kphjpnplkjjncpbc.meaning: What remains of the measuring of a fever that can still carry a practice or memory after the original whole is gone. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Thoas in Troilus and Cressida 01185a.

reciprocal_kdppipchgmhgcjok.label: Hold a place for the absent · fitting hinges · for another's benefit
reciprocal_kdppipchgmhgcjok.meaning: To leave a practical place for someone's part in the fitting of a hinge during uncertainty about their return. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Thoas in Troilus and Cressida 01185a.

reciprocal_leeeplkeombjgbgg.label: distinguish an inherited fault in passing of a message · by a trace
reciprocal_leeeplkeombjgbgg.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to Tohu in 1 Samuel 1:1.

reciprocal_dmeamegjdbpdgcmi.label: exact at the fork of division of a household · against the tally
reciprocal_dmeamegjdbpdgcmi.meaning: Said of knowledge that can distinguish two lines at the moment they parted, even if their subsequent history is obscure. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to Tohu in 1 Samuel 1:1.

reciprocal_gjfmgiiihhpofdbe.label: suggest at second hand
reciprocal_gjfmgiiihhpofdbe.meaning: The substance of suggest passed on by a hearer who can vouch for hearing it but cannot vouch for the underlying claim.

reciprocal_hjmekdpacdhdilek.label: practical force of suggestion
reciprocal_hjmekdpacdhdilek.meaning: What a hearer reasonably takes suggestion to commit the speaker to doing.

reciprocal_kldjlmpacmjolfdl.label: answerable suggest
reciprocal_kldjlmpacmjolfdl.meaning: suggest — An utterance of this kind given in circumstances where its speaker can be called back to clarify it. It carries a different weight from a rumour with identical words.

reciprocal_fppgkilcbennmpdi.label: tortoise sign
reciprocal_fppgkilcbennmpdi.meaning: The presence of tortoise inferred from a fresh trace, while the creature itself remains out of sight.

reciprocal_bffgegdioplbgdbk.label: tortoise refuge
reciprocal_bffgegdioplbgdbk.meaning: A place the observer leaves undisturbed because tortoise repeatedly returns to it for cover. One sighting alone gives no such claim.

reciprocal_pjhkghkhgaajihfo.label: site-faithful tortoise
reciprocal_pjhkghkhgaajihfo.meaning: tortoise — An individual of this kind whose repeated returns to one place are reliable enough for someone to recognize or await it there. The word describes one animal's habits and carries no claim that it is tame.

reciprocal_cnijabfonenpmhnk.label: bracket the uncertainty in drawing of a chart · out of public sight

reciprocal_jfinlcemlnelkdbb.label: By retracing the last sure mark · teaching a route · at one's own cost

reciprocal_jbdgpjkiegajebda.label: Identify by its company · passing messages · at one's own cost
reciprocal_jbdgpjkiegajebda.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the passing of a message by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. reciprocal_pbdajmgijenbpbmg.label: up to the point of parting in passing of a message · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_pbdajmgijenbpbmg.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Toryne in Antony and Cleopatra 00730a.

reciprocal_bmgpmbjlieichjld.label: Identify by its company · calling a council · out of public sight
reciprocal_bmgpmbjlieichjld.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the calling of a council by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. reciprocal_gaapnmkgfmmmeeog.label: so far as the hand remembers in calling of a council · by inherited custom
reciprocal_gaapnmkgfmmmeeog.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Tob in Judges 11:5.

reciprocal_bbkaknfjgdhkiaal.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · drawing charts · at a distance
reciprocal_bbkaknfjgdhkiaal.meaning: To give a judgment about the drawing of a chart temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. reciprocal_fobhhgdejfdodlbm.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · drying grain · for another's benefit
reciprocal_fobhhgdejfdodlbm.meaning: The share of a decision about the drying of a harvest that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. reciprocal_fmpbdidjbiopgkao.label: Locate between known limits · teaching a route · under shared liability
reciprocal_fmpbdidjbiopgkao.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the teaching of a route by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. reciprocal_lcjihofihbhnbckm.label: by the point of last agreement in teaching of a route · after consent
reciprocal_lcjihofihbhnbckm.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. reciprocal_hipeemlkjcaigcgo.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Toby in Twelfth Night 00085a.

reciprocal_dgiilmmgncaifpcl.label: so far as the hand remembers in division of a household · pending a challenge

reciprocal_nconbdohnoplgobl.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · tending a shared lamp · against the tally
reciprocal_nconbdohnoplgobl.meaning: To give a judgment about the care of a shared lamp temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. reciprocal_jhnkdedhhjhikihi.label: Learned down one branch · naming a child · after a disputed account

reciprocal_iocdkgcgcbjcchfa.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · carrying a burden · after loss of the original
reciprocal_iocdkgcgcbjcchfa.meaning: To give a judgment about the carrying of a burden temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to Tobiah in Nehemiah 13:8.

reciprocal_ccdcjemkncnlfdak.label: Common ground that still bears work · carrying a burden · with a reserve
reciprocal_ccdcjemkncnlfdak.meaning: The portion of the carrying of a burden that remains jointly workable during a dispute. Its scope is measured by what both parties still actually do. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Tobiah in Nehemiah 13:8.

reciprocal_nlgfmjajklgmeicm.label: distinguish an inherited fault in keeping of a child's confidence · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_nlgfmjajklgmeicm.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Tobit in Paradise Lost, Book IV, 166–171.

reciprocal_dekgffflgikhalin.label: taught within one line of dividing of inherited tools · after a handover
reciprocal_dekgffflgikhalin.meaning: Said of a skill transmitted within one line of teachers. Outsiders may perform the same work by a recognizably different sequence. reciprocal_idhdcahnoconjkmi.label: restore the order of return of a borrowed thing · at a distance

reciprocal_llgliffaobegmfbb.label: Learned down one branch · choosing witnesses · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_llgliffaobegmfbb.meaning: Said of knowledge of the selection of a witness that is exact on one line of descent or transmission while adjacent lines remain undocumented. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to Togarmah in 1 Chronicles 1:6.

reciprocal_dalglgfpjafbkafm.label: topaz witness-piece

reciprocal_lohnkdldakgacmfg.label: topaz trace

reciprocal_bhnhngoicjdjigob.label: recovered topaz
reciprocal_bhnhngoicjdjigob.meaning: topaz — Material of this kind recovered from an earlier use and accepted for another on the strength of what it can still do.

reciprocal_boelkaeahpoljlge.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · handing over a key · in the wrong season
reciprocal_boelkaeahpoljlge.meaning: To give a judgment about the handover of a key temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Topas in Twelfth Night 00809a.

reciprocal_bbfmlnmnddnbbcem.label: duty that survives the key in handover of a key · between strangers
reciprocal_bbfmlnmnddnbbcem.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to Topas in Twelfth Night 00809a.

reciprocal_gcpgaakbfacjhcem.label: Transmit beyond the written record · recovering strays · against the tally
reciprocal_gcpgaakbfacjhcem.meaning: To transmit a practice of the rescue of a stray animal beyond the last person or occasion named in its written record. The practice may continue on different terms. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to tophet in Paradise Lost, Book I, 403–405.

reciprocal_jimflcnabjjafofi.label: so far as the hand remembers in reckoning of a debt · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_jimflcnabjjafofi.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to tophet in Paradise Lost, Book I, 403–405.

reciprocal_njaljlbihakojibm.label: Identify by its company · dividing a household · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_njaljlbihakojibm.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the division of a household by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to topheth in 2 Kings 23:10.

reciprocal_eknhnphjcckcmhbp.label: up to the point of parting in division of a household · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_eknhnphjcckcmhbp.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to topheth in 2 Kings 23:10.

reciprocal_jochafljelcfcdad.label: unmix two accounts of taking of soundings · under divided authority
reciprocal_jochafljelcfcdad.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Tophel in Deuteronomy 1:1.

reciprocal_obddabpbedocpnmb.label: up to the point of parting in taking of soundings · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_obddabpbedocpnmb.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to Tophel in Deuteronomy 1:1.

reciprocal_cmnakfejlakjoced.label: Trace through successive hands · telling a voyage · at a distance
reciprocal_cmnakfejlakjoced.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the telling of a voyage by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. reciprocal_dfkdnidiodablgoo.label: taught within one line of division of a household · after a handover
reciprocal_dfkdnidiodablgoo.meaning: Said of a skill transmitted within one line of teachers. Outsiders may perform the same work by a recognizably different sequence. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to Tola in Genesis 46:13.

reciprocal_gemdajdkdcighgni.label: trace the hand behind making of a mould · at the second attempt
reciprocal_gemdajdkdcighgni.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. reciprocal_niibjclknjfhpepa.label: exact at the fork of making of a mould · between generations
reciprocal_niibjclknjfhpepa.meaning: Said of knowledge that can distinguish two lines at the moment they parted, even if their subsequent history is obscure. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to tolad in 1 Chronicles 4:29.

reciprocal_kbnhdboamhiiidhb.label: Leave someone the means to continue · drying grain · by private agreement
reciprocal_kbnhdboamhiiidhb.meaning: To give someone the means to continue with the drying of a harvest once immediate assistance ends. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Toledo in Henry VIII 00236a.

reciprocal_bahfhglobfpfhblk.label: Time made free by a prior gift · reckoning a debt · at a distance
reciprocal_bahfhglobfpfhblk.meaning: Said of a period of freedom in which an earlier provision of the reckoning of a debt allows someone else to choose a course without immediate dependence. reciprocal_lfdhcbcknebnpiln.label: mouth warning
