reciprocal_bnniobmfikajcimh.label: working knowledge of A mouth into the current

reciprocal_ahjncoiphpaccgob.label: hindsight of A mouth into the current

reciprocal_pklkfdmccndaljjn.label: A mouth into the current passed by the hand

reciprocal_omefepllfaebhhlb.label: by the point of last agreement in telling of a voyage · in the wrong season

reciprocal_mafgddjeeelocajd.label: recover the old edge of collection of a toll · at the second attempt

reciprocal_ihcailgjklbjlmdi.label: by the point of last agreement in collection of a toll · by inherited custom

reciprocal_oioefhmeficjfkad.label: so far as the hand remembers in laying out of a boundary · after consent

reciprocal_gdmdjemmcolhlkne.label: restore the order of naming of a child · after loss of the original

reciprocal_agcpkiocpkninfbj.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · laying down office · as a rehearsal

reciprocal_enldcelohbfnbhkd.label: duty that survives the key in collection of a toll · between strangers
reciprocal_enldcelohbfnbhkd.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to tou in 1 Chronicles 18:9.

reciprocal_hibnialmdjfjgncp.label: fox witness-piece

reciprocal_pgpjicpaelaleiib.label: fox blade refuge

reciprocal_niadnooielioddmn.label: recovered fox

reciprocal_mgibkminanknbifo.label: The fox gets a vote as a deed

reciprocal_aljoaindedcljgpl.label: The fox has changed its coat turned towards someone
reciprocal_aljoaindedcljgpl.meaning: A pointed use of “The fox has changed its coat” as an intervention in another person's situation. The addressee can accept or resist that reading.

reciprocal_kikckglapnbjphjc.label: the second occasion for The fox has changed its coat

reciprocal_kikckglapnbjphjc.origin: narrower alternative from tōl po’fülen oilumowfu

reciprocal_jnfealajngcheflh.label: foxship refuge

reciprocal_iklimijdcbilbnep.label: up to the point of parting in taking of testimony · on first use

reciprocal_ejkdnicmdlbnlhig.label: reach of Letter name tōmä

reciprocal_akpnpghdofkibngn.label: edge of conference

reciprocal_opcjbfnapoaecbem.label: freely assembled conference

reciprocal_mbopcnlpknapmfka.label: Stay past the handover · changing the night watch · by inherited custom

reciprocal_pnfclkndgfkcbpap.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · changing the night watch · before a witness

reciprocal_bgoaccmbiepnnpcl.label: recover the old edge of setting of a price · on independent confirmation

reciprocal_hipfnaedjbljbipo.label: Stay past the handover · storing water · between generations

reciprocal_djhgiobofjcgjndn.label: learned well enough to reverse in storage of water · against the tally
reciprocal_djhgiobofjcgjndn.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. reciprocal_jkaacgkmidakeoac.label: Identify by its company · returning a loan · between strangers

reciprocal_mnkdnmgjidbnifek.label: up to the point of parting in return of a borrowed thing · out of public sight

reciprocal_aokdcphkljflbmne.label: as far as the old promise ran in taking of testimony · before a witness

reciprocal_jblgfaolnbgldape.label: turtle-dove sign

reciprocal_lfcejklkckidmefd.label: Locate between known limits · keeping seed · with a reserve
reciprocal_lfcejklkckidmefd.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the keeping of seed by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Ekron in Joshua 15:46.

reciprocal_khiedgbifjdhlhol.label: by the point of last agreement in keeping of seed · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_khiedgbifjdhlhol.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to Ekron in Joshua 15:46.

reciprocal_enjimbadlihlafbi.label: recover the old edge of dividing of inherited tools · after a handover
reciprocal_enjimbadlihlafbi.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to Ekronite in Joshua 13:3.

reciprocal_oomckebodgjgfnpb.label: by the point of last agreement in dividing of inherited tools · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_oomckebodgjgfnpb.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Ekronite in Joshua 13:3.

reciprocal_hbnnepfgggcmaocj.label: bracket the uncertainty in keeping of seed · after consent
reciprocal_hbnnepfgggcmaocj.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to Ekronite in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, Joshua 13:3.

reciprocal_hkngnpaapcplmkbe.label: duty that survives the key in placing of a bridge · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_hkngnpaapcplmkbe.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to Ekronite in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, Joshua 13:3.

reciprocal_fhkhjacbpjgidbgm.label: restore the order of sealing of a letter · in the wrong season
reciprocal_fhkhjacbpjgidbgm.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Ecbatan in Paradise Lost, Book XI, 393–400.

reciprocal_ccpeejiajpahijlh.label: as far as the old promise ran in sealing of a letter · in company with a novice
reciprocal_ccpeejiajpahijlh.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to Ecbatan in Paradise Lost, Book XI, 393–400.

reciprocal_fhbldmeefabjcjbl.label: distinguish an inherited fault in dyeing of cloth · after consent
reciprocal_fhbldmeefabjcjbl.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to eker in 1 Chronicles 2:27.

reciprocal_adnioeppihbejjhp.label: taught within one line of setting of a price · at a distance
reciprocal_adnioeppihbejjhp.meaning: Said of a skill transmitted within one line of teachers. Outsiders may perform the same work by a recognizably different sequence. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to eker in 1 Chronicles 2:27.

reciprocal_fdijghffahiikikk.label: exposition at second hand
reciprocal_fdijghffahiikikk.meaning: The substance of exposition passed on by a hearer who can vouch for hearing it but cannot vouch for the underlying claim.

reciprocal_nkanlhodechaepke.label: practical force of exposition
reciprocal_nkanlhodechaepke.meaning: What a hearer reasonably takes exposition to commit the speaker to doing.

reciprocal_dohlnjmlflchicki.label: answerable exposition
reciprocal_dohlnjmlflchicki.meaning: exposition — An utterance of this kind given in circumstances where its speaker can be called back to clarify it. It carries a different weight from a rumour with identical words.

reciprocal_bpplfcidooebghmn.label: read the gap in timing of a departure · out of public sight
reciprocal_bpplfcidooebghmn.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to Exton in Richard II 00580a.

reciprocal_dkiobjkojhdimipg.label: so far as the hand remembers in timing of a departure · by a trace
reciprocal_dkiobjkojhdimipg.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to Exton in Richard II 00580a.

reciprocal_gkijajpfolmnebda.label: Restore a neglected voice · sharing inherited tools · in the wrong season
reciprocal_gkijajpfolmnebda.meaning: To bring a disregarded account of the dividing of inherited tools into hearing without taking credit for originating it. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Exeter in Richard III 01049a.

reciprocal_lbiehpclfhoinloe.label: voice of the first correction in dividing of inherited tools · pending a challenge
reciprocal_lbiehpclfhoinloe.meaning: A small change in a repeated account which identifies the person who first corrected it. Names a provisional arrangement that stands until someone brings a specific objection. Allusion to Exeter in Richard III 01049a.

reciprocal_mhnkabpdicbkcmjp.label: echo by local measure
reciprocal_mhnkabpdicbkcmjp.meaning: The quality called echo as judged against the things actually available for comparison here.

reciprocal_nabdkhmmdnjphcff.label: trained rebound
reciprocal_nabdkhmmdnjphcff.meaning: An instance of rebound performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_cfohfaopjoaikhfn.label: echo to the practical threshold
reciprocal_cfohfaopjoaikhfn.meaning: echo — Having the quality in question to the degree required for the immediate work. Further degrees may be perceptible yet irrelevant to the present choice.

reciprocal_igghegnkecbgmofn.label: To measure an echo with a thumb as a deed
reciprocal_igghegnkecbgmofn.meaning: The act or lived situation pictured by the idiom “To measure an echo with a thumb”, recognized in a particular case before anyone gives it a name.
reciprocal_igghegnkecbgmofn.origin: productive contrast from ekol rãnth trembārjel mem’en

reciprocal_oopnmdejdfkbjfbb.label: To measure an echo with a thumb turned towards someone
reciprocal_oopnmdejdfkbjfbb.meaning: A pointed use of “To measure an echo with a thumb” as an intervention in another person's situation. The addressee can accept or resist that reading.
reciprocal_oopnmdejdfkbjfbb.origin: productive contrast from ekol rãnth trembārjel mem’en

reciprocal_jneeafcgggilhgkd.label: the second occasion for To measure an echo with a thumb
reciprocal_jneeafcgggilhgkd.meaning: To measure an echo with a thumb — A recurrence of the situation pictured in this idiom that those involved recognize in time to respond differently.
reciprocal_jneeafcgggilhgkd.origin: narrower alternative from ekol rãnth trembārjel mem’en

reciprocal_mcnemnkngnbcbndb.label: inward An echo that asks your name
reciprocal_mcnemnkngnbcbndb.meaning: The inward experience caught by “An echo that asks your name” while the person living through it has yet to tell anyone.
reciprocal_mcnemnkngnbcbndb.origin: productive contrast from ekol chetib nel’den wÏōowya

reciprocal_cgnfjnodefliiema.label: recognized An echo that asks your name
reciprocal_cgnfjnodefliiema.meaning: A moment of recognizing in another's account the experience that “An echo that asks your name” had named only privately.
reciprocal_cgnfjnodefliiema.origin: productive contrast from ekol chetib nel’den wÏōowya

reciprocal_ecpikhelpcfgijap.label: An echo that asks your name spoken back
reciprocal_ecpikhelpcfgijap.meaning: An echo that asks your name — The experience pictured by the idiom when someone else puts it into words before the person feeling it has been able to do so.
reciprocal_ecpikhelpcfgijap.origin: narrower alternative from ekol chetib nel’den wÏōowya

reciprocal_cjahceamodaepkml.label: To hand back the echo as a deed
reciprocal_cjahceamodaepkml.meaning: The act or lived situation pictured by the idiom “To hand back the echo”, recognized in a particular case before anyone gives it a name.
reciprocal_cjahceamodaepkml.origin: productive contrast from ekol tar fāw’en

reciprocal_ldbfoknflopmbdop.label: To hand back the echo turned towards someone
reciprocal_ldbfoknflopmbdop.meaning: A pointed use of “To hand back the echo” as an intervention in another person's situation. The addressee can accept or resist that reading.
reciprocal_ldbfoknflopmbdop.origin: productive contrast from ekol tar fāw’en

reciprocal_mjggieconnmhjbgi.label: the second occasion for To hand back the echo
reciprocal_mjggieconnmhjbgi.meaning: To hand back the echo — A recurrence of the situation pictured in this idiom that those involved recognize in time to respond differently.
reciprocal_mjggieconnmhjbgi.origin: narrower alternative from ekol tar fāw’en

reciprocal_fdhhlmkgmokkbkdd.label: An echo in the wrong hat as a deed
reciprocal_fdhhlmkgmokkbkdd.meaning: The act or lived situation pictured by the idiom “An echo in the wrong hat”, recognized in a particular case before anyone gives it a name.
reciprocal_fdhhlmkgmokkbkdd.origin: productive contrast from ekol ni murlamet’mū harenfelen

reciprocal_naecmbhdjkekkfid.label: An echo in the wrong hat turned towards someone
reciprocal_naecmbhdjkekkfid.meaning: A pointed use of “An echo in the wrong hat” as an intervention in another person's situation. The addressee can accept or resist that reading.
reciprocal_naecmbhdjkekkfid.origin: productive contrast from ekol ni murlamet’mū harenfelen

reciprocal_chobbkahfojgpljb.label: the second occasion for An echo in the wrong hat
reciprocal_chobbkahfojgpljb.meaning: An echo in the wrong hat — A recurrence of the situation pictured in this idiom that those involved recognize in time to respond differently.
reciprocal_chobbkahfojgpljb.origin: narrower alternative from ekol ni murlamet’mū harenfelen

reciprocal_nikpnpgkdfjagpoi.label: working knowledge of To oil the echo
reciprocal_nikpnpgkdfjagpoi.meaning: The practical judgment encapsulated in “To oil the echo” when it changes a person's next move while there is still time to act.

reciprocal_ddefhmkanbichfdo.label: hindsight of To oil the echo
reciprocal_ddefhmkanbichfdo.meaning: The retrospective recognition expressed by “To oil the echo” once the chance to act on it in that particular instance has passed.

reciprocal_jljfokbpakppakaa.label: To oil the echo passed by the hand
reciprocal_jljfokbpakppakaa.meaning: To oil the echo — The practical insight expressed in the idiom when one person passes it to another by demonstrating the timing of an act.

reciprocal_ejbbonpoakpjcgbo.label: To return the echo its silence as a deed
reciprocal_ejbbonpoakpjcgbo.meaning: The act or lived situation pictured by the idiom “To return the echo its silence”, recognized in a particular case before anyone gives it a name.
reciprocal_ejbbonpoakpjcgbo.origin: productive contrast from ekolel po’dwengen tar fāw’en

reciprocal_odfhlgpdpeamnfmj.label: To return the echo its silence turned towards someone
reciprocal_odfhlgpdpeamnfmj.meaning: A pointed use of “To return the echo its silence” as an intervention in another person's situation. The addressee can accept or resist that reading.
reciprocal_odfhlgpdpeamnfmj.origin: productive contrast from ekolel po’dwengen tar fāw’en

reciprocal_kofboidncohgafhf.label: the second occasion for To return the echo its silence
reciprocal_kofboidncohgafhf.meaning: To return the echo its silence — A recurrence of the situation pictured in this idiom that those involved recognize in time to respond differently.
reciprocal_kofboidncohgafhf.origin: narrower alternative from ekolel po’dwengen tar fāw’en

reciprocal_lkgdbnjnapmfggfh.label: To win the echo’s race as a deed
reciprocal_lkgdbnjnapmfggfh.meaning: The act or lived situation pictured by the idiom “To win the echo’s race”, recognized in a particular case before anyone gives it a name.
reciprocal_lkgdbnjnapmfggfh.origin: productive contrast from ekol’i loitŧhmarjong zift’en

reciprocal_lopmdipdmmihknmm.label: To win the echo’s race turned towards someone
reciprocal_lopmdipdmmihknmm.meaning: A pointed use of “To win the echo’s race” as an intervention in another person's situation. The addressee can accept or resist that reading.
reciprocal_lopmdipdmmihknmm.origin: productive contrast from ekol’i loitŧhmarjong zift’en

reciprocal_ahcomaoahpcockio.label: the second occasion for To win the echo’s race
reciprocal_ahcomaoahpcockio.meaning: To win the echo’s race — A recurrence of the situation pictured in this idiom that those involved recognize in time to respond differently.
reciprocal_ahcomaoahpcockio.origin: narrower alternative from ekol’i loitŧhmarjong zift’en

reciprocal_nkbelkaknggebhho.label: starling sign
reciprocal_nkbelkaknggebhho.meaning: The presence of starling inferred from a fresh trace, while the creature itself remains out of sight.

reciprocal_kejajhojkjbpdcll.label: starling refuge
reciprocal_kejajhojkjbpdcll.meaning: A place the observer leaves undisturbed because starling repeatedly returns to it for cover. One sighting alone gives no such claim.

reciprocal_negjbpllhbkecepf.label: site-faithful starling
reciprocal_negjbpllhbkecepf.meaning: starling — An individual of this kind whose repeated returns to one place are reliable enough for someone to recognize or await it there. The word describes one animal's habits and carries no claim that it is tame.

reciprocal_apggoejolhofpebi.label: Trace through successive hands · caring for graves · by private agreement
reciprocal_apggoejolhofpebi.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the care of a grave by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Aeacus in Henry VI, Part 2 00153b.

reciprocal_ffligcfmahaofocm.label: Time made free by a prior gift · recording descent · by a trace
reciprocal_ffligcfmahaofocm.meaning: Said of a period of freedom in which an earlier provision of the record of a descent allows someone else to choose a course without immediate dependence. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to Aeacus in Henry VI, Part 2 00153b.

reciprocal_bhmppnnhpolinhdi.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · learning a dance · on first use
reciprocal_bhmppnnhpolinhdi.meaning: To give a judgment about the learning of a dance temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Applies on a first attempt, while those involved still have no local precedent of their own. Allusion to easter-acts in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, Acts 12:4.

reciprocal_dcophjgpadjnmoig.label: A voice recognizable in the retelling · learning a dance · between strangers
reciprocal_dcophjgpadjnmoig.meaning: A remembered turn of phrase that discloses whose account of the learning of a dance is being repeated even after the speaker's name has dropped out. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to easter-acts in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, Acts 12:4.

reciprocal_mbcolhdadllddemk.label: Trace through successive hands · telling a voyage · after a handover
reciprocal_mbcolhdadllddemk.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the telling of a voyage by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to Ehi in Genesis 46:21.

reciprocal_hghfccdmbannamjd.label: exact at the fork of telling of a voyage · with a reserve
reciprocal_hghfccdmbannamjd.meaning: Said of knowledge that can distinguish two lines at the moment they parted, even if their subsequent history is obscure. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Ehi in Genesis 46:21.

reciprocal_gljojbphnhljcdka.label: stay to see calling of a council take hold · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_gljojbphnhljcdka.meaning: To accompany a person far enough beyond a handover to see whether they can actually continue alone. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Ehud in Judges 3:26.

reciprocal_iomjnokejigdnnda.label: learned well enough to reverse in rehearsal of a song · after loss of the original
reciprocal_iomjnokejigdnnda.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to Ehud in Judges 3:26.

reciprocal_chanobehcoogcmaf.label: trace the hand behind telling of a voyage · on first use
reciprocal_chanobehcoogcmaf.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. Applies on a first attempt, while those involved still have no local precedent of their own. Allusion to Er in Genesis 38:3.

reciprocal_lceakeegogpjdlcm.label: taught within one line of telling of a voyage · between generations
reciprocal_lceakeegogpjdlcm.meaning: Said of a skill transmitted within one line of teachers. Outsiders may perform the same work by a recognizably different sequence. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Er in Genesis 38:3.

reciprocal_bnfmfnafejoalcmi.label: restore the order of drying of a harvest · pending a challenge
reciprocal_bnfmfnafejoalcmi.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Names a provisional arrangement that stands until someone brings a specific objection. Allusion to ercles in A Midsummer Night's Dream, passage 0094.

reciprocal_hbcbpbfodefegnbl.label: so far as the hand remembers in landing of a boat · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_hbcbpbfodefegnbl.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to ercles in A Midsummer Night's Dream, passage 0094.

reciprocal_pjpbjpdfapknnfle.label: Identify by its company · sealing a letter · after a disputed account
reciprocal_pjpbjpdfapknnfle.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the sealing of a letter by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Used in response to an actual difference between people's accounts of what happened. Allusion to Ercoco in Paradise Lost, Book XI, 393–400.

reciprocal_cnikmkgnhfnknona.label: up to the point of parting in return of a borrowed thing · at the second attempt
reciprocal_cnikmkgnhfnknona.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Ercoco in Paradise Lost, Book XI, 393–400.

reciprocal_banmeipblnpmfcii.label: Trace through successive hands · keeping seed · out of public sight
reciprocal_banmeipblnpmfcii.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the keeping of seed by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to Eran in Numbers 26:36.

reciprocal_lcojnbnefmbmnpoj.label: duty that survives the key in record of a descent · at the second attempt
reciprocal_lcojnbnefmbmnpoj.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Eran in Numbers 26:36.

reciprocal_hpgmeikbejdlhfda.label: stay to see handover of a key take hold · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_hpgmeikbejdlhfda.meaning: To accompany a person far enough beyond a handover to see whether they can actually continue alone. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to Erastus in Acts 19:22.

reciprocal_jdojcmbckloflkei.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · timing a departure · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_jdojcmbckloflkei.meaning: The share of a decision about the timing of a departure that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to Erastus in Acts 19:22.

reciprocal_gihocehealmjcknl.label: Bound a disagreement · calling a council · under shared liability
reciprocal_gihocehealmjcknl.meaning: To isolate the disputed part of the calling of a council so that the people involved can still work together on the rest. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to Erpingham in Henry V 00494a.

reciprocal_gamohbancdfjmndn.label: Common ground that still bears work · calling a council · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_gamohbancdfjmndn.meaning: The portion of the calling of a council that remains jointly workable during a dispute. Its scope is measured by what both parties still actually do. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to Erpingham in Henry V 00494a.

reciprocal_lankbolhmibpnodf.label: Trace through successive hands · taking testimony · at a distance
reciprocal_lankbolhmibpnodf.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the taking of testimony by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to Erech in Genesis 10:10.

reciprocal_mdodhopddfipkeoa.label: Learned down one branch · taking testimony · after a failed trial
reciprocal_mdodhopddfipkeoa.meaning: Said of knowledge of the taking of testimony that is exact on one line of descent or transmission while adjacent lines remain undocumented. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to Erech in Genesis 10:10.

reciprocal_gmiemndmleoaljpa.label: Identify by its company · fitting hinges · after a handover
reciprocal_gmiemndmleoaljpa.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the fitting of a hinge by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to Erebus in Paradise Lost, Book II, 879–884.

reciprocal_jecjogmpeljloabm.label: so far as the hand remembers in fitting of a hinge · by inherited custom
reciprocal_jecjogmpeljloabm.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Erebus in Paradise Lost, Book II, 879–884.

reciprocal_cjcnjkhlgefnfpac.label: restore the order of division of a household · at one's own cost
reciprocal_cjcnjkhlgefnfpac.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to Ermengare in Henry V 00037g.

reciprocal_gobigpefecckiilf.label: as far as the old promise ran in division of a household · for another's benefit
reciprocal_gobigpefecckiilf.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Ermengare in Henry V 00037g.

reciprocal_ghelafaioocdloah.label: Trace through successive hands · telling a voyage · for another's benefit
reciprocal_ghelafaioocdloah.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the telling of a voyage by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Eri in Numbers 26:16.

reciprocal_ogclgghghcoigbpf.label: learned well enough to reverse in telling of a voyage · as the sole available course
reciprocal_ogclgghghcoigbpf.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Eri in Numbers 26:16.

reciprocal_gccblncppgengdfb.label: Restore a neglected voice · settling quarrels · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_gccblncppgengdfb.meaning: To bring a disregarded account of the settling of a quarrel into hearing without taking credit for originating it. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Eros in Antony and Cleopatra 01077a.

reciprocal_fdlkenipngpkpceo.label: By what the hand can actually fit · settling quarrels · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_fdlkenipngpkpceo.meaning: With the tolerance that matters in the daily handling of the settling of a quarrel, even when a finer distinction exists on paper. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Eros in Antony and Cleopatra 01077a.

reciprocal_oeofgmngkjnpkdeo.label: Trace through successive hands · sealing a letter · after a failed trial
reciprocal_oeofgmngkjnpkdeo.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the sealing of a letter by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to Ebal in Genesis 36:23.

reciprocal_ehanemgdjdlgcipn.label: Counted without a hearing · weighing shares · with a reserve
reciprocal_ehanemgdjdlgcipn.meaning: A member or instance of the weighing of a share counted in a total but never called individually. It has numerical presence without an individual hearing. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Ebal in Genesis 36:23.

reciprocal_gbkohojmekepbdnh.label: Identify by its company · counting sleepers · without a common tongue
reciprocal_gbkohojmekepbdnh.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the counting of sleepers by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Used when a shared word is unavailable and meaning must pass through gesture, example, or an object. Allusion to Ebronah in Numbers 33:34.

reciprocal_efkaohojcgiiibje.label: up to the point of parting in counting of sleepers · before a witness
reciprocal_efkaohojcgiiibje.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Ebronah in Numbers 33:34.

reciprocal_indpminilooehhii.label: trace the hand behind taking of testimony · by a trace
reciprocal_indpminilooehhii.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to Eber in Genesis 10:21.

reciprocal_epcgfgkghneaflip.label: taught within one line of taking of testimony · by inherited custom
reciprocal_epcgfgkghneaflip.meaning: Said of a skill transmitted within one line of teachers. Outsiders may perform the same work by a recognizably different sequence. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Eber in Genesis 10:21.

reciprocal_kcmjlniknlaobikn.label: Trace through successive hands · telling a voyage · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_kcmjlniknlaobikn.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the telling of a voyage by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to Ebed in Judges 9:30.

reciprocal_bcpdamhfnjnofdpn.label: by the point of last agreement in telling of a voyage · before a witness
reciprocal_bcpdamhfnjnofdpn.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Ebed in Judges 9:30.

reciprocal_bceifepbpjgmogfa.label: Identify by its company · making a mould · by a trace
reciprocal_bceifepbpjgmogfa.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the making of a mould by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. reciprocal_bmlcnbhpdlohccka.label: By retracing the last sure mark · drawing charts · after consent

reciprocal_nlhojnjoccodhjli.label: read the gap in timing of a departure · as a rehearsal

reciprocal_dhnekddmddlkcieo.label: as far as the old promise ran in selection of a witness · under a closing opportunity

reciprocal_fchipcbfonpaekpm.label: recover the old edge of laying out of a boundary · on independent confirmation

reciprocal_oombpjlgpjjhnnpe.label: blade hand-wear

reciprocal_nglocmbdmdblidjm.label: dislike borne for someone else

reciprocal_mcalfninfigdbgpd.label: Leave someone the means to continue · opening roads · after a failed trial
reciprocal_mcalfninfigdbgpd.meaning: To give someone the means to continue with the opening of a road once immediate assistance ends. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to Leo in Leviathan, Chapter 42, Hobbes_0161_1145.1.

reciprocal_gidmolbinhpndgif.label: voice of the first correction in taking of soundings · at one's own cost
reciprocal_gidmolbinhpndgif.meaning: A small change in a repeated account which identifies the person who first corrected it. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to Leo in Leviathan, Chapter 42, Hobbes_0161_1145.1.

reciprocal_ehhlmgjelkeckeff.label: reach of sung fa
reciprocal_ehhlmgjelkeckeff.meaning: The stretch of speech to which sung fa applies in a particular utterance. Moving the boundary can change who or what is included.

reciprocal_bfjmgogdepccbbap.label: echoed sung fa
reciprocal_bfjmgogdepccbbap.meaning: An occurrence of sung fa taken over from another speaker whose framing the present speaker need not endorse.

reciprocal_eocpopnhacbpfngo.label: sung fa carried over
reciprocal_eocpopnhacbpfngo.meaning: sung fa — An occurrence of this grammatical form whose interpretation depends on a preceding speaker's wording. Taken alone, it leaves a question of scope or reference open.

reciprocal_nmdlaoifhmoopnpo.label: Borrow the lee, give back the wind as a deed
reciprocal_nmdlaoifhmoopnpo.meaning: The act or lived situation pictured by the idiom “Borrow the lee, give back the wind”, recognized in a particular case before anyone gives it a name.
reciprocal_nmdlaoifhmoopnpo.origin: productive contrast from Li ouvlemvãhe, enif tar fāwe

reciprocal_phpdalhkceagajen.label: Borrow the lee, give back the wind turned towards someone
reciprocal_phpdalhkceagajen.meaning: A pointed use of “Borrow the lee, give back the wind” as an intervention in another person's situation. The addressee can accept or resist that reading.
reciprocal_phpdalhkceagajen.origin: productive contrast from Li ouvlemvãhe, enif tar fāwe

reciprocal_boicbbbinnoaopmg.label: the second occasion for Borrow the lee, give back the wind
reciprocal_boicbbbinnoaopmg.meaning: Borrow the lee, give back the wind — A recurrence of the situation pictured in this idiom that those involved recognize in time to respond differently.
reciprocal_boicbbbinnoaopmg.origin: narrower alternative from Li ouvlemvãhe, enif tar fāwe

reciprocal_gldmodobbmiaccnk.label: Stay past the handover · timing a departure · after a failed trial
reciprocal_gldmodobbmiaccnk.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the timing of a departure after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to Lichas in Paradise Lost, Book II, 542–546.

reciprocal_hdfgdbnbpplfnmob.label: learned well enough to reverse in timing of a departure · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_hdfgdbnbpplfnmob.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Lichas in Paradise Lost, Book II, 542–546.

reciprocal_mpkceicapbijgkej.label: unmix two accounts of giving of a pledge · after consent
reciprocal_mpkceicapbijgkej.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to Lycaonia in Acts 14:6.

reciprocal_edhhhnjbbcjmigmp.label: up to the point of parting in choice of a guardian · on first use
reciprocal_edhhhnjbbcjmigmp.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Applies on a first attempt, while those involved still have no local precedent of their own. Allusion to Lycaonia in Acts 14:6.

reciprocal_kpbhpdopgcelagnc.label: distinguish an inherited fault in placing of a mooring · under shared liability
reciprocal_kpbhpdopgcelagnc.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to likhi in 1 Chronicles 7:19.

reciprocal_ldckdjgnamkanmha.label: Learned down one branch · keeping a promise · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_ldckdjgnamkanmha.meaning: Said of knowledge of the keeping of a promise that is exact on one line of descent or transmission while adjacent lines remain undocumented. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to likhi in 1 Chronicles 7:19.

reciprocal_pgnehkfofhfpmmhj.label: recover the old edge of division of a catch · between generations
reciprocal_pgnehkfofhfpmmhj.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Lycia in Acts 27:5.

reciprocal_pmjjnnmjanhdohbn.label: Learned well enough to retrace · sharing a catch · before a witness
reciprocal_pmjjnnmjanhdohbn.meaning: Said of a route, habit, or piece of knowledge of the division of a catch which can be retraced independently after learning it in someone else's company. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Lycia in Acts 27:5.

reciprocal_ijjangnhgakcgdgg.label: leek season-sign
reciprocal_ijjangnhgakcgdgg.meaning: The stage of leek that local people watch to tell when other seasonal work can begin.

reciprocal_mgkhmnhofenkjlod.label: leek reserve-stock
reciprocal_mgkhmnhofenkjlod.meaning: A living part of leek set aside so that next season's stock survives the present harvest.

reciprocal_odcamlclheoagcod.label: volunteer leek
reciprocal_odcamlclheoagcod.meaning: leek — A plant of this kind that establishes itself where nobody in the present season planted it. Said when its appearance matters as evidence of earlier growth.

reciprocal_iohmlkaephdpnjal.label: Stand by within reach · sharing a catch · at a distance
reciprocal_iohmlkaephdpnjal.meaning: To remain close enough to help with the division of a catch while leaving the person concerned free to finish the act. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to Lychorida in Pericles, Prince of Tyre 00292a.

reciprocal_ddnlidckcjkomhba.label: Time made free by a prior gift · sharing a catch · after a handover
reciprocal_ddnlidckcjkomhba.meaning: Said of a period of freedom in which an earlier provision of the division of a catch allows someone else to choose a course without immediate dependence. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to Lychorida in Pericles, Prince of Tyre 00292a.

reciprocal_amaiijibkcgdpmhg.label: Leave someone the means to continue · calling a council · at a distance
reciprocal_amaiijibkcgdpmhg.meaning: To give someone the means to continue with the calling of a council once immediate assistance ends. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to Lycurgus in Coriolanus 00300b.

reciprocal_hpjefhlffmaionof.label: Time made free by a prior gift · collecting tolls · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_hpjefhlffmaionof.meaning: Said of a period of freedom in which an earlier provision of the collection of a toll allows someone else to choose a course without immediate dependence. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Lycurgus in Coriolanus 00300b.

reciprocal_khbpdgbfafpbkjjc.label: Identify by its company · caring for graves · under shared liability
reciprocal_khbpdgbfafpbkjjc.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the care of a grave by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to Leander in The Two Gentlemen of Verona 00007a.

reciprocal_bodhocbcdlpfjppp.label: so far as the hand remembers in care of a grave · before a witness
reciprocal_bodhocbcdlpfjppp.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Leander in The Two Gentlemen of Verona 00007a.

reciprocal_bcjbddebemcdjnda.label: distinguish an inherited fault in calling of a council · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_bcjbddebemcdjnda.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Lear in King Lear 00032a.

reciprocal_nelmjkkecjglffpl.label: Learned down one branch · laying down office · after a disputed account
reciprocal_nelmjkkecjglffpl.meaning: Said of knowledge of the laying down of an office that is exact on one line of descent or transmission while adjacent lines remain undocumented. Used in response to an actual difference between people's accounts of what happened. Allusion to Lear in King Lear 00032a.

reciprocal_edoaiocppnibkhkj.label: elbow (slip) hand-wear
reciprocal_edoaiocppnibkhkj.meaning: The polish or hollow left by repeated handling of elbow (slip), valued as evidence of who used it or how.

reciprocal_jlfnnhdelmmnmadf.label: elbow (slip) stand-in
reciprocal_jlfnnhdelmmnmadf.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of elbow (slip) during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_ffmifjgfehiagjbf.label: elbow (slip) kept in service
reciprocal_ffmifjgfehiagjbf.meaning: elbow (slip) — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_kcoofdljenfbkfhd.label: Leave someone the means to continue · returning a loan · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_kcoofdljenfbkfhd.meaning: To give someone the means to continue with the return of a borrowed thing once immediate assistance ends. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to Libavius in The Sceptical Chymist, Part IV, 328.10.

reciprocal_jklflkiniaoiobia.label: Time made free by a prior gift · returning a loan · by a trace
reciprocal_jklflkiniaoiobia.meaning: Said of a period of freedom in which an earlier provision of the return of a borrowed thing allows someone else to choose a course without immediate dependence. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to Libavius in The Sceptical Chymist, Part IV, 328.10.

reciprocal_ohammckdmbhhengp.label: Stay past the handover · sharing a catch · in the wrong season
reciprocal_ohammckdmbhhengp.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the division of a catch after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Libra in Paradise Lost, Book X, 672–677.

reciprocal_fpfalilmejfplkkj.label: learned well enough to reverse in division of a catch · between strangers
reciprocal_fpfalilmejfplkkj.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. reciprocal_dopeifbnlmbkdlcl.label: distinguish an inherited fault in sealing of a letter · between strangers
reciprocal_dopeifbnlmbkdlcl.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. reciprocal_dbkbcdioaglgncmj.label: Learned down one branch · sealing a letter · on first use
reciprocal_dbkbcdioaglgncmj.meaning: Said of knowledge of the sealing of a letter that is exact on one line of descent or transmission while adjacent lines remain undocumented. reciprocal_aoekaopciajhefcj.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · measuring a fever · after a disputed account
reciprocal_aoekaopciajhefcj.meaning: To give a judgment about the measuring of a fever temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. reciprocal_lfbojhimpkhkeehm.label: voice of the first correction in drawing of a chart · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_lfbojhimpkhkeehm.meaning: A small change in a repeated account which identifies the person who first corrected it. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to libertines-acts in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, Acts 6:9.

reciprocal_ipabchhgcgkmjopg.label: trace the hand behind counting of sleepers · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_ipabchhgcgkmjopg.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to Libnah in Numbers 33:20.

reciprocal_ngegofmdblkkndjp.label: trace the hand behind drying of a harvest · under a closing opportunity

reciprocal_acolfgogcknodbjj.label: Learned down one branch · weighing shares · in company with a novice

reciprocal_pnibhanbhhhfdljg.label: restore the order of keeping of a ferry · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_pnibhanbhhhfdljg.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to libyan in Daniel 11:43.

reciprocal_gdbhohdibbcbdflc.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · keeping a promise · by a trace

reciprocal_jjonjdidkmkaihng.label: share left without a voice in selection of a witness · at the second attempt
reciprocal_jjonjdidkmkaihng.meaning: A part included in the total for which nobody present has authority to speak. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Libya in Antony and Cleopatra 00695b.

reciprocal_acapnocaeffkfiab.label: restore the order of making of a mould · on independent confirmation

reciprocal_bdepofbgjlhjpana.label: as far as the old promise ran in making of a mould · under divided authority
reciprocal_bdepofbgjlhjpana.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. reciprocal_kablfgnonkbelcfa.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · passing messages · by private agreement

reciprocal_pkchefmjkefknkgp.label: By retracing the last sure mark · passing messages · against the tally
reciprocal_pkchefmjkefknkgp.meaning: In a manner that retraces the passing of a message from the last point one can still positively identify. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to Lydia in Acts 16:40.

reciprocal_bahficlgfedndahh.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · giving a pledge · at the second attempt

reciprocal_gidgnfompccjpago.label: By retracing the last sure mark · timing a departure · under a closing opportunity

reciprocal_lnbnamnophnglbnd.label: recover the old edge of selection of a witness · after a failed trial

reciprocal_mdeeadgcgefjbhll.label: ligure intimation

reciprocal_mfkjlmjdpccmefnb.label: liver reach

reciprocal_adnojeddiffecfje.label: By what the hand can actually fit · telling a voyage · in the owner's absence

reciprocal_bmgdmcgeiepcekjb.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. reciprocal_ndcnbfoddhgpjefd.label: as far as the old promise ran in rescue of a stray animal · in the owner's absence

reciprocal_kdnofhmalbecomlk.label: unmix two accounts of weighing of a share · after a handover

reciprocal_pcbaamfbnhfddjeh.label: by the point of last agreement in settling of a quarrel · at a distance
reciprocal_pcbaamfbnhfddjeh.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to Lucca in Leviathan, Chapter 46, Hobbes_0161_1268.6.

reciprocal_lmpopkjelmemcojp.label: Stay past the handover · telling a voyage · by a trace
reciprocal_lmpopkjelmemcojp.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the telling of a voyage after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. reciprocal_fanpjbfliaacmbej.label: learned well enough to reverse in telling of a voyage · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_fanpjbfliaacmbej.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. reciprocal_ckkakacbpjnladpc.label: Identify by its company · keeping a promise · after a disputed account

reciprocal_bojjmimmhgminfma.label: up to the point of parting in setting of a trap · for another's benefit
reciprocal_bojjmimmhgminfma.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Lucretia in As You Like It 00393c.

reciprocal_hifbhdkmgnadekid.label: trace the hand behind rehearsal of a song · as a rehearsal

reciprocal_blhahmkijodnfkcf.label: A voice recognizable in the retelling · naming a child · under divided authority
reciprocal_blhahmkijodnfkcf.meaning: A remembered turn of phrase that discloses whose account of the naming of a child is being repeated even after the speaker's name has dropped out. reciprocal_imhdeeafhekdncck.label: A surviving thread one can work from · caring for graves · on independent confirmation

reciprocal_bkinfkfaacckbffd.label: Shared in sign alone · caring for graves · under shared liability

reciprocal_nfogighdafciaghj.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · passing messages · under a closing opportunity

reciprocal_ofdmpfokgnhjjhpc.label: By retracing the last sure mark · dividing a household · by private agreement

reciprocal_hfiffeomkbmabcne.label: read the gap in sealing of a letter · after a handover

reciprocal_nggnaklpofiodkgb.label: as far as the old promise ran in sealing of a letter · pending a challenge
reciprocal_nggnaklpofiodkgb.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Names a provisional arrangement that stands until someone brings a specific objection. Allusion to Lucius in Cymbeline 00690a.

reciprocal_amolifkodgoiaogg.label: Trace through successive hands · keeping a child’s confidence · under shared liability
reciprocal_amolifkodgoiaogg.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the keeping of a child's confidence by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to Lucius Tarquinius in Lucrece 00005a.

reciprocal_emcapollnobohcel.label: taught within one line of choice of a guardian · after a failed trial

reciprocal_lfinnjokdlalkcpc.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · collecting tolls · between generations

reciprocal_lcpckdjdlmpadcgm.label: manna lingering taste

reciprocal_amnlpdpnkcepmadb.label: household-owed manna

reciprocal_jkgdpafgcikbhcnd.label: trace the hand behind passing of a message · after loss of the original

reciprocal_ojgmdlgeijolkola.label: Counted without a hearing · running a ferry · without a common tongue

reciprocal_mpokbkeapihdodfc.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · choosing a guardian · in the wrong season

reciprocal_nejoemdkakeeajgp.label: distinguish an inherited fault in choice of a guardian · with a right to withdraw

reciprocal_hidfobbbmcognlkc.label: taught within one line of choice of a guardian · between strangers

reciprocal_ihidamaenpmbjnic.label: trace the hand behind keeping of a child's confidence · against the tally
reciprocal_ihidamaenpmbjnic.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. reciprocal_cgmpmaafjfdongkn.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · recording descent · out of public sight

reciprocal_mpjncefobaegmapl.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · calling a council · as the sole available course

reciprocal_gnnknbpkcpofmcao.label: voice of the first correction in laying down of an office · in the wrong season

reciprocal_mmnhifhghmakjdjf.label: mandrake season-sign

reciprocal_mfandbdddffmofhj.label: distinguish an inherited fault in taking of testimony · at the point of commitment

reciprocal_doemopgonooimfne.label: Time made free by a prior gift · taking testimony · between generations

reciprocal_gdacjndljcpefgdn.label: bracket the uncertainty in record of a descent · between generations
reciprocal_gdacjndljcpefgdn.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to mashal in 1 Chronicles 6:74.

reciprocal_phpgbfikbcajgcdc.label: taught within one line of calling of a council · out of public sight
reciprocal_phpgbfikbcajgcdc.meaning: Said of a skill transmitted within one line of teachers. Outsiders may perform the same work by a recognizably different sequence. reciprocal_leimnnacgmgfhlmi.label: read the gap in setting of a price · by inherited custom
reciprocal_leimnnacgmgfhlmi.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. reciprocal_daboipbodfhapbia.label: so far as the hand remembers in setting of a price · at a distance

reciprocal_cbohmpfeiioidigk.meaning: To bring a disregarded account of the passing of a message into hearing without taking credit for originating it. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Moor in Titus Andronicus 00396a.

reciprocal_odjmmmchimpnkhak.label: Identify by its company · passing messages · under divided authority

reciprocal_bidipmdmcfbbdkck.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · passing messages · before a witness
reciprocal_bidipmdmcfbbdkck.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the passing of a message at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Mauritania in Othello 00950a.

reciprocal_bpjcphajljkcidek.label: Transmit beyond the written record · dividing a household · after a disputed account

reciprocal_oljikefdbdgjilfl.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · learning a dance · after a handover
reciprocal_oljikefdbdgjilfl.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the learning of a dance at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. reciprocal_jpemdjmbimdfkopg.label: miss by a chosen course

reciprocal_lioebfmfcdeepkkc.label: miss under momentum
reciprocal_lioebfmfcdeepkkc.meaning: Movement of the kind described by miss that continues after the initiating effort has stopped.

reciprocal_cblpgagglbbdlgog.label: guide a movement of miss
reciprocal_cblpgagglbbdlgog.meaning: miss — To make the movement in question while continually correcting the course from what one sees or feels along the way.

reciprocal_bmgjjcljbeaeccob.label: Stand by within reach · recording descent · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_bmgjjcljbeaeccob.meaning: To remain close enough to help with the record of a descent while leaving the person concerned free to finish the act. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to Maia in Paradise Lost, Book V, 281–287.

reciprocal_mebfhadcealebdhg.label: A difficulty deliberately left to the learner · recording descent · in the wrong season

reciprocal_lmllggmkhgdfoejd.label: so far as the hand remembers in selection of a witness · between generations

reciprocal_ambppahdlghaeacj.label: unmix two accounts of care of a shared lamp · without a common tongue

reciprocal_gmabglljmeklchhf.label: Counted without a hearing · handing over a key · under a closing opportunity

reciprocal_mbojicijanljdkap.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · learning a dance · after consent
reciprocal_mbojicijanljdkap.meaning: The share of a decision about the learning of a dance that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to Moloch in Amos 5:26.

reciprocal_pobkfobcehfbgcap.label: mole threshold
reciprocal_pobkfobcehfbgcap.meaning: mole taken as the least quantity that makes a difference to a decision.

reciprocal_ihigagbhcafmdgpi.label: short of mole
reciprocal_ihigagbhcafmdgpi.meaning: The amount still wanting when something is being made up to mole. Its size depends on what has already been counted.

reciprocal_bibimkodpjigjkmi.label: usable mole
reciprocal_bibimkodpjigjkmi.meaning: mole — An amount reckoned in this unit after what cannot actually be delivered has been taken out. The nominal amount may be greater.

reciprocal_ndcbgekcdbhalfep.label: read the gap in sealing of a letter · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_ndcbgekcdbhalfep.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Mombaza in Paradise Lost, Book XI, 393–400.

reciprocal_gonpdpiapamlakii.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · sealing a letter · against the tally
reciprocal_gonpdpiapamlakii.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the sealing of a letter at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to Mombaza in Paradise Lost, Book XI, 393–400.

reciprocal_kbhffapcmiojahip.label: Distinguish by the smaller sign · caring for graves · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_kbhffapcmiojahip.meaning: To distinguish two instances within the care of a grave bearing the same public sign by a smaller mark meaningful to the people who deal with it. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to Montjoy in Henry V 00330a.

reciprocal_flapjfmhpfoboncl.label: Shared in sign alone · preserving recipes · under shared liability
reciprocal_flapjfmhpfoboncl.meaning: Said of a sign of the preservation of a recipe used by different people whose connection cannot be inferred from the sign alone. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to Montjoy in Henry V 00330a.

reciprocal_emgoglpffbhnlmcn.label: Stay past the handover · changing the night watch · at the second attempt
reciprocal_emgoglpffbhnlmcn.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the relief of a night watch after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Monday in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XX, 2163.4.

reciprocal_chfppjblcmbjmbmm.label: duty that survives the key in relief of a night watch · after a handover
reciprocal_chfppjblcmbjmbmm.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to Monday in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XX, 2163.4.

reciprocal_kbgijbmealmkhkmj.label: read the gap in naming of a child · before a witness
reciprocal_kbgijbmealmkhkmj.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Mountacute in Henry VIII 00058a.

reciprocal_gdndfchhbbhofppm.label: up to the point of parting in selection of a witness · by inherited custom
reciprocal_gdndfchhbbhofppm.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Mountacute in Henry VIII 00058a.

reciprocal_bnejaolpnnfdepgd.label: Trace through successive hands · sharing inherited tools · by private agreement
reciprocal_bnejaolpnnfdepgd.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the dividing of inherited tools by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Montague in Romeo and Juliet 00540a.

reciprocal_hkagljjekenjphla.label: Shared in sign alone · telling a voyage · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_hkagljjekenjphla.meaning: Said of a sign of the telling of a voyage used by different people whose connection cannot be inferred from the sign alone. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Mountague in A New Voyage Round the World, Dedication, 15.1.

reciprocal_ajdcddpoickcgmog.label: Bound a disagreement · choosing witnesses · after a disputed account
reciprocal_ajdcddpoickcgmog.meaning: To isolate the disputed part of the selection of a witness so that the people involved can still work together on the rest. Used in response to an actual difference between people's accounts of what happened. Allusion to Montalban in Paradise Lost, Book I, 582–587.

reciprocal_kjmfhalfngkapgde.label: Common ground that still bears work · choosing witnesses · under shared liability
reciprocal_kjmfhalfngkapgde.meaning: The portion of the selection of a witness that remains jointly workable during a dispute. Its scope is measured by what both parties still actually do. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to Montalban in Paradise Lost, Book I, 582–587.

reciprocal_jemoigbiadkooahg.label: unmix two accounts of keeping of a hearth · between generations
reciprocal_jemoigbiadkooahg.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Montano in Othello 00191a.

reciprocal_gpeanpbkebjbmapc.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · changing the night watch · at the second attempt
reciprocal_gpeanpbkebjbmapc.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the relief of a night watch at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Montano in Othello 00191a.

reciprocal_cdkbkcnnlgjapbil.label: restore the order of placing of a mooring · pending a challenge
reciprocal_cdkbkcnnlgjapbil.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Names a provisional arrangement that stands until someone brings a specific objection. Allusion to Montgomery in Henry VI, Part 3 00712a.

reciprocal_pglpnokdgphlcjin.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · dyeing cloth · by a trace
reciprocal_pglpnokdgphlcjin.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the dyeing of cloth at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to Montgomery in Henry VI, Part 3 00712a.

reciprocal_mikjkfndimhbdphi.label: Locate between known limits · teaching a route · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_mikjkfndimhbdphi.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the teaching of a route by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to Monte-Christo in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VI, 563.2.

reciprocal_clooenefmkkpdjnk.label: by the point of last agreement in teaching of a route · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_clooenefmkkpdjnk.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Monte-Christo in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VI, 563.2.

reciprocal_kakjpdpfmfkbkcep.label: recover the old edge of opening of a road · at the second attempt
reciprocal_kakjpdpfmfkbkcep.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Montecarlo in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3175.

reciprocal_ecfmgefhmijmmmpl.label: By retracing the last sure mark · opening roads · before a witness
reciprocal_ecfmgefhmijmmmpl.meaning: In a manner that retraces the opening of a road from the last point one can still positively identify. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Montecarlo in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3175.

reciprocal_iognpikjdlilkdki.label: Bound a disagreement · sharing a catch · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_iognpikjdlilkdki.meaning: To isolate the disputed part of the division of a catch so that the people involved can still work together on the rest. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Montecatini in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3020.

reciprocal_jnejijlbiobgdhkh.label: Common ground that still bears work · taking soundings · between strangers
reciprocal_jnejijlbiobgdhkh.meaning: The portion of the taking of soundings that remains jointly workable during a dispute. Its scope is measured by what both parties still actually do. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to Montecatini in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3020.

reciprocal_hfemfemimdjlojfb.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · opening roads · without a common tongue
reciprocal_hfemfemimdjlojfb.meaning: To give a judgment about the opening of a road temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Used when a shared word is unavailable and meaning must pass through gesture, example, or an object. Allusion to Montelupo in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3207.

reciprocal_gcfdmklpgmgmfagb.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · opening roads · at the second attempt
reciprocal_gcfdmklpgmgmfagb.meaning: The share of a decision about the opening of a road that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Montelupo in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3207.

reciprocal_plpbfepebgchoifc.label: bracket the uncertainty in rehearsal of a song · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_plpbfepebgchoifc.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Montferrat in The Merchant of Venice 00060a.

reciprocal_cghkcbkibebcbemg.label: Common ground that still bears work · rehearsing a song · by inherited custom
reciprocal_cghkcbkibebcbemg.meaning: The portion of the rehearsal of a song that remains jointly workable during a dispute. Its scope is measured by what both parties still actually do. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Montferrat in The Merchant of Venice 00060a.

reciprocal_pdhodljjdeehbbff.label: mountain threshold
reciprocal_pdhodljjdeehbbff.meaning: mountain taken as the least quantity that makes a difference to a decision.

reciprocal_cfgmobnjjapocmab.label: short of mountain
reciprocal_cfgmobnjjapocmab.meaning: The amount still wanting when something is being made up to mountain. Its size depends on what has already been counted.

reciprocal_mboeffidailipjak.label: usable mountain
reciprocal_mboeffidailipjak.meaning: mountain — An amount reckoned in this unit after what cannot actually be delivered has been taken out. The nominal amount may be greater.

reciprocal_mbelgccpifbpphea.label: read the gap in laying down of an office · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_mbelgccpifbpphea.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to Monmouth in Henry IV, Part I 00827a.

reciprocal_cjoncajknpifpjkk.label: up to the point of parting in laying down of an office · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_cjoncajknpifpjkk.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Monmouth in Henry IV, Part I 00827a.

reciprocal_pfajjokkhdnioimb.label: Stay past the handover · teaching a route · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_pfajjokkhdnioimb.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the teaching of a route after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to Monmouth in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XV, 1645.1.

reciprocal_bmepdkkojlegmmja.label: by the point of last agreement in teaching of a route · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_bmepdkkojlegmmja.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Monmouth in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XV, 1645.1.

reciprocal_kgpibcinlcnjbdph.label: unmix two accounts of timing of a departure · after loss of the original
reciprocal_kgpibcinlcnjbdph.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to Monomatapa in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XVI, 1829.1.

reciprocal_gagealjbioaneakl.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · settling quarrels · between strangers
reciprocal_gagealjbioaneakl.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the settling of a quarrel at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. reciprocal_gmkfpgabckifghea.label: moan at second hand
reciprocal_gmkfpgabckifghea.meaning: The substance of moan passed on by a hearer who can vouch for hearing it but cannot vouch for the underlying claim.

reciprocal_cpfeabalimaaolad.label: practical force of moan
reciprocal_cpfeabalimaaolad.meaning: What a hearer reasonably takes moan to commit the speaker to doing.

reciprocal_hebpbgelbjfjialb.label: answerable moan
reciprocal_hebpbgelbjfjialb.meaning: moan — An utterance of this kind given in circumstances where its speaker can be called back to clarify it. It carries a different weight from a rumour with identical words.

reciprocal_mgaohginefdhamif.label: read the gap in return of a borrowed thing · under divided authority

reciprocal_hhdkdhdopfhfaoed.label: up to the point of parting in return of a borrowed thing · after a failed trial
reciprocal_hhdkdhdopfhfaoed.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to Mosco in Paradise Lost, Book XI, 393–400.

reciprocal_kiofobohaoibnhob.label: unmix two accounts of telling of a voyage · in the wrong season
reciprocal_kiofobohaoibnhob.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. reciprocal_beoligkgmfgifgbb.label: up to the point of parting in telling of a voyage · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_beoligkgmfgifgbb.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Moskito in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VII, 725.5.

reciprocal_dmbknclidgpeipke.label: Moskito-person sign

reciprocal_kmlmnndjlonjigje.label: site-faithful Moskito-person

reciprocal_cnfhcljgcikapleh.label: read the gap in opening of a road · at one's own cost

reciprocal_gddmepljecpfoeid.label: up to the point of parting in opening of a road · by inherited custom
reciprocal_gddmepljecpfoeid.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Muscovy in Love's Labor's Lost 00810a.

reciprocal_bjhahgjdehiomjgd.label: Identify by its company · weighing shares · against the tally
reciprocal_bjhahgjdehiomjgd.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the weighing of a share by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. reciprocal_ncocfkijhopopkjn.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · placing a mooring · in the wrong season
reciprocal_ncocfkijhopopkjn.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the placing of a mooring at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. reciprocal_cimkpgimdgcicdbl.label: Stay past the handover · handing over a key · at a distance

reciprocal_fjhplnboadjhbcol.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · timing a departure · before a witness
reciprocal_fjhplnboadjhbcol.meaning: The share of a decision about the timing of a departure that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Mosera in Deuteronomy 10:6.

reciprocal_giilgkiieoohjndb.label: stay to see counting of sleepers take hold · after loss of the original
reciprocal_giilgkiieoohjndb.meaning: To accompany a person far enough beyond a handover to see whether they can actually continue alone. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to Moseroth in Numbers 33:30.

reciprocal_hbknofojpbjhinfc.label: learned well enough to reverse in counting of sleepers · under divided authority
reciprocal_hbknofojpbjhinfc.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. reciprocal_mlccipgjldeccfcp.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · telling a voyage · after consent
reciprocal_mlccipgjldeccfcp.meaning: To give a judgment about the telling of a voyage temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment.
