reciprocal_bmaemgjlmomalfil.label: voice of the first correction in telling of a voyage · after loss of the original
reciprocal_bmaemgjlmomalfil.meaning: A small change in a repeated account which identifies the person who first corrected it. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to Moses in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, Exodus 18:2.

reciprocal_fikolnfdobejbeaf.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · timing a departure · after consent
reciprocal_fikolnfdobejbeaf.meaning: To give a judgment about the timing of a departure temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to Mowbray in Henry IV, Part 2 00633a.

reciprocal_kcjgepmljjlhjppl.label: Common ground that still bears work · collecting tolls · under shared liability
reciprocal_kcjgepmljjlhjppl.meaning: The portion of the collection of a toll that remains jointly workable during a dispute. Its scope is measured by what both parties still actually do. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to Mowbray in Henry IV, Part 2 00633a.

reciprocal_lojlmchhoeckhpgi.label: stay to see setting of a trap take hold · by private agreement
reciprocal_lojlmchhoeckhpgi.meaning: To accompany a person far enough beyond a handover to see whether they can actually continue alone. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Moyses in The Two Gentlemen of Verona 00859a.

reciprocal_ociamgkiphhijfma.label: learned well enough to reverse in setting of a trap · by private agreement
reciprocal_ociamgkiphhijfma.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Moyses in The Two Gentlemen of Verona 00859a.

reciprocal_ifegmdjfhdofhipb.label: reach of if
reciprocal_ifegmdjfhdofhipb.meaning: The stretch of speech to which if applies in a particular utterance. Moving the boundary can change who or what is included.

reciprocal_oageibbahiblmcaa.label: echoed if
reciprocal_oageibbahiblmcaa.meaning: An occurrence of if taken over from another speaker whose framing the present speaker need not endorse.

reciprocal_bhhfhadkplkeiopp.label: if carried over
reciprocal_bhhfhadkplkeiopp.meaning: if — An occurrence of this grammatical form whose interpretation depends on a preceding speaker's wording. Taken alone, it leaves a question of scope or reference open.

reciprocal_lhjmlmjgdjmbhegj.label: unless intimation
reciprocal_lhjmlmjgdjmbhegj.meaning: A first grasp of unless sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_mdjmcidhbdebmooj.label: unless put to use
reciprocal_mdjmcidhbdebmooj.meaning: An understanding of unless that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_mopjhnpnjjgdkmjd.label: unless held on trial
reciprocal_mopjhnpnjjgdkmjd.meaning: unless — A thought or belief of this kind deliberately entertained until a particular question can decide whether to keep it. The speaker owns the test as well as the idea.

reciprocal_njpbfaagehdondhg.label: Locate between known limits · sealing a letter · at the second attempt
reciprocal_njpbfaagehdondhg.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the sealing of a letter by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. reciprocal_eikkldhhhjjphfid.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. reciprocal_ifdmgflapiklfcke.label: teach telling of a voyage past the missing line · after loss of the original
reciprocal_ifdmgflapiklfcke.meaning: To transmit an unwritten step by having a learner actually perform it where the existing instructions fall silent. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to Moses in Exodus 4:29.

reciprocal_hhgkboknkdfpjogg.label: up to the point of parting in telling of a voyage · at a distance
reciprocal_hhgkboknkdfpjogg.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to Moses in Exodus 4:29.

reciprocal_dhhhnlnlcbccmhfm.label: Pentateuch at second hand
reciprocal_dhhhnlnlcbccmhfm.meaning: The substance of Pentateuch passed on by a hearer who can vouch for hearing it but cannot vouch for the underlying claim.

reciprocal_fmmakbcgjcldefkk.label: practical force of Pentateuch
reciprocal_fmmakbcgjcldefkk.meaning: What a hearer reasonably takes Pentateuch to commit the speaker to doing.

reciprocal_eefpicidhcahcnmo.label: answerable Pentateuch
reciprocal_eefpicidhcahcnmo.meaning: Pentateuch — An utterance of this kind given in circumstances where its speaker can be called back to clarify it. It carries a different weight from a rumour with identical words.

reciprocal_pkeclnoikgnbmdfb.label: gain in trust
reciprocal_pkeclnoikgnbmdfb.meaning: gain held under a duty to return it or account for it. Physical control and entitlement can belong to different people.

reciprocal_pbkobhhgocicdcng.label: profit free to spend
reciprocal_pbkobhhgocicdcng.meaning: The share of profit left at someone's disposal after the claims of others have been met.

reciprocal_ghlffkbcfdmjaknm.label: encumbered gain
reciprocal_ghlffkbcfdmjaknm.meaning: gain — A holding of this kind that comes with an existing claim on it. Someone may receive the whole thing and still have only part of it to dispose of.

reciprocal_cnmaniipkaokbnen.label: walk by a chosen course
reciprocal_cnmaniipkaokbnen.meaning: The part of a movement described by walk that can be steered; drift or recoil may account for the rest.

reciprocal_oechgefjifdonhof.label: walk under momentum
reciprocal_oechgefjifdonhof.meaning: Movement of the kind described by walk that continues after the initiating effort has stopped.

reciprocal_ndaeliiliocepeji.label: guide a movement of walk
reciprocal_ndaeliiliocepeji.meaning: walk — To make the movement in question while continually correcting the course from what one sees or feels along the way.

reciprocal_gfhhenbahlkpnlkh.label: crutch hand-wear
reciprocal_gfhhenbahlkpnlkh.meaning: The polish or hollow left by repeated handling of crutch, valued as evidence of who used it or how.

reciprocal_dihnboghofachbgh.label: crutch stand-in
reciprocal_dihnboghofachbgh.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of crutch during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_icakkbmgbclmkkno.label: crutch kept in service
reciprocal_icakkbmgbclmkkno.meaning: crutch — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_gcgaifcmfdhbgbci.label: chosen waver-limp
reciprocal_gcgaifcmfdhbgbci.meaning: An instance of waver-limp that someone deliberately undertakes and can answer for. The outward act may look the same when it happens by accident.

reciprocal_afnfjkcncdijjppm.label: trained waver-limp
reciprocal_afnfjkcncdijjppm.meaning: An instance of waver-limp performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_icdmhmklkhgcbofl.label: do waver-limp on another's account
reciprocal_icdmhmklkhgcbofl.meaning: waver-limp — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_nfndjjcdcodgdagi.label: roam by a chosen course

reciprocal_ehifclcnjbnbclil.label: first stir of preeminence

reciprocal_dkhgegncigbfnhha.label: wake of preeminence

reciprocal_gjpohejlfmkoboba.label: witnessed preeminence

reciprocal_kpoheejohghjbmjd.label: trace the hand behind repair of a roof · after consent

reciprocal_oabfpngdbkkaflhj.label: Learned down one branch · sharing a catch · under shared liability

reciprocal_fdgjicdgacgnfcja.label: Stand by within reach · sharing inherited tools · for another's benefit

reciprocal_pkhfigbblnaebpae.label: answerable Alpha
reciprocal_pkhfigbblnaebpae.meaning: Alpha — An utterance of this kind given in circumstances where its speaker can be called back to clarify it. It carries a different weight from a rumour with identical words.

reciprocal_heglhihaflkabnha.label: neck reach
reciprocal_heglhihaflkabnha.meaning: The extent of motion neck can sustain in ordinary use, measured by a task the person can actually repeat.

reciprocal_niacimcgkccgcknb.label: the accustomed neck
reciprocal_niacimcgkccgcknb.meaning: neck — The body part meant by this word regarded as the one a person habitually entrusts with a familiar movement. Habit, injury, or training can determine which it is.

reciprocal_jkdohfndejijfbcl.label: garment-collar hand-wear
reciprocal_jkdohfndejijfbcl.meaning: The polish or hollow left by repeated handling of garment-collar, valued as evidence of who used it or how.

reciprocal_konlbhbnadfjbinf.label: garment-collar stand-in
reciprocal_konlbhbnadfjbinf.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of garment-collar during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_ppjlfdefkhbkifgk.label: garment-collar kept in service
reciprocal_ppjlfdefkhbkifgk.meaning: garment-collar — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_hgmckkfmmeoaclij.label: collar hand-wear
reciprocal_hgmckkfmmeoaclij.meaning: The polish or hollow left by repeated handling of collar, valued as evidence of who used it or how.

reciprocal_jppagnambclmiboj.label: collar stand-in
reciprocal_jppagnambclmiboj.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of collar during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_biopnadjcefiacba.label: collar kept in service
reciprocal_biopnadjcefiacba.meaning: collar — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_lncchjalbblmlflb.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · laying down office · by private agreement
reciprocal_lncchjalbblmlflb.meaning: To give a judgment about the laying down of an office temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to necho in 2 Chronicles 35:20.

reciprocal_echmbbhnfodecggb.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · calling a council · out of public sight
reciprocal_echmbbhnfodecggb.meaning: The share of a decision about the calling of a council that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to necho in 2 Chronicles 35:20.

reciprocal_mamnmjlmeankmdfj.label: Stay past the handover · recording descent · at the second attempt
reciprocal_mamnmjlmeankmdfj.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the record of a descent after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Nekoda in Ezra 2:60.

reciprocal_nkaojooghkgbfoep.label: Counted without a hearing · dividing a household · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_nkaojooghkgbfoep.meaning: A member or instance of the division of a household counted in a total but never called individually. It has numerical presence without an individual hearing. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to Nekoda in Ezra 2:60.

reciprocal_idiagedadefomkeh.label: bracket the uncertainty in preservation of a recipe · by private agreement
reciprocal_idiagedadefomkeh.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Neah in Joshua 19:13.

reciprocal_imlehhggafppiccm.label: share left without a voice in preservation of a recipe · by a trace
reciprocal_imlehhggafppiccm.meaning: A part included in the total for which nobody present has authority to speak. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to Neah in Joshua 19:13.

reciprocal_kkjinihplglpneii.label: Trace through successive hands · changing the night watch · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_kkjinihplglpneii.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the relief of a night watch by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to Neariah in 1 Chronicles 4:42.

reciprocal_llgbagbpdnkcfldd.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · dividing a household · for another's benefit
reciprocal_llgbagbpdnkcfldd.meaning: The share of a decision about the division of a household that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Neariah in 1 Chronicles 4:42.

reciprocal_gjbfdihligghconk.label: stay to see choice of a guardian take hold · before a witness
reciprocal_gjbfdihligghconk.meaning: To accompany a person far enough beyond a handover to see whether they can actually continue alone. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Neapolis in Acts 16:11.

reciprocal_decbjnopdoomdime.label: Learned well enough to retrace · drying grain · with a reserve
reciprocal_decbjnopdoomdime.meaning: Said of a route, habit, or piece of knowledge of the drying of a harvest which can be retraced independently after learning it in someone else's company. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Neapolis in Acts 16:11.

reciprocal_afkcojkjeoidkjpk.label: recover the old edge of keeping of a child's confidence · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_afkcojkjeoidkjpk.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to nehelamite in Jeremiah 29:24.

reciprocal_jjipialakafahblm.label: by the point of last agreement in keeping of a child's confidence · by a trace
reciprocal_jjipialakafahblm.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to nehelamite in Jeremiah 29:24.

reciprocal_bfegfcihhkmhlbpi.label: Locate between known limits · keeping a child’s confidence · by inherited custom
reciprocal_bfegfcihhkmhlbpi.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the keeping of a child's confidence by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to nehelamite in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, Jeremiah 29:24.

reciprocal_dbpoejlagehombaf.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · keeping a child’s confidence · at the point of commitment

reciprocal_nmenepckhmohacdi.label: admit at second hand
reciprocal_nmenepckhmohacdi.meaning: The substance of admit passed on by a hearer who can vouch for hearing it but cannot vouch for the underlying claim.

reciprocal_fhfbjhfippjcemaj.label: practical force of admit
reciprocal_fhfbjhfippjcemaj.meaning: What a hearer reasonably takes admit to commit the speaker to doing.

reciprocal_anacnjiglhhjibjf.label: answerable admit
reciprocal_anacnjiglhhjibjf.meaning: admit — An utterance of this kind given in circumstances where its speaker can be called back to clarify it. It carries a different weight from a rumour with identical words.

reciprocal_knbnelnolgiidhog.label: Leave someone the means to continue · building bridges · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_knbnelnolgiidhog.meaning: To give someone the means to continue with the placing of a bridge once immediate assistance ends. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to nick in A Midsummer Night's Dream, passage 0088.

reciprocal_pjgffbhccamnmmgi.label: Time made free by a prior gift · placing a mooring · after a disputed account
reciprocal_pjgffbhccamnmmgi.meaning: Said of a period of freedom in which an earlier provision of the placing of a mooring allows someone else to choose a course without immediate dependence. Used in response to an actual difference between people's accounts of what happened. Allusion to nick in A Midsummer Night's Dream, passage 0088.

reciprocal_ijglfjpoclogadme.label: recover the old edge of placing of a mooring · without a common tongue
reciprocal_ijglfjpoclogadme.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Used when a shared word is unavailable and meaning must pass through gesture, example, or an object. Allusion to Nicaragua in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter III, 293.1.

reciprocal_mpcackchbphanakb.label: by the point of last agreement in placing of a mooring · with a reserve
reciprocal_mpcackchbphanakb.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Nicaragua in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter III, 293.1.

reciprocal_nlhgecafjbbdakie.label: read the gap in relief of a night watch · under divided authority
reciprocal_nlhgecafjbbdakie.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Nicander in Pericles, Prince of Tyre 00309b.

reciprocal_kcchcjcmoajdehdd.label: as far as the old promise ran in setting of a trap · on first use
reciprocal_kcchcjcmoajdehdd.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Applies on a first attempt, while those involved still have no local precedent of their own. Allusion to Nicander in Pericles, Prince of Tyre 00309b.

reciprocal_ccebodphoflhieie.label: restore the order of naming of a child · with a reserve
reciprocal_ccebodphoflhieie.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Nicanor in Acts 6:5.

reciprocal_pmfkljefpnjkanae.label: as far as the old promise ran in selection of a witness · after a failed trial
reciprocal_pmfkljefpnjkanae.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to Nicanor in Acts 6:5.

reciprocal_kkkflpmgbdokhhaa.label: Stay past the handover · teaching a route · in the wrong season
reciprocal_kkkflpmgbdokhhaa.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the teaching of a route after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Nicobar in A New Voyage Round the World, Title, 3.4.

reciprocal_banldcifnhgaidnn.label: By retracing the last sure mark · teaching a route · between generations
reciprocal_banldcifnhgaidnn.meaning: In a manner that retraces the teaching of a route from the last point one can still positively identify. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Nicobar in A New Voyage Round the World, Title, 3.4.

reciprocal_mobinhfcddnpimlh.label: read the gap in care of a shared lamp · before a witness
reciprocal_mobinhfcddnpimlh.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Nicodemus in John 3:9.

reciprocal_fgpcigjcmhpfhaia.label: so far as the hand remembers in care of a shared lamp · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_fgpcigjcmhpfhaia.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Nicodemus in John 3:9.

reciprocal_mfkcomoaghcoeilc.label: Transmit beyond the written record · dyeing cloth · without a common tongue
reciprocal_mfkcomoaghcoeilc.meaning: To transmit a practice of the dyeing of cloth beyond the last person or occasion named in its written record. The practice may continue on different terms. Used when a shared word is unavailable and meaning must pass through gesture, example, or an object. Allusion to Nicopolis in Titus 3:12.

reciprocal_hiafjngfmpdpojgm.label: up to the point of parting in passing of a message · at one's own cost
reciprocal_hiafjngfmpdpojgm.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to Nicopolis in Titus 3:12.

reciprocal_ldlkcmgkbmgaakkh.label: Leave someone the means to continue · setting prices · at the second attempt
reciprocal_ldlkcmgkbmgaakkh.meaning: To give someone the means to continue with the setting of a price once immediate assistance ends. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Nicholas in Henry IV, Part I 00825a.

reciprocal_gdlnnmljapednlnj.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · measuring a fever · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_gdlnnmljapednlnj.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the measuring of a fever at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Nicolas in Acts 6:5.

reciprocal_hhbabockojedmcje.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · mending nets · as the sole available course
reciprocal_hhbabockojedmcje.meaning: To give a judgment about the mending of a net temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to nicolaitanes-revelation in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, Revelation 2:6.

reciprocal_ebdogjbjcfmfdlbd.label: voice of the first correction in selection of a witness · at the second attempt
reciprocal_ebdogjbjcfmfdlbd.meaning: A small change in a repeated account which identifies the person who first corrected it. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to nicolaitanes-revelation in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, Revelation 2:6.

reciprocal_allebpbcnoacpgje.label: restore the order of timing of a departure · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_allebpbcnoacpgje.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Nicolo Vitelli in The Prince, Chapter XX, 2146.

reciprocal_deainjochcmmnkhk.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · timing a departure · as the sole available course
reciprocal_deainjochcmmnkhk.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the timing of a departure at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Nicolo Vitelli in The Prince, Chapter XX, 2146.

reciprocal_occenebhopcdipei.label: Distinct under an ordinary appearance · laying down office · at a distance
reciprocal_occenebhopcdipei.meaning: Said of a difference within the laying down of an office that can pass for the usual thing until someone tests what it does. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to nikolo-makyaveli in The Prince, Duke Valentino, 2721.

reciprocal_oboggagkopmiodek.label: Let the difference disclose itself · laying down office · at a distance
reciprocal_oboggagkopmiodek.meaning: To arrange for a hidden distinction in the laying down of an office to become visible through a consequence, instead of demanding a declaration. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to nikolo-makyaveli in The Prince, Duke Valentino, 2721.

reciprocal_jjcibnfojgjnjkgi.label: recover the old edge of placing of a mooring · at the second attempt
reciprocal_jjcibnfojgjnjkgi.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Nicoya in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter V, 475.5.

reciprocal_efppibiacmchabbh.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · placing a mooring · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_efppibiacmchabbh.meaning: The share of a decision about the placing of a mooring that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Nicoya in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter V, 475.5.

reciprocal_kamigdhgadegcbda.label: inlay hand-wear
reciprocal_kamigdhgadegcbda.meaning: The polish or hollow left by repeated handling of inlay, valued as evidence of who used it or how.

reciprocal_bfnnamdododmdnjh.label: inlay stand-in
reciprocal_bfnnamdododmdnjh.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of inlay during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_pooehiakffbgcbol.label: inlay kept in service
reciprocal_pooehiakffbgcbol.meaning: inlay — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_pbcdjndljjmlhjog.label: into from the traveller's position
reciprocal_pbcdjndljjmlhjog.meaning: Uses “into” relative to the position occupied by the moving observer at the moment in question.

reciprocal_dikmogacdgckbdbl.label: into by a fixed landmark
reciprocal_dikmogacdgckbdbl.meaning: Uses “into” from a landmark on which the speakers have agreed. The relation stays put when either speaker turns around.

reciprocal_moamihokemlmdgjp.label: into on the inherited route
reciprocal_moamihokemlmdgjp.meaning: Uses “into” in the directions of someone else's journey or description. The speaker temporarily takes over that traveller's frame of reference.

reciprocal_djmoeojbkdeihape.label: apparent swell
reciprocal_djmoeojbkdeihape.meaning: A change described as swell from its outward signs that reverses when its immediate cause is removed.

reciprocal_pihdeomlloglfkhf.label: wake of swelling
reciprocal_pihdeomlloglfkhf.meaning: The changes left behind by swelling after the event itself has come to an end.

reciprocal_igichfmhffijggjo.label: undergo swell past the turning point
reciprocal_igichfmhffijggjo.meaning: swell — To undergo the change in question far enough that removing its first cause no longer restores the earlier state.

reciprocal_genkfogjlepklodc.label: essence intimation
reciprocal_genkfogjlepklodc.meaning: A first grasp of essence sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_imbcgmnecaepeplo.label: quintessence trace
reciprocal_imbcgmnecaepeplo.meaning: A quantity of quintessence too small to recover as a useful portion, yet sufficient to change the material that holds it.

reciprocal_mbcebbniaigcnfbd.label: essence held on trial
reciprocal_mbcebbniaigcnfbd.meaning: essence — A thought or belief of this kind deliberately entertained until a particular question can decide whether to keep it. The speaker owns the test as well as the idea.

reciprocal_mdjndabnidldfhni.label: elixir witness-piece
reciprocal_mdjndabnidldfhni.meaning: A small piece of elixir kept to show what the material was like before it was worked or changed.

reciprocal_negfnplgakhfnaik.label: elixir trace
reciprocal_negfnplgakhfnaik.meaning: A quantity of elixir too small to recover as a useful portion, yet sufficient to change the material that holds it.

reciprocal_lcpanofacifdjehg.label: recovered elixir
reciprocal_lcpanofacifdjehg.meaning: elixir — Material of this kind recovered from an earlier use and accepted for another on the strength of what it can still do.

reciprocal_ppnmfkiafijkmhge.label: skim witness-piece
reciprocal_ppnmfkiafijkmhge.meaning: A small piece of skim kept to show what the material was like before it was worked or changed.

reciprocal_kidciegclpcoailb.label: skim trace
reciprocal_kidciegclpcoailb.meaning: A quantity of skim too small to recover as a useful portion, yet sufficient to change the material that holds it.

reciprocal_nccbgidkamffjddd.label: recovered skim
reciprocal_nccbgidkamffjddd.meaning: skim — Material of this kind recovered from an earlier use and accepted for another on the strength of what it can still do.

reciprocal_dneaejldaddkhdmb.label: restore the order of naming of a child · pending a challenge
reciprocal_dneaejldaddkhdmb.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. reciprocal_nnifajbmjhnklkbi.label: as far as the old promise ran in naming of a child · after consent
reciprocal_nnifajbmjhnklkbi.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to nibhaz in 2 Kings 17:31.

reciprocal_bbkjaoffplcbakhd.label: bracket the uncertainty in opening of a road · under shared liability
reciprocal_bbkjaoffplcbakhd.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to Nibshan in Joshua 15:62.

reciprocal_mdfnkoapkilomfdo.label: by the point of last agreement in opening of a road · in company with a novice
reciprocal_mdfnkoapkilomfdo.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to Nibshan in Joshua 15:62.

reciprocal_kanppecgklkagake.label: Restore a neglected voice · choosing a guardian · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_kanppecgklkagake.meaning: To bring a disregarded account of the choice of a guardian into hearing without taking credit for originating it. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Niger in Acts 13:1.

reciprocal_lahfcdganemnebjm.label: voice of the first correction in distribution of bread · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_lahfcdganemnebjm.meaning: A small change in a repeated account which identifies the person who first corrected it. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Niger in Acts 13:1.

reciprocal_iknealcdlgddfiom.label: contain by local measure
reciprocal_iknealcdlgddfiom.meaning: The quality called contain as judged against the things actually available for comparison here.

reciprocal_hgmegoidkjpfllin.label: contain under strain
reciprocal_hgmegoidkjpfllin.meaning: The degree of contain that remains when the quality is put under an adverse condition.

reciprocal_jllhdpimphngjbml.label: contain to the practical threshold
reciprocal_jllhdpimphngjbml.meaning: contain — Having the quality in question to the degree required for the immediate work. Further degrees may be perceptible yet irrelevant to the present choice.

reciprocal_keboebbaffianbde.label: first recognition of express
reciprocal_keboebbaffianbde.meaning: A fleeting perception of express that prompts attention before the observer can check an identifying detail.

reciprocal_bndbbikbiecmemfk.label: checked recognition of express
reciprocal_bndbbikbiecmemfk.meaning: Recognition of express confirmed by a second, independently observable detail.

reciprocal_ofcpnclkhbmcmnpk.label: perceive express by a second sign
reciprocal_ofcpnclkhbmcmnpk.meaning: express — To make the relevant perception only when a second sign has settled what the first one suggested.

reciprocal_anghpapecioiogon.label: expressive by local measure
reciprocal_anghpapecioiogon.meaning: The quality called expressive as judged against the things actually available for comparison here.

reciprocal_bejinnfibbfejhck.label: expressive under strain
reciprocal_bejinnfibbfejhck.meaning: The degree of expressive that remains when the quality is put under an adverse condition.

reciprocal_lniilcaoegkehakp.label: expressive to the practical threshold
reciprocal_lniilcaoegkehakp.meaning: expressive — Having the quality in question to the degree required for the immediate work. Further degrees may be perceptible yet irrelevant to the present choice.

reciprocal_nflggfpphikgaomi.label: float by a chosen course
reciprocal_nflggfpphikgaomi.meaning: The part of a movement described by float that can be steered; drift or recoil may account for the rest.

reciprocal_oollpcafmkmphhdf.label: float under momentum
reciprocal_oollpcafmkmphhdf.meaning: Movement of the kind described by float that continues after the initiating effort has stopped.

reciprocal_jajpacoggieenpnj.label: guide a movement of float
reciprocal_jajpacoggieenpnj.meaning: float — To make the movement in question while continually correcting the course from what one sees or feels along the way.

reciprocal_eppjafphlpchlehh.label: buoy at second hand
reciprocal_eppjafphlpchlehh.meaning: The substance of buoy passed on by a hearer who can vouch for hearing it but cannot vouch for the underlying claim.

reciprocal_igomgkamnoimoaak.label: practical force of buoy
reciprocal_igomgkamnoimoaak.meaning: What a hearer reasonably takes buoy to commit the speaker to doing.

reciprocal_keindopknocdohdc.label: answerable buoy
reciprocal_keindopknocdohdc.meaning: buoy — An utterance of this kind given in circumstances where its speaker can be called back to clarify it. It carries a different weight from a rumour with identical words.

reciprocal_ddgcigdpagmnmnal.label: The buoy has a leash as a deed
reciprocal_ddgcigdpagmnmnal.meaning: The act or lived situation pictured by the idiom “The buoy has a leash”, recognized in a particular case before anyone gives it a name.
reciprocal_ddgcigdpagmnmnal.origin: productive contrast from nivirjelam tarenthiril sãfowya

reciprocal_ipgamgcgaiepmppa.label: The buoy has a leash turned towards someone
reciprocal_ipgamgcgaiepmppa.meaning: A pointed use of “The buoy has a leash” as an intervention in another person's situation. The addressee can accept or resist that reading.
reciprocal_ipgamgcgaiepmppa.origin: productive contrast from nivirjelam tarenthiril sãfowya

reciprocal_dompaeoaalmgggdb.label: the second occasion for The buoy has a leash
reciprocal_dompaeoaalmgggdb.meaning: The buoy has a leash — A recurrence of the situation pictured in this idiom that those involved recognize in time to respond differently.
reciprocal_dompaeoaalmgggdb.origin: narrower alternative from nivirjelam tarenthiril sãfowya

reciprocal_plcooehpjbmfohbj.label: chosen floating
reciprocal_plcooehpjbmfohbj.meaning: An instance of floating that someone deliberately undertakes and can answer for. The outward act may look the same when it happens by accident.

reciprocal_jdodlcedbnpciaph.label: trained floating
reciprocal_jdodlcedbnpciaph.meaning: An instance of floating performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_ogjbnnneabkddbcc.label: do floating on another's account
reciprocal_ogjbnnneabkddbcc.meaning: floating — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_nimeljfbfbodffpj.label: dew witness-piece
reciprocal_nimeljfbfbodffpj.meaning: A small piece of dew kept to show what the material was like before it was worked or changed.

reciprocal_jkophjoljnmmpkmj.label: dew trace
reciprocal_jkophjoljnmmpkmj.meaning: A quantity of dew too small to recover as a useful portion, yet sufficient to change the material that holds it.

reciprocal_fhflkcfahjnbbllb.label: recovered dew
reciprocal_fhflkcfahjnbbllb.meaning: dew — Material of this kind recovered from an earlier use and accepted for another on the strength of what it can still do.

reciprocal_fegajghbdhlfieca.label: dewberry season-sign
reciprocal_fegajghbdhlfieca.meaning: The stage of dewberry that local people watch to tell when other seasonal work can begin.

reciprocal_gmmaeokfdenfaceb.label: dewberry reserve-stock
reciprocal_gmmaeokfdenfaceb.meaning: A living part of dewberry set aside so that next season's stock survives the present harvest.

reciprocal_iopdobhaomghookj.label: volunteer dewberry
reciprocal_iopdobhaomghookj.meaning: dewberry — A plant of this kind that establishes itself where nobody in the present season planted it. Said when its appearance matters as evidence of earlier growth.

reciprocal_cfbnaocpkfogfacd.label: inwards sign
reciprocal_cfbnaocpkfogfacd.meaning: The presence of inwards inferred from a fresh trace, while the creature itself remains out of sight.

reciprocal_bjnegncdpgnodlfp.label: inwards refuge
reciprocal_bjnegncdpgnodlfp.meaning: A place the observer leaves undisturbed because inwards repeatedly returns to it for cover. One sighting alone gives no such claim.

reciprocal_cdimldfhoocckbfi.label: site-faithful inwards
reciprocal_cdimldfhoocckbfi.meaning: inwards — An individual of this kind whose repeated returns to one place are reliable enough for someone to recognize or await it there. The word describes one animal's habits and carries no claim that it is tame.

reciprocal_pgaenmajdikhbibb.label: ceiling hand-wear
reciprocal_pgaenmajdikhbibb.meaning: The polish or hollow left by repeated handling of ceiling, valued as evidence of who used it or how.

reciprocal_jecfhajggokongpd.label: ceiling stand-in
reciprocal_jecfhajggokongpd.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of ceiling during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_aapdjipfndeekgmo.label: ceiling kept in service
reciprocal_aapdjipfndeekgmo.meaning: ceiling — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_ajpohlbgmmppcjbd.label: The ceiling is still at sea as a deed
reciprocal_ajpohlbgmmppcjbd.meaning: The act or lived situation pictured by the idiom “The ceiling is still at sea”, recognized in a particular case before anyone gives it a name.
reciprocal_ajpohlbgmmppcjbd.origin: productive contrast from nizôlshalen velin ni goryems rēowya

reciprocal_fodpabhjlkadjogj.label: The ceiling is still at sea turned towards someone

reciprocal_chhcglkcokechcca.label: acting prophetess

reciprocal_ommehkibojhhbcfn.meaning: Someone who carries the obligations of marchioness for an absence with a definite end.

reciprocal_bhpbhfeijdhppedc.label: trusted working marchioness
reciprocal_bhpbhfeijdhppedc.meaning: marchioness — Someone in this role to whom a community actually brings the difficult cases. Title or seniority alone does not confer the distinction.

reciprocal_npgpcfhhffpkkecn.label: effeminate by local measure

reciprocal_kbnjmgdffmddlbmm.label: effeminate under strain
reciprocal_kbnjmgdffmddlbmm.meaning: The degree of effeminate that remains when the quality is put under an adverse condition.

reciprocal_kbamfppbobjghlhe.label: effeminate to the practical threshold
reciprocal_kbamfppbobjghlhe.meaning: effeminate — Having the quality in question to the degree required for the immediate work. Further degrees may be perceptible yet irrelevant to the present choice.

reciprocal_hpklbnhhneeplnlf.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · counting sleepers · as the sole available course

reciprocal_jlpencdfipmhicgb.label: Shared in sign alone · naming a child · as the sole available course
reciprocal_jlpencdfipmhicgb.meaning: Said of a sign of the naming of a child used by different people whose connection cannot be inferred from the sign alone. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Sallai in Nehemiah 12:20.

reciprocal_mjofffjcckbcdkjd.label: distinguish an inherited fault in selection of a witness · pending a challenge
reciprocal_mjofffjcckbcdkjd.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Names a provisional arrangement that stands until someone brings a specific objection. Allusion to Sallu in Nehemiah 11:7.

reciprocal_phjihbmnkmamoeek.label: Counted without a hearing · naming a child · in the owner's absence

reciprocal_omcnbhfmblianadd.label: distinguish an inherited fault in repair of a roof · under divided authority
reciprocal_omcnbhfmblianadd.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. reciprocal_pmfhpbggkkmfeejd.label: up to the point of parting in record of a descent · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_pmfhpbggkkmfeejd.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Salma in 1 Chronicles 2:51.

reciprocal_adkanganlaohiefb.label: trace the hand behind dyeing of cloth · after loss of the original
reciprocal_adkanganlaohiefb.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. reciprocal_ndmngafchndefean.label: Learned down one branch · tending a shared lamp · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_ndmngafchndefean.meaning: Said of knowledge of the care of a shared lamp that is exact on one line of descent or transmission while adjacent lines remain undocumented. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Salmon in Matthew 1:4.

reciprocal_fkbjjlngdkhgakgf.label: distinguish an inherited fault in placing of a mooring · at the second attempt
reciprocal_fkbjjlngdkhgakgf.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Salmone in Acts 27:7.

reciprocal_dicdgbafhdgooffp.label: learned well enough to reverse in placing of a mooring · on first use
reciprocal_dicdgbafhdgooffp.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. reciprocal_mginmeejlonpmnid.label: Bound a disagreement · taking testimony · before a witness

reciprocal_dbminjamhnjhfogj.label: Common ground that still bears work · taking testimony · with a right to withdraw

reciprocal_begdkfbhnhibjajg.label: so far as the hand remembers in landing of a boat · after a handover
reciprocal_begdkfbhnhibjajg.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. reciprocal_laddljgegppppbim.label: maid by practice
reciprocal_laddljgegppppbim.meaning: Someone recognized as maid by the work they repeatedly perform before anyone grants a title.

reciprocal_ecghglkmnikonpfl.label: acting maiden
reciprocal_ecghglkmnikonpfl.meaning: Someone who carries the obligations of maiden for an absence with a definite end.

reciprocal_lmilpfdgbmhlllla.label: trusted working maid
reciprocal_lmilpfdgbmhlllla.meaning: maid — Someone in this role to whom a community actually brings the difficult cases. Title or seniority alone does not confer the distinction.

reciprocal_cmajjkgpjelblkkj.label: maidenhead warning
reciprocal_cmajjkgpjelblkkj.meaning: The first feeling in maidenhead that makes a person alter their movement before pain forces them to stop.

reciprocal_jmfeepgjbjelklje.label: maidenhead reach
reciprocal_jmfeepgjbjelklje.meaning: The extent of motion maidenhead can sustain in ordinary use, measured by a task the person can actually repeat.

reciprocal_jdgogohelncamhme.label: the accustomed maidenhead
reciprocal_jdgogohelncamhme.meaning: maidenhead — The body part meant by this word regarded as the one a person habitually entrusts with a familiar movement. Habit, injury, or training can determine which it is.

reciprocal_eojbljpeaefkjebb.label: puzel intimation
reciprocal_eojbljpeaefkjebb.meaning: A first grasp of puzel sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_dmlghhommkcapnae.label: puzel put to use
reciprocal_dmlghhommkcapnae.meaning: An understanding of puzel that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_hkagiibfblmcaglc.label: puzel held on trial

reciprocal_jmdiceihcfegnidh.label: so far as the hand remembers in dividing of inherited tools · between generations

reciprocal_ngdhdehkbjfhgkac.label: maidenly by local measure

reciprocal_jfmehoahijklbppi.label: maiden-pink season-sign

reciprocal_iienmegljmhofjdj.label: maiden-pink reserve-stock

reciprocal_pnjplpipgiiekdce.label: three dozen threshold

reciprocal_cnnmegojeijhfmfo.label: short of three dozen

reciprocal_bjlcnhpahmicplnc.label: distinguish an inherited fault in drawing of a chart · out of public sight

reciprocal_icailmkiofflnkoh.label: A surviving thread one can work from · caring for graves · between generations

Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to San Francesco in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3286.

reciprocal_fplliklikccoidce.label: Hold a place for the absent · caring for graves · at the second attempt
reciprocal_fplliklikccoidce.meaning: To leave a practical place for someone's part in the care of a grave during uncertainty about their return. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to San Francesco in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3286.

reciprocal_cbkmabofnlkjnhki.label: Identify by its company · running a ferry · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_cbkmabofnlkjnhki.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the keeping of a ferry by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to San Leo in The Prince, Duke Valentino, 2707.

reciprocal_fameaafefcpoflci.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · reckoning a debt · after consent
reciprocal_fameaafefcpoflci.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the reckoning of a debt at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to San Leo in The Prince, Duke Valentino, 2707.

reciprocal_cfkpomicfdoofdio.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · storing water · under shared liability
reciprocal_cfkpomicfdoofdio.meaning: To give a judgment about the storage of water temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to San Michele in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 2889.

reciprocal_coeaefpanakcjnpg.label: duty that survives the key in laying out of a boundary · at the second attempt
reciprocal_coeaefpanakcjnpg.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to San Michele in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 2889.

reciprocal_mlcjkkagjjpobbdm.label: unmix two accounts of settling of a quarrel · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_mlcjkkagjjpobbdm.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to San Miniato in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3115.

reciprocal_jgjdhliablbdelhb.label: as far as the old promise ran in settling of a quarrel · with a reserve
reciprocal_jgjdhliablbdelhb.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to San Miniato in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3115.

reciprocal_emjifgekfdcphlpa.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · telling a voyage · under shared liability
reciprocal_emjifgekfdcphlpa.meaning: To give a judgment about the telling of a voyage temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to St in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VII, 709.5.

reciprocal_bhlleihhnhlaadhe.label: Time made free by a prior gift · telling a voyage · between generations
reciprocal_bhlleihhnhlaadhe.meaning: Said of a period of freedom in which an earlier provision of the telling of a voyage allows someone else to choose a course without immediate dependence. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to St in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VII, 709.5.

reciprocal_iboaklkbhichpoka.label: Locate between known limits · teaching a route · after a handover
reciprocal_iboaklkbhichpoka.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the teaching of a route by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to St in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VII, 691.4.

reciprocal_llnhloelmlmjbmnp.label: up to the point of parting in teaching of a route · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_llnhloelmlmjbmnp.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to St in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VII, 691.4.

reciprocal_beohbldgodfbjlbf.label: A surviving thread one can work from · carrying a burden · under divided authority
reciprocal_beohbldgodfbjlbf.meaning: What remains of the carrying of a burden that can still carry a practice or memory after the original whole is gone. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to sanballat in Nehemiah 6:5.

reciprocal_jbmckcpgllljmhng.label: Hold a place for the absent · carrying a burden · between strangers
reciprocal_jbmckcpgllljmhng.meaning: To leave a practical place for someone's part in the carrying of a burden during uncertainty about their return. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to sanballat in Nehemiah 6:5.

reciprocal_glodkjokkbhnlgec.label: recover the old edge of naming of a child · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_glodkjokkbhnlgec.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Sancho Panza in Two Treatises of Government, First Treatise, Chapter VIII, 362.5.

reciprocal_jfiecnfceogmcand.label: By retracing the last sure mark · naming a child · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_jfiecnfceogmcand.meaning: In a manner that retraces the naming of a child from the last point one can still positively identify. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Sancho Panza in Two Treatises of Government, First Treatise, Chapter VIII, 362.5.

reciprocal_fgpjkeigalpielbl.label: Bound a disagreement · placing a mooring · by private agreement
reciprocal_fgpjkeigalpielbl.meaning: To isolate the disputed part of the placing of a mooring so that the people involved can still work together on the rest. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Sandal in Henry VI, Part 3 00152a.

reciprocal_cmalbngjbnhkjdfc.label: Common ground that still bears work · landing a boat · by private agreement
reciprocal_cmalbngjbnhkjdfc.meaning: The portion of the landing of a boat that remains jointly workable during a dispute. Its scope is measured by what both parties still actually do. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Sandal in Henry VI, Part 3 00152a.

reciprocal_nnkpnpjocehaepjd.label: Identify by its company · storing water · before a witness
reciprocal_nnkpnpjocehaepjd.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the storage of water by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Sands in Henry VIII 00129a.

reciprocal_fhkapfmhocdjffbd.label: up to the point of parting in storage of water · under shared liability
reciprocal_fhkapfmhocdjffbd.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to Sands in Henry VIII 00129a.

reciprocal_iipghkmfglgjhmdl.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · passing messages · by inherited custom
reciprocal_iipghkmfglgjhmdl.meaning: To give a judgment about the passing of a message temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Sander in Henry VI, Part 2 00239a.

reciprocal_gajphfeenblicklm.label: Time made free by a prior gift · passing messages · between strangers
reciprocal_gajphfeenblicklm.meaning: Said of a period of freedom in which an earlier provision of the passing of a message allows someone else to choose a course without immediate dependence. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to Sander in Henry VI, Part 2 00239a.

reciprocal_bfiomfhdfnjogjpg.label: Locate between known limits · teaching a route · at one's own cost
reciprocal_bfiomfhdfnjogjpg.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the teaching of a route by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to St in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VII, 703.3.

reciprocal_cngjbjmnedeahikp.label: duty that survives the key in drawing of a chart · against the tally
reciprocal_cngjbjmnedeahikp.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to St in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VII, 703.3.

reciprocal_laepaogfkddmbenh.label: recover the old edge of drawing of a chart · with a reserve
reciprocal_laepaogfkddmbenh.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to St in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XVIII, 2021.1.

reciprocal_jdfkjkigaoihfabk.label: By retracing the last sure mark · drawing charts · after a handover
reciprocal_jdfkjkigaoihfabk.meaning: In a manner that retraces the drawing of a chart from the last point one can still positively identify. Applies during the first span of responsibility after someone else has handed the work over. Allusion to St in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XVIII, 2021.1.

reciprocal_lonjeghhgimkckdj.label: Locate between known limits · drawing charts · with a reserve
reciprocal_lonjeghhgimkckdj.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the drawing of a chart by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to St.-John in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XV, 1561.2.

reciprocal_nolfehmljhhcimeh.label: so far as the hand remembers in drawing of a chart · before a witness
reciprocal_nolfehmljhhcimeh.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to St.-John in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XV, 1561.2.

reciprocal_iehhhoaaniaeobek.label: restore the order of placing of a mooring · after consent
reciprocal_iehhhoaaniaeobek.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. reciprocal_ccfelkbmooihdaeo.label: up to the point of parting in placing of a mooring · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_ccfelkbmooihdaeo.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to Santa in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter V, 483.3.

reciprocal_kcebjdeeaghcgech.label: recover the old edge of placing of a mooring · at a distance
reciprocal_kcebjdeeaghcgech.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. reciprocal_ficpcbpcdgomiehf.label: By retracing the last sure mark · placing a mooring · under divided authority
reciprocal_ficpcbpcdgomiehf.meaning: In a manner that retraces the placing of a mooring from the last point one can still positively identify. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Santa-Clara in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VI, 647.1.

reciprocal_ebcpllknphplcplp.label: recover the old edge of landing of a boat · with a reserve
reciprocal_ebcpllknphplcplp.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Santa Barbara in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter III, 329.3.

reciprocal_hkpamipecojonhnn.label: so far as the hand remembers in placing of a mooring · in company with a novice
reciprocal_hkpamipecojonhnn.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to Santa Barbara in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter III, 329.3.

reciprocal_globfdapcgpnpecl.label: bracket the uncertainty in drawing of a chart · by private agreement
reciprocal_globfdapcgpnpecl.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Santa-Hellena in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VI, 563.2.

reciprocal_iiehcjognkjdjmal.label: Learned well enough to retrace · drawing charts · in company with a novice
reciprocal_iiehcjognkjdjmal.meaning: Said of a route, habit, or piece of knowledge of the drawing of a chart which can be retraced independently after learning it in someone else's company. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to Santa-Hellena in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter VI, 563.2.

reciprocal_iepakdimekgknffd.label: Locate between known limits · marking a boundary · on first use
reciprocal_iepakdimekgknffd.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the laying out of a boundary by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. reciprocal_lonkielaedbjlkpd.label: by the point of last agreement in weighing of a share · against the tally
reciprocal_lonkielaedbjlkpd.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to Santa-Martha in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter V, 479.5.

reciprocal_kphnndcichcgolkf.label: read the gap in repair of a roof · in company with a novice
reciprocal_kphnndcichcgolkf.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to Santrailles in Henry VI, Part 1 00125a.

reciprocal_glaclfbgibgnpime.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · keeping a promise · at one's own cost
reciprocal_glaclfbgibgnpime.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the keeping of a promise at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to Santrailles in Henry VI, Part 1 00125a.

reciprocal_ldeecmpaaihlpdji.label: bracket the uncertainty in collection of a toll · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_ldeecmpaaihlpdji.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Saint Jago on Cuba in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter III, 325.5.

reciprocal_ejehjmilceikgild.label: By retracing the last sure mark · collecting tolls · by private agreement
reciprocal_ejehjmilceikgild.meaning: In a manner that retraces the collection of a toll from the last point one can still positively identify. Applies within a particular agreement between participants, even where public custom differs. Allusion to Saint Jago on Cuba in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter III, 325.5.

reciprocal_cgjdkclgngijcpia.label: recover the old edge of opening of a road · between strangers
reciprocal_cgjdkclgngijcpia.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to Sansannah in Joshua 15:31.

reciprocal_hfpdbgaibjoplpom.label: By retracing the last sure mark · opening roads · between generations
reciprocal_hfpdbgaibjoplpom.meaning: In a manner that retraces the opening of a road from the last point one can still positively identify. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Sansannah in Joshua 15:31.

reciprocal_kkcdclicihifcflk.label: sand witness-piece
reciprocal_kkcdclicihifcflk.meaning: A small piece of sand kept to show what the material was like before it was worked or changed.

reciprocal_jpekcbdfdemmilag.label: sand trace
reciprocal_jpekcbdfdemmilag.meaning: A quantity of sand too small to recover as a useful portion, yet sufficient to change the material that holds it.

reciprocal_khdefpnnmbamccip.label: recovered sand
reciprocal_khdefpnnmbamccip.meaning: sand — Material of this kind recovered from an earlier use and accepted for another on the strength of what it can still do.

reciprocal_ngcjeonjejjminpi.label: shoal water-mark
reciprocal_ngcjeonjejjminpi.meaning: A sign left by shoal after the water has moved, used to read its former reach.

reciprocal_gnoojkpaemkkcmpk.label: shoal passage-window
reciprocal_gnoojkpaemkkcmpk.meaning: The interval in which shoal permits passage. A moment of quiet can be too short to count.

reciprocal_aminpcmlapmogcii.label: the waitable shoal
reciprocal_aminpcmlapmogcii.meaning: shoal — A local occurrence of this kind of water or current whose return matters enough, and is predictable enough, for people to time their work by it.

reciprocal_idhjihdmkaenaahf.label: Locate between known limits · teaching a route · by a trace
reciprocal_idhjihdmkaenaahf.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the teaching of a route by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. reciprocal_chakkkjghklobhhi.label: learned well enough to reverse in teaching of a route · with a reserve
reciprocal_chakkkjghklobhhi.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. reciprocal_mhpgnddpijngkdoj.label: Stay past the handover · taking testimony · on first use
reciprocal_mhpgnddpijngkdoj.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the taking of testimony after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. reciprocal_lfjkidnainhecmoj.label: learned well enough to reverse in telling of a voyage · in the wrong season
reciprocal_lfjkidnainhecmoj.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Psyche in A New Voyage Round the World, Bookseller’s catalogue, 2429.1.

reciprocal_icmehaionhbimfge.label: Leave someone the means to continue · settling quarrels · between generations
reciprocal_icmehaionhbimfge.meaning: To give someone the means to continue with the settling of a quarrel once immediate assistance ends. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Simon in Henry IV, Part 2 00518a.

reciprocal_gbepjkkjpjncjcbd.label: Time made free by a prior gift · settling quarrels · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_gbepjkkjpjncjcbd.meaning: Said of a period of freedom in which an earlier provision of the settling of a quarrel allows someone else to choose a course without immediate dependence. reciprocal_hoabngbnegknpnod.label: Leave someone the means to continue · sealing a letter · by inherited custom
reciprocal_hoabngbnegknpnod.meaning: To give someone the means to continue with the sealing of a letter once immediate assistance ends. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Sowter in Twelfth Night 00459a.

reciprocal_enjlddmojpanfdib.label: Time made free by a prior gift · distributing bread · by a trace
reciprocal_enjlddmojpanfdib.meaning: Said of a period of freedom in which an earlier provision of the distribution of bread allows someone else to choose a course without immediate dependence. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to Sowter in Twelfth Night 00459a.

reciprocal_lipnedcjhjkpcfkh.label: trace the hand behind setting of a price · before a witness
reciprocal_lipnedcjhjkpcfkh.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Saul in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, 1 Samuel 22:21.

reciprocal_dladigmifcbifdgm.label: A voice recognizable in the retelling · handing over a key · after consent
reciprocal_dladigmifcbifdgm.meaning: A remembered turn of phrase that discloses whose account of the handover of a key is being repeated even after the speaker's name has dropped out. reciprocal_ojgnnfijoomhchfb.label: emerods intimation
reciprocal_ojgnnfijoomhchfb.meaning: A first grasp of emerods sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_bmlaemfhnceckgje.label: emerods put to use
reciprocal_bmlaemfhnceckgje.meaning: An understanding of emerods that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_hlhpocidalfnfkne.label: emerods held on trial
reciprocal_hlhpocidalfnfkne.meaning: emerods — A thought or belief of this kind deliberately entertained until a particular question can decide whether to keep it. The speaker owns the test as well as the idea.

reciprocal_ddfchegpgolkkmjc.label: chosen botch
reciprocal_ddfchegpgolkkmjc.meaning: An instance of botch that someone deliberately undertakes and can answer for. The outward act may look the same when it happens by accident.

reciprocal_ahdgpmfpkioengmo.label: trained botch
reciprocal_ahdgpmfpkioengmo.meaning: An instance of botch performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_flbempiaenebheea.label: do botch on another's account
reciprocal_flbempiaenebheea.meaning: botch — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_apbakbekpmcjechh.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · setting prices · between generations
reciprocal_apbakbekpmcjechh.meaning: To give a judgment about the setting of a price temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Sabeans in Ezekiel 23:42.

reciprocal_aonbdfpcjfnjminl.label: duty that survives the key in selection of a witness · in the wrong season
reciprocal_aonbdfpcjfnjminl.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Sabeans in Ezekiel 23:42.

reciprocal_dkegfcnceodiokjo.label: have in trust
reciprocal_dkegfcnceodiokjo.meaning: have held under a duty to return it or account for it. Physical control and entitlement can belong to different people.

reciprocal_glidklajhcfgfmbd.label: have free to spend
reciprocal_glidklajhcfgfmbd.meaning: The share of have left at someone's disposal after the claims of others have been met.

reciprocal_nnhjmmcjfgfhgkoa.label: encumbered have
reciprocal_nnhjmmcjfgfhgkoa.meaning: have — A holding of this kind that comes with an existing claim on it. Someone may receive the whole thing and still have only part of it to dispose of.

reciprocal_ljdfkmkdhaaebelg.label: restore the order of keeping of a promise · against the tally
reciprocal_ljdfkmkdhaaebelg.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to charbon in All's Well That Ends Well, passage 0142.

reciprocal_kdmondkaongofdpb.label: so far as the hand remembers in keeping of a promise · with a reserve

reciprocal_ddjbmennjngaigod.label: Leave someone the means to continue · learning a dance · under divided authority

reciprocal_pllojemhldfakboj.label: Time made free by a prior gift · learning a dance · after a disputed account
reciprocal_pllojemhldfakboj.meaning: Said of a period of freedom in which an earlier provision of the learning of a dance allows someone else to choose a course without immediate dependence. reciprocal_klcehgiebjbncnef.label: count the absent into learning of a dance · in company with a novice
reciprocal_klcehgiebjbncnef.meaning: To recognize a missing participant by a part of the work which otherwise has no one to perform it. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to Shadwell in A New Voyage Round the World, Bookseller’s catalogue, 2419.1.

reciprocal_jgcijjgmiokbnemf.label: Counted without a hearing · learning a dance · in the wrong season
reciprocal_jgcijjgmiokbnemf.meaning: A member or instance of the learning of a dance counted in a total but never called individually. It has numerical presence without an individual hearing. reciprocal_bhafmmpcebhaapkg.label: restore the order of learning of a dance · after a handover
reciprocal_bhafmmpcebhaapkg.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. reciprocal_iecfiknpoaphijlc.label: up to the point of parting in learning of a dance · on independent confirmation

reciprocal_kandkjpijbkeaink.label: surface hand-wear
reciprocal_kandkjpijbkeaink.meaning: The polish or hollow left by repeated handling of surface, valued as evidence of who used it or how.

reciprocal_obpgdnmfillailjp.label: surface stand-in
reciprocal_obpgdnmfillailjp.meaning: Something fitted to do the work of surface during its absence. Success is judged by the job it does.

reciprocal_kdamfcadgoafnbcp.label: surface kept in service
reciprocal_kdamfcadgoafnbcp.meaning: surface — An object of this kind whose continued use depends on repairs made by its users after its original maker has ceased to maintain it.

reciprocal_ckiopilpaecibogm.label: beetle sign
reciprocal_ckiopilpaecibogm.meaning: The presence of beetle inferred from a fresh trace, while the creature itself remains out of sight.

reciprocal_egdelhjjikifeabo.label: beetle refuge

reciprocal_kebcjckbhkjmpnke.label: up to the point of parting in taking of soundings · under divided authority
reciprocal_kebcjckbhkjmpnke.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Seneh in 1 Samuel 14:4.

reciprocal_pfkiiamfpehijafp.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · handing over a key · after a disputed account
reciprocal_pfkiiamfpehijafp.meaning: To give a judgment about the handover of a key temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. reciprocal_kohljnjhefabmjdf.label: Common ground that still bears work · collecting tolls · after loss of the original
reciprocal_kohljnjhefabmjdf.meaning: The portion of the collection of a toll that remains jointly workable during a dispute. Its scope is measured by what both parties still actually do. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to sennacherib in 2 Chronicles 32:2.

reciprocal_lcjogcjindjcakkc.label: restore the order of opening of a road · after loss of the original
reciprocal_lcjogcjindjcakkc.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. reciprocal_nepombkmpjjcdinn.label: so far as the hand remembers in placing of a bridge · with a reserve
reciprocal_nepombkmpjjcdinn.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. reciprocal_jpajfbojdojlbaab.label: bracket the uncertainty in making of a mould · without a common tongue
reciprocal_jpajfbojdojlbaab.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Used when a shared word is unavailable and meaning must pass through gesture, example, or an object. Allusion to senir in Ezekiel 27:5.

reciprocal_kjinngjnekkjkhap.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · making a mould · under shared liability

reciprocal_omlpbmibmfhadaan.label: unmix two accounts of naming of a child · as a rehearsal

reciprocal_hojpnlnchpognpde.label: as far as the old promise ran in naming of a child · as a rehearsal

reciprocal_bhiefmnejclmddop.label: Trace through successive hands · choosing a guardian · under divided authority

reciprocal_ninbfeaaphjeifhk.label: by the point of last agreement in naming of a child · with a reserve

reciprocal_hagnhcnjogclfbbm.label: site-faithful slowworm

reciprocal_dihlmagmghnjkmgm.label: Stand by within reach · setting prices · after a disputed account

reciprocal_ehohbcgkbdindkmg.label: by the point of last agreement in dyeing of cloth · after consent
