Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to Socrates in Leviathan, Chapter 46, Hobbes_0161_1280.6.

reciprocal_kpfemhopbdffiglc.label: socket warning
reciprocal_kpfemhopbdffiglc.meaning: The first feeling in socket that makes a person alter their movement before pain forces them to stop.

reciprocal_pfdebhohajcpaadj.label: socket reach
reciprocal_pfdebhohajcpaadj.meaning: The extent of motion socket can sustain in ordinary use, measured by a task the person can actually repeat.

reciprocal_ecjkckdmmcfhegdo.label: the accustomed socket
reciprocal_ecjkckdmmcfhegdo.meaning: socket — The body part meant by this word regarded as the one a person habitually entrusts with a familiar movement. Habit, injury, or training can determine which it is.

reciprocal_anpmhefnfaakcdnn.label: Stay past the handover · changing the night watch · after a failed trial
reciprocal_anpmhefnfaakcdnn.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the relief of a night watch after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to Sawkins in A New Voyage Round the World, Introduction, 103.2.

reciprocal_jgbjgjclphcfgbfo.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · changing the night watch · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_jgbjgjclphcfgbfo.meaning: The share of a decision about the relief of a night watch that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Sawkins in A New Voyage Round the World, Introduction, 103.2.

reciprocal_badbjbemempbfpbc.label: distinguish an inherited fault in choice of a guardian · at a distance
reciprocal_badbjbemempbfpbc.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to socho in 1 Chronicles 4:18.

reciprocal_lgegojkpmjenihcn.label: exact at the fork of choice of a guardian · in company with a novice
reciprocal_lgegojkpmjenihcn.meaning: Said of knowledge that can distinguish two lines at the moment they parted, even if their subsequent history is obscure. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to socho in 1 Chronicles 4:18.

reciprocal_emcinbiglnaopeca.label: Trace through successive hands · marking seasons · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_emcinbiglnaopeca.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the marking of a season by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Sochoh in 1 Kings 4:10.

reciprocal_pejklcnpkfeeened.label: By retracing the last sure mark · sharing inherited tools · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_pejklcnpkfeeened.meaning: In a manner that retraces the dividing of inherited tools from the last point one can still positively identify. Used when waiting will soon make the action physically impossible. Allusion to Socoh in Joshua 15:48.

reciprocal_kfljmemnegcmpoim.label: read the gap in telling of a voyage · under divided authority
reciprocal_kfljmemnegcmpoim.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Sorek in Judges 16:4.

reciprocal_dmmdjnodbkefhhec.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · telling a voyage · against the tally
reciprocal_dmmdjnodbkefhhec.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the telling of a voyage at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to Sorek in Judges 16:4.

reciprocal_aeloagephmnpiico.label: distinguish an inherited fault in telling of a voyage · for another's benefit
reciprocal_aeloagephmnpiico.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Sodi in Numbers 13:10.

reciprocal_hjinldniobghccfe.label: Learned down one branch · telling a voyage · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_hjinldniobghccfe.meaning: Said of knowledge of the telling of a voyage that is exact on one line of descent or transmission while adjacent lines remain undocumented. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to Sodi in Numbers 13:10.

reciprocal_ekcfmddadmacbbkl.label: Trace through successive hands · taking testimony · pending a challenge
reciprocal_ekcfmddadmacbbkl.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the taking of testimony by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. Names a provisional arrangement that stands until someone brings a specific objection. Allusion to Sodom in Genesis 14:12.

reciprocal_oknhlnblmanchcac.label: so far as the hand remembers in weighing of a share · before a witness
reciprocal_oknhlnblmanchcac.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Sodoma in Romans 9:29.

reciprocal_bpkekenjpjlgmnkh.label: chosen sodomy
reciprocal_bpkekenjpjlgmnkh.meaning: An instance of sodomy that someone deliberately undertakes and can answer for. The outward act may look the same when it happens by accident.

reciprocal_dejhkcekocgnkeie.label: trained sodomy
reciprocal_dejhkcekocgnkeie.meaning: An instance of sodomy performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_jiigbdipiackfaoe.label: do sodomy on another's account
reciprocal_jiigbdipiackfaoe.meaning: sodomy — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_ajpfafahjjpflcfd.label: sodomite[source-label] by practice
reciprocal_ajpfafahjjpflcfd.meaning: Someone recognized as sodomite[source-label] by the work they repeatedly perform before anyone grants a title.

reciprocal_jibilddcfeihbgel.label: acting sodomite
reciprocal_jibilddcfeihbgel.meaning: Someone who carries the obligations of sodomite for an absence with a definite end.

reciprocal_fbanjiijakgfogdo.label: trusted working sodomite[source-label]
reciprocal_fbanjiijakgfogdo.meaning: sodomite[source-label] — Someone in this role to whom a community actually brings the difficult cases. Title or seniority alone does not confer the distinction.

reciprocal_dnppbbkeomegjmmo.label: distinguish an inherited fault in keeping of a child's confidence · after loss of the original
reciprocal_dnppbbkeomegjmmo.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to Sopater in Acts 20:4.

reciprocal_dcekhaeeopdicicc.label: A difficulty deliberately left to the learner · choosing a guardian · on first use
reciprocal_dcekhaeeopdicicc.meaning: The margin of difficulty in the choice of a guardian a helper leaves untouched so the learner can discover their own reach. Applies on a first attempt, while those involved still have no local precedent of their own. Allusion to Sopater in Acts 20:4.

reciprocal_lngpepbjllnijjap.label: trace the hand behind carrying of a burden · by inherited custom
reciprocal_lngpepbjllnijjap.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to sotai in Ezra 2:55.

reciprocal_jpmffcnecdphccoe.label: Learned well enough to retrace · carrying a burden · on first use
reciprocal_jpmffcnecdphccoe.meaning: Said of a route, habit, or piece of knowledge of the carrying of a burden which can be retraced independently after learning it in someone else's company. Applies on a first attempt, while those involved still have no local precedent of their own. Allusion to sotai in Ezra 2:55.

reciprocal_neikeodplfhekomc.label: returning appreciate
reciprocal_neikeodplfhekomc.meaning: A return of appreciate after a stretch in which the person believed the feeling had passed.

reciprocal_dmgafclelekpiecm.label: appreciate held in check
reciprocal_dmgafclelekpiecm.meaning: appreciate felt fully while its outward expression is withheld for another person's sake.

reciprocal_ihkepkgdohdplaki.label: appreciate borne for someone else
reciprocal_ihkepkgdohdplaki.meaning: appreciate — This feeling experienced on another person's behalf when the immediate gain, hurt, or danger belongs to that other person.

reciprocal_immllnpnohhnnkpa.label: Identify by its company · recording descent · in the wrong season
reciprocal_immllnpnohhnnkpa.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the record of a descent by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Soto in The Taming of the Shrew 00033a.

reciprocal_edjnijmbgkekapkk.label: as far as the old promise ran in record of a descent · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_edjnijmbgkekapkk.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Soto in The Taming of the Shrew 00033a.

reciprocal_aphjgeacghiopohi.label: first stir of swoon
reciprocal_aphjgeacghiopohi.meaning: The earliest observable part of swoon, identifiable before its full course can be known.

reciprocal_nbaoceafmmkmogpc.label: wake of swoon
reciprocal_nbaoceafmmkmogpc.meaning: The changes left behind by swoon after the event itself has come to an end.

reciprocal_amhhdkleilpjffji.label: witnessed swoon
reciprocal_amhhdkleilpjffji.meaning: swoon — An occurrence of this kind someone can date or place from their own presence. The word marks what that witness can vouch for.

reciprocal_fklbmijecdgeopdh.label: restore the order of sealing of a letter · after loss of the original
reciprocal_fklbmijecdgeopdh.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to Sofala in Paradise Lost, Book XI, 393–400.

reciprocal_lanpimaanachcnnh.label: up to the point of parting in sealing of a letter · against the tally
reciprocal_lanpimaanachcnnh.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to Sofala in Paradise Lost, Book XI, 393–400.

reciprocal_gmbinaomehpinoam.label: distinguish an inherited fault in carrying of a burden · after a failed trial
reciprocal_gmbinaomehpinoam.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to sophereth in Ezra 2:55.

reciprocal_mdnogdmhgdmjgjjp.label: learned well enough to reverse in carrying of a burden · between generations
reciprocal_mdnogdmhgdmjgjjp.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to sophereth in Ezra 2:55.

reciprocal_gofefeeelicmmpfn.label: restore the order of sealing of a letter · between strangers
reciprocal_gofefeeelicmmpfn.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to Sophi in Paradise Lost, Book X, 431–436.

reciprocal_lbgibkdplkinclpe.label: as far as the old promise ran in return of a borrowed thing · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_lbgibkdplkinclpe.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Sophi in Paradise Lost, Book X, 431–436.

reciprocal_hahedhnijdpgaokj.label: Stay past the handover · drawing charts · after a disputed account
reciprocal_hahedhnijdpgaokj.meaning: To take on continuing responsibility for the drawing of a chart after the temporary obligation of accompanying somebody has ended. Used in response to an actual difference between people's accounts of what happened. Allusion to Sophonisba in A New Voyage Round the World, Bookseller’s catalogue, 2479.1.

reciprocal_gmpjhbikbmmmfcae.label: learned well enough to reverse in telling of a voyage · after loss of the original
reciprocal_gmpjhbikbmmmfcae.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to Sophonisba in A New Voyage Round the World, Bookseller’s catalogue, 2479.1.

reciprocal_lfkmjloagbpadgno.label: Identify by its company · drying grain · at the second attempt

reciprocal_bmkcengngadafjdf.label: as far as the old promise ran in drying of a harvest · after loss of the original

Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to Sol in Troilus and Cressida 00204b.

reciprocal_cggcoieddceodghb.label: Identify by its company · drawing charts · at the point of commitment

reciprocal_lnhgichmjblhjgpg.label: so far as the hand remembers in drawing of a chart · between strangers
reciprocal_lnhgichmjblhjgpg.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. reciprocal_nddhmomkglindbmj.label: Identify by its company · sealing a letter · by a trace

reciprocal_opnlhfjchmfhnnho.label: up to the point of parting in return of a borrowed thing · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_opnlhfjchmfhnnho.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. reciprocal_fcjbmjgoamlfkggg.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · passing messages · without a common tongue
reciprocal_fcjbmjgoamlfkggg.meaning: To give a judgment about the passing of a message temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Used when a shared word is unavailable and meaning must pass through gesture, example, or an object. Allusion to Salisbury in Richard II 00269a.

reciprocal_knhikdfedfehfepg.label: so far as the hand remembers in passing of a message · at one's own cost
reciprocal_knhikdfedfehfepg.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to Salisbury in Richard II 00269a.

reciprocal_gdnedjmgoibedida.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · passing messages · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_gdnedjmgoibedida.meaning: To give a judgment about the passing of a message temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Used for the first act after which an ordinary reversal is no longer possible. Allusion to Salisbury in Richard III 01023a.

reciprocal_hbkbbjnbnmeojhef.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · passing messages · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_hbkbbjnbnmeojhef.meaning: The share of a decision about the passing of a message that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to Salisbury in Richard III 01023a.

reciprocal_igkbioemgaljocoo.label: Bound a disagreement · rehearsing a song · for another's benefit
reciprocal_igkbioemgaljocoo.meaning: To isolate the disputed part of the rehearsal of a song so that the people involved can still work together on the rest. reciprocal_cpacigfambmpickj.label: Common ground that still bears work · rehearsing a song · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_cpacigfambmpickj.meaning: The portion of the rehearsal of a song that remains jointly workable during a dispute. Its scope is measured by what both parties still actually do. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Solyman in The Merchant of Venice 00120a.

reciprocal_kckoalgillhhijon.label: Restore a neglected voice · caring for graves · under divided authority
reciprocal_kckoalgillhhijon.meaning: To bring a disregarded account of the care of a grave into hearing without taking credit for originating it. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Solinus in The Comedy of Errors 00003a.

reciprocal_flllgmlpgldiegkl.label: so far as the hand remembers in care of a grave · against the tally
reciprocal_flllgmlpgldiegkl.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to Solinus in The Comedy of Errors 00003a.

reciprocal_ngpchkkaafacphfe.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · tending a sickbed · between strangers
reciprocal_ngpchkkaafacphfe.meaning: To give a judgment about the tending of a sickbed temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to Solomon in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, 1 Kings 4:26.

reciprocal_idfpclohanmpcncn.label: voice of the first correction in care of a grave · without a common tongue
reciprocal_idfpclohanmpcncn.meaning: A small change in a repeated account which identifies the person who first corrected it. Used when a shared word is unavailable and meaning must pass through gesture, example, or an object. Allusion to Solomon in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, 1 Kings 4:26.

reciprocal_eanenabmpleiibdm.label: Leave someone the means to continue · caring for graves · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_eanenabmpleiibdm.meaning: To give someone the means to continue with the care of a grave once immediate assistance ends. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to Solon in Leviathan, Chapter 29, Hobbes_0161_770.2.

reciprocal_nifcoaoocbjodhch.label: Time made free by a prior gift · caring for graves · after a disputed account
reciprocal_nifcoaoocbjodhch.meaning: Said of a period of freedom in which an earlier provision of the care of a grave allows someone else to choose a course without immediate dependence. Used in response to an actual difference between people's accounts of what happened. Allusion to Solon in Leviathan, Chapter 29, Hobbes_0161_770.2.

reciprocal_fmakidhiknpbknch.label: bracket the uncertainty in drawing of a chart · by inherited custom
reciprocal_fmakidhiknpbknch.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Sologue in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter XII, 1247.1.

reciprocal_dhpbhjphifhfdejl.label: so far as the hand remembers in telling of a voyage · by a trace
reciprocal_dhpbhjphifhfdejl.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. reciprocal_aocomfogfjejghmi.label: bracket the uncertainty in handover of a key · under shared liability
reciprocal_aocomfogfjejghmi.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to Somme in Henry V 00276a.

reciprocal_jknmolabehemolam.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · running a ferry · between strangers
reciprocal_jknmolabehemolam.meaning: The share of a decision about the keeping of a ferry that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to Somme in Henry V 00276a.

reciprocal_nibhjoobeicfciof.label: restore the order of fitting of a hinge · against the tally

reciprocal_flbofmngddghmhle.label: as far as the old promise ran in fitting of a hinge · after a disputed account
reciprocal_flbofmngddghmhle.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. Used in response to an actual difference between people's accounts of what happened. Allusion to Somerville in Henry VI, Part 3 00756a.

reciprocal_ndgdnmfpeidbecad.label: recover the old edge of teaching of a route · after a failed trial
reciprocal_ndgdnmfpeidbecad.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to Somers in Leviathan, Chapter 22, Hobbes_0161_579.6.

reciprocal_applfmeedghfbomi.label: By retracing the last sure mark · drawing charts · by a trace
reciprocal_applfmeedghfbomi.meaning: In a manner that retraces the drawing of a chart from the last point one can still positively identify. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to Somers in Leviathan, Chapter 22, Hobbes_0161_579.6.

reciprocal_pfblapndkggkippo.label: unmix two accounts of telling of a voyage · after a failed trial
reciprocal_pfblapndkggkippo.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to Somerset in A New Voyage Round the World, Introduction, 101.3.

reciprocal_jieegcnnchpdohkp.label: so far as the hand remembers in telling of a voyage · with a reserve
reciprocal_jieegcnnchpdohkp.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Somerset in A New Voyage Round the World, Introduction, 101.3.

reciprocal_fmnpalbfjmnmjikk.label: first stir of crash
reciprocal_fmnpalbfjmnmjikk.meaning: The earliest observable part of crash, identifiable before its full course can be known.

reciprocal_pmdcgabpadebpdln.label: sound passage-window
reciprocal_pmdcgabpadebpdln.meaning: The interval in which sound permits passage. A moment of quiet can be too short to count.

reciprocal_hikogbfgbiiloiga.label: witnessed crash
reciprocal_hikogbfgbiiloiga.meaning: crash — An occurrence of this kind someone can date or place from their own presence. The word marks what that witness can vouch for.

reciprocal_lfegncnpcbblmkkb.label: can sound, in the expression for munching intimation
reciprocal_lfegncnpcbblmkkb.meaning: A first grasp of can sound, in the expression for munching sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_jfgbcinmhfpapiph.label: can sound, in the expression for munching put to use
reciprocal_jfgbcinmhfpapiph.meaning: An understanding of can sound, in the expression for munching that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_kimamhjigjlpnhlb.label: can sound, in the expression for munching held on trial
reciprocal_kimamhjigjlpnhlb.meaning: can sound, in the expression for munching — A thought or belief of this kind deliberately entertained until a particular question can decide whether to keep it. The speaker owns the test as well as the idea.

reciprocal_djooajeajdkfogeh.label: letter of the alphabet at second hand
reciprocal_djooajeajdkfogeh.meaning: The substance of letter of the alphabet passed on by a hearer who can vouch for hearing it but cannot vouch for the underlying claim.

reciprocal_aaebofpnbcjallbh.label: practical force of letter of the alphabet
reciprocal_aaebofpnbcjallbh.meaning: What a hearer reasonably takes letter of the alphabet to commit the speaker to doing.

reciprocal_mcednklpfhchmocg.label: answerable letter of the alphabet
reciprocal_mcednklpfhchmocg.meaning: letter of the alphabet — An utterance of this kind given in circumstances where its speaker can be called back to clarify it. It carries a different weight from a rumour with identical words.

reciprocal_lgejffgbmahieppp.label: opening of lower-octave
reciprocal_lgejffgbmahieppp.meaning: The earliest part of lower-octave in which an action becomes possible, even if a reckoning on paper puts its beginning earlier.

reciprocal_ncghkmmgkcihamdn.label: grace of lower-octave
reciprocal_ncghkmmgkcihamdn.meaning: The unofficial tail of lower-octave during which a person is still received as being in time.

reciprocal_kebdcjcdhlfgkfdi.label: lower-octave reckoned together
reciprocal_kebdcjcdhlfgkfdi.meaning: lower-octave — An interval of this kind reckoned from an event shared by the people involved, so that each can identify its beginning without consulting a clock.

reciprocal_mihfamgopolhclel.label: echo by local measure
reciprocal_mihfamgopolhclel.meaning: The quality called echo as judged against the things actually available for comparison here.

reciprocal_lbekkfannkieflkg.label: checked recognition of resound
reciprocal_lbekkfannkieflkg.meaning: Recognition of resound confirmed by a second, independently observable detail.

reciprocal_ifjcbgjhihefmagj.label: echo to the practical threshold
reciprocal_ifjcbgjhihefmagj.meaning: echo — Having the quality in question to the degree required for the immediate work. Further degrees may be perceptible yet irrelevant to the present choice.

reciprocal_mgcdeoihpdealfja.label: rhymer by practice
reciprocal_mgcdeoihpdealfja.meaning: Someone recognized as rhymer by the work they repeatedly perform before anyone grants a title.

reciprocal_ipfblokeccnmiehm.label: acting rhymer
reciprocal_ipfblokeccnmiehm.meaning: Someone who carries the obligations of rhymer for an absence with a definite end.

reciprocal_didnlmaahbnhjnha.label: trusted working rhymer
reciprocal_didnlmaahbnhjnha.meaning: rhymer — Someone in this role to whom a community actually brings the difficult cases. Title or seniority alone does not confer the distinction.

reciprocal_jiienndcihpdpdoa.label: first recognition of hum
reciprocal_jiienndcihpdpdoa.meaning: A fleeting perception of hum that prompts attention before the observer can check an identifying detail.

reciprocal_dknidjdenpjbpgih.label: checked recognition of hum
reciprocal_dknidjdenpjbpgih.meaning: Recognition of hum confirmed by a second, independently observable detail.

reciprocal_fneegjdmlconkkkj.label: perceive hum by a second sign
reciprocal_fneegjdmlconkkkj.meaning: hum — To make the relevant perception only when a second sign has settled what the first one suggested.

reciprocal_jgmmlhmabhjejloa.label: read the gap in laying down of an office · after loss of the original

reciprocal_lnecfjaakckpmcki.label: Mercy through restored ordinariness intimation

reciprocal_cgjppfindbojpbdb.label: Mercy through restored ordinariness put to use

reciprocal_bdfneodmhdbndjgg.label: restore the order of storage of water · in the owner's absence

reciprocal_cphfonkjfkbedkdp.label: sultan by practice

reciprocal_ndpidaggicjlllef.label: acting sultan
reciprocal_ndpidaggicjlllef.meaning: Someone who carries the obligations of sultan for an absence with a definite end.

reciprocal_hemnlcjhbebcpjbj.label: trusted working sultan
reciprocal_hemnlcjhbebcpjbj.meaning: sultan — Someone in this role to whom a community actually brings the difficult cases. Title or seniority alone does not confer the distinction.

reciprocal_jkahmkeeijaokfei.label: brimstone witness-piece

reciprocal_kbpmojhipaccaldp.label: brimstone trace
reciprocal_kbpmojhipaccaldp.meaning: A quantity of brimstone too small to recover as a useful portion, yet sufficient to change the material that holds it.

reciprocal_caeadcdefmjmlkpm.label: recovered brimstone
reciprocal_caeadcdefmjmlkpm.meaning: brimstone — Material of this kind recovered from an earlier use and accepted for another on the strength of what it can still do.

reciprocal_jpndphejemgkhglk.label: crowd acting together
reciprocal_jpndphejemgkhglk.meaning: crowd understood as acting with an agreed voice. Mere co-presence gives no one authority to speak for the group.

reciprocal_hlgnbbaoielkfdfj.label: edge of rabble
reciprocal_hlgnbbaoielkfdfj.meaning: Those whose connection with rabble matters in practice although their membership is disputed or left unrecorded.

reciprocal_inigkobhejngjmod.label: freely assembled crowd
reciprocal_inigkobhejngjmod.meaning: crowd — A group of this kind whose members have had a real opportunity to leave and have chosen to remain together for this purpose.

reciprocal_jhocpbpmhgmjljpd.label: first stir of hubbub
reciprocal_jhocpbpmhgmjljpd.meaning: The earliest observable part of hubbub, identifiable before its full course can be known.

reciprocal_aobmkfpidjnonngm.label: wake of hubbub
reciprocal_aobmkfpidjnonngm.meaning: The changes left behind by hubbub after the event itself has come to an end.

reciprocal_nhcidkinbjohlloa.label: witnessed hubbub
reciprocal_nhcidkinbjohlloa.meaning: hubbub — An occurrence of this kind someone can date or place from their own presence. The word marks what that witness can vouch for.

reciprocal_nlkcceonndihkjoe.label: clamour at second hand

reciprocal_jbgncbpagmgofbbn.label: practical force of clamour
reciprocal_jbgncbpagmgofbbn.meaning: What a hearer reasonably takes clamour to commit the speaker to doing.

reciprocal_bblhilpgihnbldgl.label: answerable clamour
reciprocal_bblhilpgihnbldgl.meaning: clamour — An utterance of this kind given in circumstances where its speaker can be called back to clarify it. It carries a different weight from a rumour with identical words.

reciprocal_pkhiekcjkijaaije.label: returning panic

reciprocal_icpmoekbmnmgkkdh.label: panic held in check
reciprocal_icpmoekbmnmgkkdh.meaning: panic felt fully while its outward expression is withheld for another person's sake.

reciprocal_eblgpfdojjnimpkc.label: panic borne for someone else

reciprocal_ppdilpjohcjnaoff.label: Stay past the handover · teaching a route · after a handover

reciprocal_kelfleoephllekop.label: By retracing the last sure mark · teaching a route · by private agreement
reciprocal_kelfleoephllekop.meaning: In a manner that retraces the teaching of a route from the last point one can still positively identify. reciprocal_geennofaldkoidff.label: chosen suck

reciprocal_kiiophdkchmmpnaf.label: trained suck

reciprocal_fojhbkdkicoiafah.label: so far as the hand remembers in taking of testimony · before a witness

reciprocal_immfplhpacfjiona.label: unmix two accounts of keeping of seed · on first use

reciprocal_ihdgepnolfclkaeg.label: unmix two accounts of return of a borrowed thing · at the point of commitment

reciprocal_ngndgjgpabnpeode.label: usable eleven dozen
reciprocal_ngndgjgpabnpeode.meaning: eleven dozen — An amount reckoned in this unit after what cannot actually be delivered has been taken out. The nominal amount may be greater.

reciprocal_ebfoajbogndflnci.label: Bound a disagreement · dividing a household · after a failed trial
reciprocal_ebfoajbogndflnci.meaning: To isolate the disputed part of the division of a household so that the people involved can still work together on the rest. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to Onesti in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3009.

reciprocal_foaeecenoeipnnoe.label: Common ground that still bears work · choosing witnesses · with a reserve
reciprocal_foaeecenoeipnnoe.meaning: The portion of the selection of a witness that remains jointly workable during a dispute. Its scope is measured by what both parties still actually do. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Onesti in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3009.

reciprocal_eiilnhjoopkabcdo.label: Leave someone the means to continue · tending the hearth · for another's benefit
reciprocal_eiilnhjoopkabcdo.meaning: To give someone the means to continue with the keeping of a hearth once immediate assistance ends. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to Onesiphorus in 2 Timothy 1:16.

reciprocal_nbbgddjglnkikhcf.label: Time made free by a prior gift · tending the hearth · out of public sight
reciprocal_nbbgddjglnkikhcf.meaning: Said of a period of freedom in which an earlier provision of the keeping of a hearth allows someone else to choose a course without immediate dependence. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to Onesiphorus in 2 Timothy 1:16.

reciprocal_jgbkmjmpdpogoomc.label: unmix two accounts of dividing of inherited tools · at one's own cost
reciprocal_jgbkmjmpdpogoomc.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to Onesimus in Philemon 1:10.

reciprocal_jonjiagebmidgljf.label: so far as the hand remembers in dividing of inherited tools · before a witness
reciprocal_jonjiagebmidgljf.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Requires a third person present who can later say what occurred. Allusion to Onesimus in Philemon 1:10.

reciprocal_ibdgemeapdkpkofb.label: onycha sign
reciprocal_ibdgemeapdkpkofb.meaning: The presence of onycha inferred from a fresh trace, while the creature itself remains out of sight.

reciprocal_ejgailbakgdhgdmd.label: onycha refuge
reciprocal_ejgailbakgdhgdmd.meaning: A place the observer leaves undisturbed because onycha repeatedly returns to it for cover. One sighting alone gives no such claim.

reciprocal_kphoaakfmdknamfc.label: site-faithful onycha
reciprocal_kphoaakfmdknamfc.meaning: onycha — An individual of this kind whose repeated returns to one place are reliable enough for someone to recognize or await it there. The word describes one animal's habits and carries no claim that it is tame.

reciprocal_iphkbnpdpcpbkhjk.label: onyx witness-piece
reciprocal_iphkbnpdpcpbkhjk.meaning: A small piece of onyx kept to show what the material was like before it was worked or changed.

reciprocal_alnjkjkiiljkekdg.label: onyx trace
reciprocal_alnjkjkiiljkekdg.meaning: A quantity of onyx too small to recover as a useful portion, yet sufficient to change the material that holds it.

reciprocal_jjhgamiodpdkhnfp.label: recovered onyx
reciprocal_jjhgamiodpdkhnfp.meaning: onyx — Material of this kind recovered from an earlier use and accepted for another on the strength of what it can still do.

reciprocal_ghohboglonmpkdah.label: onion season-sign

reciprocal_elfoddglbjepadng.label: onion reserve-stock

reciprocal_diadljfigpgplnbb.label: volunteer onion

reciprocal_bcjechggchhnekne.label: Locate between known limits · teaching a route · before a witness

reciprocal_cbcdnooakomgoodp.label: By what the hand can actually fit · teaching a route · on independent confirmation

reciprocal_bbbffghjikfdccbh.label: bracket the uncertainty in making of a mould · after a disputed account

reciprocal_nmpbkhlbmilonppo.label: By retracing the last sure mark · making a mould · at the second attempt

reciprocal_dbnhnihhakfdijca.label: fowler by practice

reciprocal_enhpfjnjamghdcbp.label: mummer by practice
reciprocal_enhpfjnjamghdcbp.meaning: Someone recognized as mummer by the work they repeatedly perform before anyone grants a title.

reciprocal_ipeplkbonjgngada.label: acting mummer
reciprocal_ipeplkbonjgngada.meaning: Someone who carries the obligations of mummer for an absence with a definite end.

reciprocal_gfccijefbdodedob.label: trusted working mummer
reciprocal_gfccijefbdodedob.meaning: mummer — Someone in this role to whom a community actually brings the difficult cases. Title or seniority alone does not confer the distinction.

reciprocal_npmbnjhjglonimap.label: physiognomy warning
reciprocal_npmbnjhjglonimap.meaning: The first feeling in physiognomy that makes a person alter their movement before pain forces them to stop.

reciprocal_aiaakdhfmpnjkgeb.label: physiognomy reach
reciprocal_aiaakdhfmpnjkgeb.meaning: The extent of motion physiognomy can sustain in ordinary use, measured by a task the person can actually repeat.

reciprocal_bghacogiappifjbb.label: the accustomed physiognomy
reciprocal_bghacogiappifjbb.meaning: physiognomy — The body part meant by this word regarded as the one a person habitually entrusts with a familiar movement. Habit, injury, or training can determine which it is.

reciprocal_cijkfkpapncejppl.label: presence approach
reciprocal_cijkfkpapncejppl.meaning: The approach from which a traveller first recognizes presence before reaching the place itself.

reciprocal_ijdefgggbdmfjfij.label: presence meeting-ground
reciprocal_ijdefgggbdmfjfij.meaning: The part of presence people use to meet or change hands, identified by what happens there.

reciprocal_lfnaaeagkjjdocec.label: presence known as shelter
reciprocal_lfnaaeagkjjdocec.meaning: presence — A place of this kind that someone knows how to reach for safety from experience, even if it has never been formally set aside as a refuge.

reciprocal_bpfdhofcakmoonln.label: read the gap in division of a household · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_bpfdhofcakmoonln.meaning: To tell what is missing from an arrangement by recognizing the two things that normally stand on either side. The missing thing leaves no mark of its own. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Uguccione in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3054.

reciprocal_ofijbpnbjbclkgfb.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · dividing a household · in the wrong season
reciprocal_ofijbpnbjbclkgfb.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the division of a household at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Used of an act undertaken outside its accustomed season, where the old timing gives little guidance. Allusion to Uguccione in The Prince, Life of Castruccio, 3054.

reciprocal_nfcgjemjhlhbmgnp.label: opening of ut
reciprocal_nfcgjemjhlhbmgnp.meaning: The earliest part of ut in which an action becomes possible, even if a reckoning on paper puts its beginning earlier.

reciprocal_iemgleeiieoglkkk.label: grace of ut
reciprocal_iemgleeiieoglkkk.meaning: The unofficial tail of ut during which a person is still received as being in time.

reciprocal_bjlklkblgknjkjmh.label: ut reckoned together
reciprocal_bjlklkblgknjkjmh.meaning: ut — An interval of this kind reckoned from an event shared by the people involved, so that each can identify its beginning without consulting a clock.

reciprocal_gppdkicgnaoohpgo.label: trace the hand behind care of a grave · with a reserve
reciprocal_gppdkicgnaoohpgo.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Uther in Paradise Lost, Book I, 577–581.

reciprocal_clnalplnbkihjjgh.label: Learned down one branch · caring for graves · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_clnalplnbkihjjgh.meaning: Said of knowledge of the care of a grave that is exact on one line of descent or transmission while adjacent lines remain undocumented. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to Uther in Paradise Lost, Book I, 577–581.

reciprocal_iaeakjgmofllnmib.label: distinguish an inherited fault in taking of testimony · between strangers
reciprocal_iaeakjgmofllnmib.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to Uz in Genesis 10:23.

reciprocal_oaelfapcigoemkfc.label: exact at the fork of selection of a witness · between generations
reciprocal_oaelfapcigoemkfc.meaning: Said of knowledge that can distinguish two lines at the moment they parted, even if their subsequent history is obscure. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Uz in Genesis 10:23.

reciprocal_lnhjacinbmfjnijn.label: Trace through successive hands · taking testimony · at the second attempt
reciprocal_lnhjacinbmfjnijn.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the taking of testimony by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Uzal in Genesis 10:27.

reciprocal_lbcfhijikefmnhee.label: Learned down one branch · choosing witnesses · out of public sight
reciprocal_lbcfhijikefmnhee.meaning: Said of knowledge of the selection of a witness that is exact on one line of descent or transmission while adjacent lines remain undocumented. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to Uzal in Genesis 10:27.

reciprocal_ppcmlmeefmglihbh.label: Underwrite another's risk · choosing witnesses · by inherited custom
reciprocal_ppcmlmeefmglihbh.meaning: To undertake a cost personally if the proposed arrangement for the selection of a witness fails, whether or not the result can be predicted. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to utile in Leviathan, Chapter 6, Hobbes_0161_153.5.

reciprocal_lgblfiekiahfpcbh.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · taking testimony · after a failed trial
reciprocal_lgblfiekiahfpcbh.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the taking of testimony at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to utile in Leviathan, Chapter 6, Hobbes_0161_153.5.

reciprocal_ipbakjcencopebgb.label: stay to see return of a borrowed thing take hold · under shared liability
reciprocal_ipbakjcencopebgb.meaning: To accompany a person far enough beyond a handover to see whether they can actually continue alone. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to Uthai in Ezra 8:14.

reciprocal_gmpkjcibobffkcge.label: Learned well enough to retrace · taking testimony · after loss of the original
reciprocal_gmpkjcibobffkcge.meaning: Said of a route, habit, or piece of knowledge of the taking of testimony which can be retraced independently after learning it in someone else's company. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to Uthai in Ezra 8:14.

reciprocal_npeglppepnalggil.label: owl sign
reciprocal_npeglppepnalggil.meaning: The presence of owl inferred from a fresh trace, while the creature itself remains out of sight.

reciprocal_jploheekjjoacmik.label: owl refuge
reciprocal_jploheekjjoacmik.meaning: A place the observer leaves undisturbed because owl repeatedly returns to it for cover. One sighting alone gives no such claim.

reciprocal_ooopinpkcclldiil.label: site-faithful owl
reciprocal_ooopinpkcclldiil.meaning: owl — An individual of this kind whose repeated returns to one place are reliable enough for someone to recognize or await it there. The word describes one animal's habits and carries no claim that it is tame.

reciprocal_kigmhjhpbooogdfo.label: Trace through successive hands · marking a boundary · by inherited custom
reciprocal_kigmhjhpbooogdfo.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the laying out of a boundary by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. Applies when a practice owes its force to transmission through generations. Allusion to Uz in Job 1:1.

reciprocal_kpjlonafkafiajmg.label: By retracing the last sure mark · marking a boundary · between strangers
reciprocal_kpjlonafkafiajmg.meaning: In a manner that retraces the laying out of a boundary from the last point one can still positively identify. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to Uz in Job 1:1.

reciprocal_alegfeobnalmbekc.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · keeping seed · in company with a novice
reciprocal_alegfeobnalmbekc.meaning: To give a judgment about the keeping of seed temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. Used where someone learning the practice has a real share of the work. Allusion to Uzza in 2 Kings 21:26.

reciprocal_epifonbfbcjdcolf.label: duty that survives the key in keeping of seed · by a trace
reciprocal_epifonbfbcjdcolf.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Requires a recoverable physical trace in place of anyone's unaided recollection. Allusion to Uzza in 2 Kings 21:26.

reciprocal_nhgafdgfiliofabd.label: unmix two accounts of weighing of a share · at the second attempt
reciprocal_nhgafdgfiliofabd.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Uzzah in 2 Samuel 6:8.

reciprocal_pdjghdjgfnankeld.label: up to the point of parting in keeping of a promise · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_pdjghdjgfnankeld.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Uzzah in 2 Samuel 6:8.

reciprocal_fajfceimcoojgpjd.label: distinguish an inherited fault in keeping of a child's confidence · between generations
reciprocal_fajfceimcoojgpjd.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to uzai in Nehemiah 3:25.

reciprocal_imgblpnkaeagkkei.label: exact at the fork of keeping of a child's confidence · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_imgblpnkaeagkkei.meaning: Said of knowledge that can distinguish two lines at the moment they parted, even if their subsequent history is obscure. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to uzai in Nehemiah 3:25.

reciprocal_ccmbgdadhgolkmig.label: Identify by its company · choosing a guardian · pending a challenge
reciprocal_ccmbgdadhgolkmig.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the choice of a guardian by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. reciprocal_lfbmjdcfaobppkih.label: up to the point of parting in care of a shared lamp · at one's own cost
reciprocal_lfbmjdcfaobppkih.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to Uzza in 1 Chronicles 13:11.

reciprocal_kpfbdodhghhgkpoj.label: Identify by its company · dividing a household · after a failed trial
reciprocal_kpfbdodhghhgkpoj.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the division of a household by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to uzzensherah in 1 Chronicles 7:24.

reciprocal_kmjifpgagmdhcina.label: as far as the old promise ran in division of a household · under divided authority
reciprocal_kmjifpgagmdhcina.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. reciprocal_ahlhoheelokjiblo.label: trace the hand behind keeping of a hearth · at a distance
reciprocal_ahlhoheelokjiblo.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to Uzzi in 1 Chronicles 7:7.

reciprocal_pecggnjjlkokiigp.label: Learned down one branch · repairing a roof · in the wrong season
reciprocal_pecggnjjlkokiigp.meaning: Said of knowledge of the repair of a roof that is exact on one line of descent or transmission while adjacent lines remain undocumented. reciprocal_cibbfidogjmaeief.label: restore the order of giving of a pledge · out of public sight
reciprocal_cibbfidogjmaeief.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. reciprocal_nfhbkmmepnecmlgc.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · dyeing cloth · against the tally
reciprocal_nfhbkmmepnecmlgc.meaning: In a manner that stops an account of the dyeing of cloth at the last link for which someone can answer, leaving its possible continuation open. reciprocal_phimllmkonmgdebp.label: Leave someone the means to continue · giving a pledge · after a failed trial
reciprocal_phimllmkonmgdebp.meaning: To give someone the means to continue with the giving of a pledge once immediate assistance ends. Requires an earlier attempt that failed in a way the participants can identify. Allusion to Uzziah in 2 Chronicles 26:22.

reciprocal_nigingbleckndjhb.label: voice of the first correction in collection of a toll · in the owner's absence
reciprocal_nigingbleckndjhb.meaning: A small change in a repeated account which identifies the person who first corrected it. Used during an absence, with a duty to account to the returning owner. Allusion to uzziah-ezra-list in KJV Bible v0.10-kjv.278, Ezra 10:21.

reciprocal_kdmigkkedjnholij.label: distinguish an inherited fault in care of a shared lamp · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_kdmigkkedjnholij.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to Uzziel in Numbers 3:30.

reciprocal_jigijfheadegbpmp.label: taught within one line of care of a shared lamp · on independent confirmation
reciprocal_jigijfheadegbpmp.meaning: Said of a skill transmitted within one line of teachers. Outsiders may perform the same work by a recognizably different sequence. Requires agreement between two sources whose knowledge did not come from each other. Allusion to Uzziel in Numbers 3:30.

reciprocal_pojbopopooigbahd.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · calling a council · between generations
reciprocal_pojbopopooigbahd.meaning: To give a judgment about the calling of a council temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. reciprocal_dlghhcemjopkbiel.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · collecting tolls · against the tally
reciprocal_dlghhcemjopkbiel.meaning: The share of a decision about the collection of a toll that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Used where a thing actually seen conflicts with what the count or written record predicts. Allusion to Uzziah in Ezra 10:21.

reciprocal_gjmhmlfoopaddlac.label: unmix two accounts of care of a shared lamp · after a failed trial
reciprocal_gjmhmlfoopaddlac.meaning: To disentangle two accounts whose chief sign is the same, using smaller details that travel with each. reciprocal_kdaokpmdjellmgfb.label: as far as the old promise ran in keeping of a ferry · at the point of commitment
reciprocal_kdaokpmdjellmgfb.meaning: In doing or recounting work, strictly within the extent of an earlier undertaking whose further extension remains an open choice. reciprocal_ahilckenenklmcde.label: Detect an omission by the count · dyeing cloth · after a failed trial
reciprocal_ahilckenenklmcde.meaning: To detect a gap in the dyeing of cloth because the count or pattern expects another occurrence before it can close. reciprocal_cobefiihfonhogdg.label: share left without a voice in keeping of a ferry · as a rehearsal
reciprocal_cobefiihfonhogdg.meaning: A part included in the total for which nobody present has authority to speak. Applies when an act may be tried and reversed before anything is committed. Allusion to uel in Ezra 10:34.

reciprocal_kiecgoaoejpgpljn.label: UPHARSIN intimation
reciprocal_kiecgoaoejpgpljn.meaning: A first grasp of UPHARSIN sufficient to direct a question while the grounds for an answer are still missing.

reciprocal_lbnnidjkhpcblkam.label: UPHARSIN put to use
reciprocal_lbnnidjkhpcblkam.meaning: An understanding of UPHARSIN that survives application to a fresh case without prompting.

reciprocal_cgenikkgfflneifa.label: UPHARSIN held on trial
reciprocal_cgenikkgfflneifa.meaning: UPHARSIN — A thought or belief of this kind deliberately entertained until a particular question can decide whether to keep it. The speaker owns the test as well as the idea.

reciprocal_fgoahopipgiohalh.label: restore the order of distribution of bread · at a distance
reciprocal_fgoahopipgiohalh.meaning: To put scattered parts back in sequence by recognizing which neighbours belong together. Recovering the individual names of the pieces may be impossible. Requires acting across enough distance that the immediate result cannot be observed. Allusion to uphaz in Daniel 10:5.

reciprocal_kpdbecihgpidkokg.label: up to the point of parting in measuring of a fever · at one's own cost
reciprocal_kpdbecihgpidkokg.meaning: In reporting another's progress, only as far as the moment the speaker ceased to accompany them. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to uphaz in Daniel 10:5.

reciprocal_cpckhmdjjeehmjpg.label: amend at second hand
reciprocal_cpckhmdjjeehmjpg.meaning: The substance of amend passed on by a hearer who can vouch for hearing it but cannot vouch for the underlying claim.

reciprocal_blmloidcnjdjkefp.label: practical force of fix
reciprocal_blmloidcnjdjkefp.meaning: What a hearer reasonably takes fix to commit the speaker to doing.

reciprocal_enmngknkmfggpfdd.label: answerable amend
reciprocal_enmngknkmfggpfdd.meaning: amend — An utterance of this kind given in circumstances where its speaker can be called back to clarify it. It carries a different weight from a rumour with identical words.

reciprocal_okmcedgolpnecokf.label: amends in trust
reciprocal_okmcedgolpnecokf.meaning: amends held under a duty to return it or account for it. Physical control and entitlement can belong to different people.

reciprocal_imbmcgbapelpjhhm.label: amends free to spend
reciprocal_imbmcgbapelpjhhm.meaning: The share of amends left at someone's disposal after the claims of others have been met.

reciprocal_pdenchgombkkpklc.label: encumbered amends
reciprocal_pdenchgombkkpklc.meaning: amends — A holding of this kind that comes with an existing claim on it. Someone may receive the whole thing and still have only part of it to dispose of.

reciprocal_jnpdchhclfcaaann.label: repairer by practice
reciprocal_jnpdchhclfcaaann.meaning: Someone recognized as repairer by the work they repeatedly perform before anyone grants a title.

reciprocal_cpnkhfmljdijafee.label: acting repairer
reciprocal_cpnkhfmljdijafee.meaning: Someone who carries the obligations of repairer for an absence with a definite end.

reciprocal_jcmbpabbicodlhik.label: trusted working repairer
reciprocal_jcmbpabbicodlhik.meaning: repairer — Someone in this role to whom a community actually brings the difficult cases. Title or seniority alone does not confer the distinction.

reciprocal_mlbiflkfdmlpaggk.label: Trace through successive hands · sharing inherited tools · under a closing opportunity
reciprocal_mlbiflkfdmlpaggk.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the dividing of inherited tools by a chain of independently named links. reciprocal_cdgkolplgomahnkc.label: Learned down one branch · sharing inherited tools · with a reserve
reciprocal_cdgkolplgomahnkc.meaning: Said of knowledge of the dividing of inherited tools that is exact on one line of descent or transmission while adjacent lines remain undocumented. Used where some means are deliberately kept back to meet a second need. Allusion to Ulam in 1 Chronicles 8:39.

reciprocal_mcdniankphhhklmo.label: bracket the uncertainty in keeping of a ferry · for another's benefit
reciprocal_mcdniankphhhklmo.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to ulai in Daniel 8:16.

reciprocal_hfjkaigigcdnodhc.label: By retracing the last sure mark · building bridges · between strangers
reciprocal_hfjkaigigcdnodhc.meaning: In a manner that retraces the placing of a bridge from the last point one can still positively identify. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to ulai in Daniel 8:16.

reciprocal_pohhaedmcjelohhf.label: distinguish an inherited fault in keeping of a ferry · on first use
reciprocal_pohhaedmcjelohhf.meaning: To recognize that several apparent failures descend from a single earlier fault and therefore call for one repair at their common source. Applies on a first attempt, while those involved still have no local precedent of their own. Allusion to ulla in 1 Chronicles 7:39.

reciprocal_mpdnomainpgbjhdd.label: taught within one line of taking of soundings · for another's benefit
reciprocal_mpdnomainpgbjhdd.meaning: Said of a skill transmitted within one line of teachers. Outsiders may perform the same work by a recognizably different sequence. Requires that the person doing the work and the person who will enjoy it are different. Allusion to ulla in 1 Chronicles 7:39.

reciprocal_ghoakghchjbgdego.label: chosen Take the opening for the whole
reciprocal_ghoakghchjbgdego.meaning: An instance of Take the opening for the whole that someone deliberately undertakes and can answer for. The outward act may look the same when it happens by accident.

reciprocal_mljmcndahjfkbgon.label: trained Take the opening for the whole
reciprocal_mljmcndahjfkbgon.meaning: An instance of Take the opening for the whole performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_iaibpmjhkfckkkde.label: do Take the opening for the whole on another's account
reciprocal_iaibpmjhkfckkkde.meaning: Take the opening for the whole — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_cdogmjcghmlanfjj.label: Identify by its company · passing messages · between generations
reciprocal_cdogmjcghmlanfjj.meaning: To identify an otherwise indistinguishable element in the passing of a message by checking the things that travel, occur, or are recorded alongside it. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Ulysses in Troilus and Cressida 01000a.

reciprocal_edlaofhlljiilgei.label: so far as the hand remembers in timing of a departure · after loss of the original
reciprocal_edlaofhlljiilgei.meaning: In describing an undertaking, up to the last movement a practitioner can still demonstrate from memory. The word makes no claim about the rest. Used where the earlier object, record, or means of comparison has actually been lost. Allusion to Ulysses in Troilus and Cressida 01000a.

reciprocal_lnggjdabcihahobf.label: bracket the uncertainty in placing of a mooring · at one's own cost
reciprocal_lnggjdabcihahobf.meaning: To establish two limits within which something unknown must fall, leaving open everything between them. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to Ulloa in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter IX, 923.2.

reciprocal_flpiikgeggdmhgec.label: By retracing the last sure mark · placing a mooring · out of public sight
reciprocal_flpiikgeggdmhgec.meaning: In a manner that retraces the placing of a mooring from the last point one can still positively identify. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to Ulloa in A New Voyage Round the World, Chapter IX, 923.2.

reciprocal_coghphocfmghjfmn.label: Leave someone the means to continue · sharing a catch · without a common tongue
reciprocal_coghphocfmghjfmn.meaning: To give someone the means to continue with the division of a catch once immediate assistance ends. Used when a shared word is unavailable and meaning must pass through gesture, example, or an object. Allusion to Umfrevile in Henry IV, Part 2 00023a.

reciprocal_kfnmfbobmiinbdfj.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · mending nets · after consent

reciprocal_hnpdlcdonfofheon.label: Leave someone the means to continue · choosing a guardian · after a disputed account

reciprocal_heejfigliibaghld.label: Time made free by a prior gift · measuring a fever · under divided authority
reciprocal_heejfigliibaghld.meaning: Said of a period of freedom in which an earlier provision of the measuring of a fever allows someone else to choose a course without immediate dependence. Applies where two people have authority over different parts and neither can settle the whole alone. Allusion to Humphrey in Henry VI, Part 2 00784a.

reciprocal_bfilhfjedjgjmdcb.label: Locate between known limits · marking a boundary · at one's own cost
reciprocal_bfilhfjedjgjmdcb.meaning: To locate an uncertain point in the laying out of a boundary by the known limits on either side, with its exact position still open. Used where one person volunteers to carry the cost and leaves the others free of it. Allusion to Ummah in Joshua 19:30.

reciprocal_fenhdilbkpomhhea.label: share left without a voice in laying out of a boundary · after consent
reciprocal_fenhdilbkpomhhea.meaning: A part included in the total for which nobody present has authority to speak. Requires an affirmative answer from the person most affected. Silence leaves this reading unavailable. Allusion to Ummah in Joshua 19:30.

reciprocal_jfeopepilceiebmk.label: Rule in an entrusted capacity · settling quarrels · by a trace
reciprocal_jfeopepilceiebmk.meaning: To give a judgment about the settling of a quarrel temporary public force by speaking in an entrusted capacity. The office can outlast that particular judgment. reciprocal_ejbhjanljicjklmf.label: Responsibility that passes with the office · settling quarrels · between strangers
reciprocal_ejbhjanljicjklmf.meaning: The share of a decision about the settling of a quarrel that attaches to whoever accepts the office, even after a change of personnel. Used when people must act together before they know each other's habits. Allusion to Hungary in Measure for Measure 00023a.

reciprocal_onhfbmeoeobkeijk.label: Distinguish by the smaller sign · choosing witnesses · by inherited custom

reciprocal_abhnibmfdamglebe.label: Shared in sign alone · choosing witnesses · at a distance

reciprocal_kkkhpajbanljpnjk.label: Learned down one branch · taking testimony · pending a challenge

reciprocal_hnghlhemppaecdbj.label: by the point of last agreement in keeping of seed · at the second attempt
reciprocal_hnghlhemppaecdbj.meaning: By returning together to the last step two people agree on before trying to settle where their accounts diverge. Applies only when the person who first failed gets to try again themselves. Allusion to Jiphtah in Joshua 15:43.

reciprocal_glhgihpmdplcomml.label: recover the old edge of laying out of a boundary · between generations
reciprocal_glhgihpmdplcomml.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Requires a younger participant to take over something an older participant has actually practised. Allusion to Jiphthahel in Joshua 19:14.

reciprocal_loklcgfpnaokpode.label: Counted without a hearing · marking a boundary · between generations

reciprocal_dblnnpfdmhhfbokp.label: Trace through successive hands · keeping seed · as the sole available course
reciprocal_dblnnpfdmhhfbokp.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the keeping of seed by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. Requires that another customary option has become materially unavailable. Allusion to Jimna in Numbers 26:44.

reciprocal_epmcbhnbidhbjlmh.label: duty that survives the key in keeping of seed · out of public sight
reciprocal_epmcbhnbidhbjlmh.meaning: A duty to answer for one's own decision after control has passed to another keeper. Applies where those doing the work are unsupervised and have to answer for their own conduct. Allusion to Jimna in Numbers 26:44.

reciprocal_hngllhcfkocpcpje.label: Trace through successive hands · telling a voyage · after consent
reciprocal_hngllhcfkocpcpje.meaning: To establish the origin of a particular practice in the telling of a voyage by a chain of independently named links. Looking alike only starts the inquiry. reciprocal_liadfpakgibpbdll.label: learned well enough to reverse in record of a descent · after consent
reciprocal_liadfpakgibpbdll.meaning: Said of a learned practice understood well enough to retrace in reverse when ordinary guidance fails. Mere repetition in the forward direction is insufficient. reciprocal_iknifolgcelkghpb.label: Identify by its company · carrying a burden · between strangers

reciprocal_fbikhejmakcgchpf.label: Only as far as someone can vouch for · carrying a burden · between strangers

reciprocal_abbdjakdklbdddoa.label: recover the old edge of opening of a road · with a right to withdraw
reciprocal_abbdjakdklbdddoa.meaning: To reconstruct a vanished limit from a practice that changes on crossing it, even where the material marker has gone. Used only where a participant can still walk away without forfeiture. Allusion to Jokdeam in Joshua 15:56.

reciprocal_jojambkcjajimccn.label: By retracing the last sure mark · making a mould · without a common tongue
reciprocal_jojambkcjajimccn.meaning: In a manner that retraces the making of a mould from the last point one can still positively identify. Used when a shared word is unavailable and meaning must pass through gesture, example, or an object. Allusion to Jokdeam in Joshua 15:56.

reciprocal_bkihlhcjoepeecmb.label: trace the hand behind taking of testimony · under shared liability
reciprocal_bkihlhcjoepeecmb.meaning: To work back through successive hands until one finds where a consequential change entered a practice or record. The first creator may remain unknown. Used only where each party bears some loss if the undertaking fails. Allusion to Joktan in 1 Chronicles 1:23.

reciprocal_obpkmpejbcagdehc.label: exact at the fork of taking of testimony · after a handover

reciprocal_koglbblhlodejkob.label: chosen tow
reciprocal_koglbblhlodejkob.meaning: An instance of tow that someone deliberately undertakes and can answer for. The outward act may look the same when it happens by accident.

reciprocal_eoedfpbgicdcpbnl.label: trained tow
reciprocal_eoedfpbgicdcpbnl.meaning: An instance of tow performed with the ease of a learned habit even while attention is occupied elsewhere.

reciprocal_dcdcaioppgchpncd.label: do tow on another's account
reciprocal_dcdcaioppgchpncd.meaning: tow — To perform the act in question as another person's delegate while retaining responsibility for one's own execution of it.

reciprocal_gokjneogiocncjbm.label: yeast witness-piece
reciprocal_gokjneogiocncjbm.meaning: A small piece of yeast kept to show what the material was like before it was worked or changed.

reciprocal_jmkckebjccdlefkk.label: yeast trace
reciprocal_jmkckebjccdlefkk.meaning: A quantity of yeast too small to recover as a useful portion, yet sufficient to change the material that holds it.

reciprocal_kgljggcheofkefid.label: recovered yeast
reciprocal_kgljggcheofkefid.meaning: yeast — Material of this kind recovered from an earlier use and accepted for another on the strength of what it can still do.

reciprocal_idiom_kjv_solomon.label: The knife before the measure
reciprocal_idiom_kjv_solomon.meaning: A proposed division that exposes which claimant cares whether the thing survives. Usually said when dividing a shared good would destroy what makes it worth having.

reciprocal_idiom_cordelia_lear_daughter.label: The scales with no song in them
reciprocal_idiom_cordelia_lear_daughter.meaning: A demand to measure a relationship by the grandeur of its public declaration. The phrase can excuse someone who refuses to enter the contest.

reciprocal_idiom_penelope_wife.label: The cloth's second night
reciprocal_idiom_penelope_wife.meaning: Room for one more decision, made by quietly reopening work everyone else thought complete. Used with admiration or exasperation, depending on who has to wait.
reciprocal_idiom_penelope_wife.origin: Literary allusion to Odyssey 2, the web of Laertes

reciprocal_idiom_gonzalo_naples_councill.label: The book beneath the bread
reciprocal_idiom_gonzalo_naples_councill.meaning: A gift that preserves who the recipient can become after today's hunger is gone. It names the part of relief that gives the future back.

reciprocal_idiom_kjv_nathan_prophet.label: The verdict that walks home
reciprocal_idiom_kjv_nathan_prophet.meaning: A judgment on a stranger that returns as an uncomfortable measure of the speaker's own behaviour. The turn of recognition is essential.

reciprocal_idiom_kjv_ruth.label: Two shadows past the gate
reciprocal_idiom_kjv_ruth.meaning: Companionship freely continued once duty and leave-taking have both run their course. Someone stays to make a life, even when invited to turn back.

reciprocal_idiom_prospero_milan_duke.label: The hand after the key
reciprocal_idiom_prospero_milan_duke.meaning: The first unforced gesture someone makes after power over them has been given up. The gesture may be an approach, a refusal, or walking away.

reciprocal_idiom_cassandra_priam_daughte.label: The storm before its cloud
reciprocal_idiom_cassandra_priam_daughte.meaning: A warning discounted because its earliest evidence is private to the observer. Saying it acknowledges a reason to investigate while time remains.
reciprocal_idiom_cassandra_priam_daughte.origin: Literary allusion to Troilus and Cressida 2.2 and 5.3

reciprocal_idiom_dogberry_messina_consta.label: The wrong cup with true water
reciprocal_idiom_dogberry_messina_consta.meaning: Sound evidence delivered in an embarrassing choice of words. Said to get a hearing back onto the observation without asking anyone to admire the wording.
reciprocal_idiom_dogberry_messina_consta.origin: Literary allusion to Much Ado About Nothing 4.2 and 5.1

reciprocal_hook_idiom.meaning: A task spoken of as already in hand because the first resistance has given way. The bite is certain; landing the catch still asks something of the hand. In teasing speech the phrase challenges premature confidence.
reciprocal_hook_idiom.label: A fish on the hook
